“He’s one of the best and most dangerous strikers in the league.”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta sweating on David Raya fitness for huge Man City clash having missed just three games since joining
Sports.content:
Next

MIKEL ARTETA may claim otherwise — but he will be desperately hoping David Raya is fit for the crunch clash with Manchester City.

The Arsenal goalkeeper is a doubt for Sunday’s clash at the Emirates after injuring his shoulder during last week’s 2-2 Prem draw at Newcastle.



Raya missed the 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday night, but his absence from a huge Prem test would almost be uncharted territory.

Since making his Arsenal debut in September 2023, Raya has missed just THREE top-flight matches.



Two of those came in the 2023-24 season, when he was ineligible to face parent club Brentford while on loan.

The other occasion was in May, when Kepa Arrizabalaga was given a rare start on the final day of the campaign as the title was already secured.

Kepa, 32, may now have to stand in again, although Arteta has not given up hope that Raya, who was at the training ground yesterday but not involved in the session, will be available.

Arteta said: “We still have a few hours before the game.

“So, we’re just trying to get everybody back.

“We will adapt to the qualities that we have with the other keepers. It is the same as we do with our full-backs, centre-backs or midfielders — that is not an issue.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“Our identity will remain the same. We will tweak a few things just to make sure the players are in their strengths. That’s it.”

Raya has kept 55 clean sheets in 118 Prem games for Arsenal, winning the league’s Golden Glove three times on the spin.

He was also named in this year’s FifPro World XI, picked by professional footballers across the globe.

The goalkeeper, 31, had more votes than any other player in the line-up — including Lamine Yamal and Lionel Messi.

That justifies Arteta’s desperation for the Spaniard to play tomorrow, but there is also Kepa’s last clash with City to throw into the mix.



The keeper had a nightmare when his then Chelsea side met City in the Carabao Cup final in March.

Kepa dropped a cross, allowing Nico O’Reilly to net the first of two goals in a 2-0 win.

But Arteta said: “The experience that Kepa has is already incredible.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Gunners winger Noni Madueke knows Raya’s major strength is his ability to play out from the back with his feet.

The winger added: “David Raya could play No 6, I swear. He is the first keeper that plays line-breaking passes.”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta ready to splash out in January transfer window with Arsenal boss to plead case with co-chair Josh Kroenke
Sports.content:
Next

MIKEL ARTETA says Arsenal are ready to splash the cash – if they can find a player that will “make a difference for the team”.

The Gunners are in the market for a new forward during the January transfer window after failing to sign one in the summer.



Arsenal were keen on Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior, but were unable to pull off a deal for either player.

The Premier League champions are now interested in Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi and RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa.



Arteta said: “We’ve always been very active in the transfer window, especially when we have certain issues.

“Have we managed to get a deal over the line? Sometimes not, so we will see if there is an opportunity there and something that we believe is going to make a difference for the team.”



The Arsenal boss will have the chance to push his case for a new attacker over the coming weeks. Gunners co-chair Josh Kroenke is due to be in London as the club have a string of big games.

They take on Manchester City this Sunday, before travelling to Tottenham the following week and Real Madrid three days later.

Arteta said: “We don’t wait to talk about these things only when it is face to face. That is why we have great phones now.

“We can have constant communication between us. But it is always great when he [Kroenke] is around.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“There is a different feeling. You can spend some time together and it’s great to understand how he is doing as well. He will be around.”

Arteta has told his players to forget about Man City’s potential punishment ahead of Sunday’s showdown – and make sure they retain their title on the pitch.

City, who were found guilty of breaking 100-plus Premier League finance rules, trail the Gunners by six points ahead of the clash at the Emirates.



Enzo Maresca’s side face a hefty points deduction or even expulsion if they fail in their appeal of the verdict.

But asked if he wants to win the title on the pitch, Arteta said: “That’s the only thing that we should put the energy and the focus on. There’s nothing else.”

City were found guilty in October but have been in limbo since as they wait to learn their fate.

The legal case has been a sideshow for months, however Arteta does not believe it will take anything away from the big game.

The Arsenal boss said: “I hope that it doesn’t, because this is a process that is still open and not resolved – we don’t know what’s going to happen.



“When you have two teams at the level they are right now on the pitch, it’s a big game and something to be enjoyed.”

Arteta is pleased with Arsenal’s start to the season, but is hungry for more and referenced the 100 points City achieved in the 2017/18 campaign as a target.

The Spaniard was an assistant of Pep Guardiola’s back then as they won the Prem by 19 points.

Arteta said: “We haven’t hit the level yet that they did, and I was there when we did 100 points. And that’s the level that is unprecedented, and every record I was beating with that.

“You want to be the best version that you can and that’s something that’s been done only once in the league and that’s what we want to do.”

Sports.title: Chelsea ratings: Makeshift back four come away without an ounce of credit as half-time sub Emegha the only bright spark
Sports.content:
Next

CHELSEA’S woes extended at Nottingham Forest with a rough 3-2 defeat that keeps them in eighth place.

The Blues now count a staggering five defeats in their last six matches across all competitions, while the loss at Forest marked their third in a row.



Nottingham opened the scoring after just five minutes when Igor Jesus met a stunning cross by Daniel Munoz and finished with an incredible volley.

The Tricky Trees got their second just six minutes into the second half when Morgan Gibbs-White converted from the penalty spot after Wesley Fofana gave the ball away and fouled Liam Delap.





Chelsea thought they got back in the game just three minutes later when second-half sub Emmanuel Emegha beat Matz Sels from close range but Gibbs-White completed his brace on 72 minutes and the Blues’ striker’s second late in the matchcouldn’t change things.

But who was the West Londoners’ biggest disappointment? SunSport’s Graham Hill rates each and every one of Xabi Alonso’s players:

EMI MARTINEZ – 6

He stood no chance for spectacular Igor Jesus’ opener before being sent the wrong way from the spot by Morgan Gibbs-White. He was booed by Forest fans but Emi Martinez is used to being the pantomime villain. He made a key second-half save from Murillo.

JOSH ACHEAMPONG – 4

It was a difficult night for Chelsea’s defence and Josh Acheampong was caught out for Forest’s third goal as Morgan Gibbs-White pounced. He was part of a Chelsea back four that never looked comfortable.



WESLEY FOFANA – 3

It was no laughing matter for Wesley Fofana. He was booed from the start by his own fans as they turned on him for his controversial interview comments. ‘You’re not wanted here’ was the chant. And, to rub it In, he brought down Liam Delap to hand Forest a second-half penalty and get a booking.

MOSES CAICEDO – 5

Recovered from a knock that forced him off against Leeds and replaced Levi Colwill in the centre of defence. He did his best to contribute out of position. He made a strong start but seemed uncertain after that as Chelsea dithered at the back.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

PEP CHAVARRIA – 5

Tested by Daniel Munoz on the flank and found himself in trouble during the build-up to Forest’s third goal. None of the Chelsea defenders came out of the game with any real credit.



JORDAN HENDERSON – 5

Back in the starting line-up to add some experience, but was wayward with his passing at times. Looked determined to change Chelsea’s fortunes, but he picked up a booking and did little to affect the game. Looked dejected as he was subbed near the end.

ROMEO LAVIA – 6

The midfielder had an injury scare before the break but recovered to make a key tackle on Liam Delap – however, he was lucky not to give away a penalty at the same time. Impoved as the game went on.

PEDRO NETO – 6

Recalled by Xabi Alonso and helped to get Chelsea back into the game. His shot bounced into Emmanuel Emegha’s path and he did the rest. He then set up a tense finish by supplying Emegha’s second goal late on. But he also found his way into referee Andy Madley’s bad books as he collected a yellow card for a bad challenge on James McAtee.

COLE PALMER – 5

He rarely showed any of the influence and class that had been his trademark. Chelsea desperately need the Cole Palmer of old to make a reappearance – and fast.

First-half free-kick routine ended with him blazing over, and that summed up Chelsea’s first half. He looked frustrated at times and a second-half sliced effort in front of goal did little to boost his morale.

DANNY WELBECK – 4

Recalled by Xabi Alonso, but had virtually no impact in a disappointing first half. He had precious little to work with, but it was no real surprise when he was replaced by Emmanuel Emegha.

His double was the only bright spark for Xabi Alonso. He was sent on for the second half and took just nine minutes to make an impact. Chelsea had looked toothless in front of goal but he twice brought them back into the game as the Dutch forward added to last week’s goal against Leeds.

Sports.title: Spygate clash descends into furious brawl as Southampton star goads Middlesbrough fans despite playing 67 times for them
Sports.content:
Next

FINN AZAZ sealed Southampton’s sweet Spygate revenge — and ran up to his former Middlesbrough fans to run their faces in it.

The Saints ace — signed from Boro last summer — cashed in on some awful defending to fire home with 10 minutes left after Ryan Manning had put them into a 59th-minute lead.



Having received dog’s abuse from the travelling fans all evening, he raced over to celebrate in front of them.

It sparked a mass melee between both sets of players.



Azaz said after the game: “They sang about my family, home and away last season so I was just waiting for my moment to get one back.”

Asked if he had any regrets, he added: “None whatsoever.”

This was the first meeting since last season’s play-off spying scandal saw Saints booted out of the Wembley final, Manning drilled home James Bree’s pass to spark stadium bedlam.

The bad blood dates back to May when Southampton’s intern analyst Will Salt was caught watching Boro’s training session ahead of their Championship semi-final play-off final with Boro.

EFL chiefs expelled Saints from the showpiece and docked them four points for this campaign — although boss Tonda Eckert escaped with a fine and suspended ban.

Saints’ graphic designer clearly used last night’s occasion to show off a sense of humour.

Plastered across the matchday programme cover were the words “ALL EYES ON US” alongside four pairs of eyes peering like secret agents.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Even the sponsors’ positioning on the front could not have been scripted better — with covert-sounding Midnite sitting right next to GPS-tracking giants Garmin.

Eckert passed up the chance to apologise to Boro fans in his programme notes — instead reflecting on the new three-year contract he signed with the club.

Hampshire Police were taking no chances with this fixture, issuing a 48-hour dispersal order across Southampton city centre from midday yesterday through to tomorrow lunchtime.

Extra patrols were also deployed outside St Mary’s to keep rival supporters apart.

The rain was streaming down, yet it did little to dampen an electric atmosphere cranked up further by a pre-match light and pyrotechnic show.



Home fans wasted no time goading their visitors, singing “We’re Southampton, we spy when we want” while several waved binoculars towards the away end.

Boro supporters hit back with chants of “You know what you are, you cheating b***ards, you know what you are.”

Saints fans responded with sarcastic cheers before launching into “You’re going to cry in a minute” and “We saw you cry on the telly.”

They then twisted the knife further with a deafening chorus of “Oh Oli McBurnie” — a brutal reminder of Boro’s Wembley agony.

Having taken Saints’ place under the arch, Boro lost 1-0 to Hull City via McBurnie’s 95th-minute winner.



Eckert had urged his players to embrace the hostile atmosphere — and both sides served up a breathless, end-to-end opening 45 minutes.

Saints should have been in front early on when a James Ward-Prowse corner was headed over unmarked by Lewis Dobbin.

Boro were denied when Will Lankshear timed his run to perfection after Dobbin lost possession, only for his one-on-one shot to be kept out by Daniel Peretz.



Azaz charged forward against his former club and thumped a 20-yarder that rattled back off the bar.

Keven Schlotterbeck then surged forward from deep but dragged his effort from the edge of the box wide.

Lankshear will have been disappointed after scuffing a shot straight at Peretz following a superb pass into the box from Sebastian Berhalter.

Boro keeper Radek Vitek then produced a wonderful fingertip stop to deflect a fierce Cyle Larin header over the bar.

After the break, Aidan Morris fired over after the ball fell into his path at the edge of the box.



Schlotterbeck made a wonderful last-ditch tackle to deny Lankshear as he raced through and was about to pull the trigger.

And Saints moved into the lead in the 59th minute — a goal that ultimately proved enough to settle a feisty contest.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Kuryu Matsuki crossed from the left and the ball fell to Bree, who played it into the path of Manning to fire home from 12 yards.

Boro pushed desperately for a leveller in the closing stages, yet Saints stood firm to claim all three points on a night that lived up to every bit of its billing.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest 3 Chelsea 2: Alonso clinging on to his job as baffling XI and Fofana horror show blow up in his face
Sports.content:
Next

CHELSEA have become the Premier League’s pushovers.

Bullied by Sunderland and Leeds, Xabi Alonso’s sorry side were beaten black and blue at Nottingham Forest – and a lot of the problems were of their manager’s own making.



Alonso picked a baffling team, stuck with an unpopular and out of form Wesley Fofana and watched his odd masterplan blow up in his face.

Chelsea are afraid of the big boys at the moment, having been steamrolled by Brian Brobbey and Dominic Calvert-Lewin in recent weeks.



So Oliver Glasner started Igor Jesus and Liam Delap together, and they caused havoc. Jesus bagged an early belter and Delap won a penalty from which Morgan Gibbs-White scored his first of two.

Emmanuel Emegha offered another silver lining for Chelsea, but while he may feel a bit chipper after scoring twice, there is nothing but doom and gloom around him.



In a bid to end their defensive dross of recent weeks, Alonso shuffled his back four around – but instead of dropping the defender who embarrassed himself in a YouTube interview this week, it was Levi Colwill watching from the bench.

Fofana, who laughed off one of his many poor performances in that interview, bizarrely started in the heart of the defence alongside midfielder Moises Caicedo and was booed by his own fans throughout.

It says a lot about their situation that those in the away end headed north expecting the worst. Their fears were confirmed almost from the off.

Even inside the first minute the Blues gave up possession in their own half and allowed their old teammate Delap to fire on Emiliano Martinez’s goal.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Four minutes later, his partner struck.

Alonso had warned his players on Friday there was no excuse not to get the basics right after the debacle against Leeds.

It would be fair to assume that marking the opponent’s striker in the box would fall into the category of basics, but they still failed at that and Jesus punished them with a beauty.

Daniel Munoz found space down the right and lifted a cross towards the Brazilian, who was being loosely attended to by Josh Acheampong.



Given the space, Jesus went for the theatrical, volleying from almost behind himself into the far corner – that it came off his shin only added to Chelsea’s embarrassment.

Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis, attending just his second game of the season, crossed himself in the stands. Whether he was praying to Christ or his striker, it worked.

The hosts were hardly full of endeavour after their goal, but they were also not up against much.

Chelsea have been prone to collapsing after setbacks, Alonso calling them fragile less than a week ago. While they did not immediately fall to pieces, there was little in terms of a response, the Blues hardly leaving their half.



No one in white looked interested in turning the tide. Morgan Rogers made a run or two, Cole Palmer played a couple of passes but beyond that there was nowhere near enough energy, intensity or even interest.

Having dropped him despite scoring against Leeds, Alonso sent on Emmanuel Emegha to try and fix things at the break.

Within minutes, Fofana had thrown them further into chaos – defending in the manner of a recovery lobotomy patient.

After misreading a long ball and allowing ex-Chelsea man Delap to race in behind, the Frenchman clattered into the back of his old teammate and handed the hosts a penalty.



At least he will be able to laugh about it sooner rather than later – this was not a performance Chelsea fans will forget in a hurry.

Gibbs-White stepped up and sent Martinez the wrong way, but it was Delap’s name The City Ground was singing in the moments after their second.

While Alonso was busy correcting his mistake of starting Fofana by sending on Colwill, his other substitute offered some hope at last.

After Rogers and Pedro Neto combined through the middle, the Portuguese winger’s shot was blocked but fell to the alert Emegha, who settled and finished low across Matz Sels for his second goal in as many appearances.



If some of the Dutch striker’s teammates had his energy and alertness, the Blues would be in a far better place.

Having one back added some fire to Chelsea for a spell.

But they could still not gain anything even resembling control and needed Martinez to parry from Murillo’s strike, coming after a free-kick won thanks to a desperate Jordan Henderson challenge.

Chelsea were back to losing their heads. Alonso was booked, Neto erupted after getting a booking of his own for a rough challenge out wide.



From that free-kick, more soft defending, Pep Chavarria given two chances to clear and not getting it further than the edge of the box, gave Forest their third and ended any hope of a comeback.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The ball fell to Xaver Schlager, whose fine clipped ball was prodded past Martinez by Gibbs-White, who had just nudged ahead of Acheampong. Chelsea headed back to London deeper in despair, leaving Forest back on the up.

Maybe Alonso could learn from Oliver Glasner who, just as he did before their win over Manchester City here, turned his fire on his players this week. Standards, it turns out, seem to matter.

Sports.title: Reckon Man City are struggling because of the looming guilty verdict? Think again – it’s far more straightforward
Sports.content:
Next

RECKON Manchester City are struggling because of the guilty verdict hanging over their head? Think again.

The answer is more straight-­forward than any looming sanctions.



Hook Erling Haaland up to a lie detector and ask if he believes Enzo Maresca can deliver a plan to beat Arsenal. The result would be very interesting.

Etihad chief Maresca is and always will be so lost in process, he cannot be a top manager.



He reminds me of a cousin who has all the degrees in the world but cannot get going in a job, so he goes back to uni.

One of the smartest people I know, but ask him to make a cup of tea and he will be stuck.



It is always just back to learning and never delivering for managers like Maresca, and it hurts his clubs.

Haaland is one of, if not THE best goalscorers in Europe.

Does he look at the moment like he is going to get as many as he usually does? No.

Rayan Cherki is one of my favourite players to watch in world football.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

When he plays, wherever he plays, he impacts the game for the good of his side.

But according to Maresca he’s not doing enough for the team. Really?

I’ll get ahead of you here, I might not be the most intelligent tactical brain out there.

But was a player like Eden Hazard told to work harder for the team, or was he told to just go out there and win it for us? Cherki and Haaland can do that if you allow them to.

Asking your match-winners to do more for the team might land better if you are winning — but they’re struggling and Maresca’s the problem.



The players are not talking about being distracted by the cloud over the club.

Cherki spoke this week and it was all about the need for more effort, endeavour and ruthlessness.

But they are not getting the right example from the top. It has always been the case with Maresca.

During his first season at Chelsea, they had the chance to go top in mid-December with a win at Everton.

All the Italian could say was this would be ahead of schedule, they weren’t ready. They drew on Merseyside and then the wheels came off.



Maresca may have been proved right then, but where was the belief?

He was too lost in the process and the journey to take the chance in front of him.

That is not a good outlook in a pressurised environment. Just finishing in the top four for Man City, under a new manager or not, is not good enough, he needs to have the minerals to win something big.



Maresca and Chelsea believed their own hype after winning the Conference League, where they did not need Cole Palmer until January — and a summer exhibition no one truly cares about.

He is selling everyone a dream that he is the smartest footballing brain in the room — but you prove that with proper silverware.

We are not hearing about the 100-plus charges as an excuse, but we are getting more than enough to make up for that from Maresca.

Now they’re struggling, we’re being reminded he is new, a lot of the players are new, things will take time.

There was no warning of that when they came flying out of the blocks at the start of the season, no erring on the cautious side then.



So why bring up the context now? Maresca is feeding City fans a plate of rubbish and telling them it’s steak.

It is hard to think of one of the City players he has improved, and it is not like he is working with a poor squad, is it?

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The midfield cost more than £320million on its own and that is not working.

Maresca had some early success, failed to build on it and now we’re at the end of November he is asking for patience — do me a favour.

Sports.title: Man Utd are NOT too good to go down and Poch can’t fix years of trouble overnight – I know how fast things can unravel
Sports.content:
Next

THERE is a phrase that should be banned from football: “They are too good to go down.”

It is usually trotted out when a club with a famous name, expensive players and a big wage bill finds itself in trouble.



It is intended to reassure but it can be the most dangerous form of complacency. I know, as last season I experienced relegation with West Ham.

History doesn’t earn points, stadiums don’t score goals and the size of your commercial operation is no use whatsoever when you are trying to defend a lead on a wet Tuesday night.



Tottenham provided an illustration last season when they came within 90 minutes of relegation. So Manchester United should be paying attention. They are in the drop zone with eight points from their 11 games.

Their 4–0 defeat at Liverpool was another miserable day, and the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino has hardly provided an instant transformation.



But the problem is bigger than one manager, formation or a dreadful afternoon at Anfield.

Think about the fans. For years they watched United dominate English football, win titles and set standards that everyone else aspired to match.

Old Trafford was feared going. The expectation was not simply to compete but to win. Now those same supporters are watching the kind of football that is difficult to recognise as United’s, with unacceptable results.

There’s also frustration about an apparent lack of a convincing direction, repeated disappointments and a sense the club has lost something of its identity.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

That is a painful transition for any fan, particularly one who remembers glory years. The atmosphere at a club can change quickly with bad results, and confidence drains away.

Players who looked comfortable begin to hesitate and passes become misplaced. Every mistake is magnified, every loss feels heavier and fans become increasingly anxious.

Momentum is precious in football and getting it back is extraordinarily difficult.



United seem to have spent years changing the people at the top of the football operation without confronting the question of why it keeps failing.

Managers come and go. The excuses and players change. Yet fans are left watching much the same depressing spectacle. There is a limit to how many times you can blame a manager.

They can pick a team, improve confidence and make tough calls but they cannot turn every poor signing into a good one, or suddenly give a squad the balance missing for years.

Not too good to go down

You can sack a manager in a day but not undo three years of poor recruitment so easily. Great United sides were feared. They believed they’d win — and opponents knew it.

Now that has been replaced by frustration, and expectation of victory by hope of avoiding another embarrassment. The club cannot keep asking supporters to pay for the privilege of watching memories.



I remember how quickly things can unravel. At West Ham, there is always a temptation to believe that the next result will change everything.

One win becomes two, the confidence returns and the season can be rescued. But when that momentum goes, it can be like trying to stop a runaway train.

Relegation rarely arrives as one catastrophic event. It is the accumulated cost of decisions that seemed very manageable at the time: The wrong players, the wrong balance, the wrong appointments and the failure to act decisively when needed.

That is why United should be worried. Not because relegation is certain but because no club should assume it is impossible.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The danger is not simply that United might go down. It is that they continue behaving like a club that believes it could never happen.



Too good to go down? Think again. The only thing that makes you too good to go down is being good enough on the pitch.

Sports.title: Southampton sink Middlesbrough in ill-tempered first meeting since 'Spygate'
Sports.content:
Southampton's unbeaten start to the season at St Mary's continued as they beat leaders Middlesbrough 2-0.

Six-and-a-half months on from 'Spygate' - which dominated the headlines during last season's play-offs - Saints emerged victorious, as they did in the semi-final second leg, in an ill-tempered affair that saw 10 yellow cards brandished to players and two to coaching staff.

Had it not been for the four-point penalty imposed on them as a result, Friday night's win would have sent them to the top of the Sky Bet Championship.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Southampton's Finn Azaz caused a stir with his celebrations after scoring his side's second goal

But goals from Ryan Manning and Finn Azaz - who goaded his former club's fans as he celebrated - put them within touching distance of the summit.

Boro's third defeat of the season opens the door to Stoke and Wolves to leapfrog them into top spot if they win on Saturday.

In the build-up, Tonda Eckert and Kim Hellberg insisted they had buried the hatchet - but neither fanbase had forgotten it. Both sets of players were booed when they came out to warm up, while chants referencing the saga echoed around St Mary's. The atmosphere was electric.

Meaningful chances came at a premium in the first half, but they were high quality when they did come.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ryan Manning opened the scoring for Southampton

The home fans fell silent for a split-second when Will Lankshear ghosted away from his man and moved one-on-one with Saints goalkeeper Daniel Peretz, who denied the Championship's top scorer.

And at the other end, Radek Vitek had to be at his best, first to tip Azaz's fierce strike onto the crossbar, then to push a Cyle Larin header over.

The first goal came just before the hour. Kuryu Matsuki's cross flew over everyone in the box, but James Bree was there to collect and fizz in a low ball that Manning ran onto and side-footed high into the net.

Image: Finn Azaz scored Southampton's second against his former club - then goaded the travelling fans

Twenty minutes later, Azaz capitalised on a defensive mistake to calmly slot home the second, before running straight towards the visiting supporters and making a sarcastic crying gesture, sparking a heated reaction.

This is not a rivalry that is going anywhere any time soon.

Azaz explains celebration - and has no regrets over it...

Southampton's Finn Azaz speaking to Sky Sports:

"They sang about my family home and away last season, so I was just waiting for my moment to get one back.

No regrets then? "None whatsoever."

Sports.title: Forest beat Chelsea to heap pressure on Alonso as Fofana is booed
Sports.content:
Morgan Gibbs-White scored two in Nottingham Forest’s 3-2 win over Chelsea at the City Ground as the crisis deepened for Xabi Alonso.

Igor Jesus volleyed Forest in front inside five minutes of what was a dismal first half for Chelsea and they never recovered parity. Wesley Fofana - booed by his own supporters throughout - conceded a penalty early in the second half that Gibbs-White converted.

Emmanuel Emegha did come off the bench to pull one back soon afterwards but another goal from the Forest captain better reflected the superiority of Oliver Glasner's side even if Emagha's second in the 89th minute made for a surprisingly nervy finale.

Forest began the evening beside the Trent with only goal difference keeping them out of the relegation zone, but victory lifts them clear of the bottom six. The spotlight now falls on Chelsea, who missed the chance to climb back into the top five.

It is four Premier League defeats in their last five games under Alonso who appears to be scrambling for solutions on the evidence of this team selection. It is not only Fofana under scrutiny at Chelsea. A club in disarray? Alonso needs to get a grip of it and fast.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Igor Jesus volleys home a stunning opener to give Nottingham Forest the lead against Chelsea

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Morgan Gibbs-White slots home a penalty to give Nottingham Forest a 2-0 lead over Chelsea

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Morgan Gibbs-White nets again to put Nottingham Forest within sight of victory over Chelsea

How Forest were too good for Chelsea

Liam Delap had been the two-goal hero in the 3-1 win over Manchester City last time out at home and would have been desperate to score against another of his former clubs but it was Igor Jesus' stunning strike that silenced the Chelsea supporters early on.

"It is the first opportunity for them to play together, they have different strengths," Glasner had told Sky Sports beforehand. Igor Jesus' strengths include volleys beyond Emiliano Martinez, it turns out. It was his first goal at the City Ground since April.

Alonso had responded to the alarming defeat to Leeds by dropping Levi Colwill and playing Moises Caicedo in defence. The Chelsea boss changed to a back four as well in a bid to find some form after losing three of their previous four Premier League games.

"Today we need strong characters, big personalities," said Alonso beforehand. "Players that know what it takes to compete in the Premier League." That explained the decision to bring in Danny Welbeck up front, with Jordan Henderson holding midfield together.

But Welbeck was a passenger in the first half, having only seven touches of the ball - half as many as anyone else - while Henderson found himself overrun. Forest were at the back line time and again. Chelsea were fortunate to be only one down at the break.

Fofana had not endeared himself to supporters by giving an unauthorised interview in which he not only talked of being close to quitting football but appeared to joke about missing a penalty in the Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool. This performance was worse.

He was culpable for Forest's second goal, bested by Delap before hastily fouling him inside the penalty box in a rash attempt to recover. Gibbs-White slotted home from the spot and Fofana was substituted to the sound obscene chants from the Chelsea fans.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Emmanuel Emegha gets Chelsea back in it at Nottingham Forest

Alonso's side did pull one back through the young substitute Emegha, when Pedro Neto's shot was deflected kindly into his path. But Xaver Schlager's sumptuous ball clipped in behind the Chelsea defence allowed Gibbs-White to hook home his second.

Emagha nodded in another late on to make the decision to omit him after scoring the first goal against Leeds look even more of an error, but it was not enough to earn an undeserved point. Forest held on and are on the up again. Chelsea have problems.

Sports.title: Scratchy Ireland still prove too strong for Australia at Twickenham
Sports.content:
Nick Timoney was among the try scorers at Twickenham as Ireland banked a sixth Nations Championship victory from seven Tests

Ireland rounded off their Nations Championship campaign with a sixth victory from seven Tests, defeating Australia 38-14 at Allianz Stadium Twickenham.

Such a record can only be matched by England and France, should either or both defeat New Zealand and South Africa this weekend, respectively - Ireland finished behind England on points difference and France due to bonus points in the northern hemisphere standings.

On Friday, centre Robbie Henshaw, back-row Nick Timoney, wing Rob Baloucoune and replacement No 8 James McNabney (two) scored tries, with Sam Prendergast adding all five conversions and a penalty.

Ireland 38-14 Australia - Score summary Ireland - Tries: Henshaw (26), Timoney (37), Baloucoune (43), McNabney (73, 80+1). Cons: Prendergast (26,39,44,74,81). Pens: Prendergast (40+3). Australia - Tries: Williams (22), Thomas (56). Cons: Gordon (23, 57).

Andy Farrell's Ireland were far from their best on the night, but the Wallabies could only score two tries through lock Jeremy Williams and scrum-half Kalani Thomas, wasting a further nine 22 entries up against a teak tough Irish defence.

The victory also saw Ireland claim the Raeburn Shield from Australia - rugby's lineal world title which dates back to the first Test match ever played in 1871. Australia had won it by beating Wales, who claimed it from New Zealand in Cardiff a fortnight ago.

Prendergast: We were scrappy at times

Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast told ITV:

"I think we stuck with it pretty well. There were some scrappy parts we'd like to be a bit better at.

"I thought we were quite clinical in their 22 but scrappy at times. I think he [Andy Farrell] will have a similar gist; there's definitely some good parts. There's loads we can be better at and want to be better at today.

"Coming into the autumn, we knew we had a couple of big games to start. We went four from four and that's what we were targeting. There was no lack of motivation.

"I'm really enjoying [playing for Ireland]. We're building towards the Rugby World Cup. Loads of highs and lows at the moment so, I won't get too high."

What's next?

Ireland are next in action during the 2027 Six Nations in February, when they start with a huge Test against England in Dublin at the Aviva Stadium on Friday February 5 (8.10pm kick-off).

Ireland's Nations Championship fixtures and results Australia 31-33 Ireland July 4 Japan 20-36 Ireland July 11 New Zealand 40-21 Ireland July 18 Ireland 42-12 Argentina November 6 Ireland 43-15 Fiji November 14 Ireland 20-17 South Africa November 21 Ireland 38-14 Australia November 27

Australia now enter their offseason and are not in action again until April 25 2027 when they face New Zealand at Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane. Australia are hosting the Rugby World Cup in 2027 between October 1-November 13.

Sports.title: 'A bit strange' - Leclerc seeking outlier to catch Mercedes in Qatar
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc believes an “outlier” has given Mercedes a “massive” advantage at the Qatar Grand Prix, after Kimi Antonelli and George Russell dominated Friday’s practice sessions.

Mercedes were nearly half a second quicker than the rest of the field at the Lusail International Circuit as Antonelli topped both sessions from Russell.

Their four-tenths advantage over closest challenger Lando Norris in second practice could have been even greater, with neither Antonelli nor Russell completing a full low-fuel lap on the soft tyres. It was an ominous sign for the rest of the field ahead of Saturday's qualifying, which gets under way at 6pm, with coverage live on Sky Sports F1 from 5.15pm.

Mercedes' dominance was similar to their pace advantage earlier in the season but the second half of 2026 has largely been very close between F1's top four teams - Mercedes, Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren.

Ferrari were over one second behind Antonelli on a dismal Friday as Leclerc spun in second practice and Lewis Hamilton suffered an engine problem which brought his Ferrari to a halt.

"Honestly it's been a very difficult day. It's not that we didn't try on the softs, we couldn't improve our lap time on the mediums," said Leclerc.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari's Charles Leclerc suffers a big spin during the second practice session at the Qatar Grand Prix

"I lost the car and had some damage so we had to repair the car but that was the first lap of FP2 and I couldn't improve and even on the new soft later on I couldn't improve.

"A very, very difficult day. The feeling is just very difficult to get right. Not even on high fuel we were strong, so for now, it looks like a very difficult weekend but we are working hard to try and understand something.

"For some reason, Mercedes are so much faster than everybody expected, so the gaps are just a little bit strange, so there's something that's an outlier and we just need to find that."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc speaks on what's happened in the aftermath of his crash with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton at the Las Vegas Grand Prix

Ferrari were not expected to be strong at the Lusail International Circuit due to the long flat out zones and high-speed corners but Leclerc suggested his team, along with McLaren and Red Bull were missing a trick that will give them more pace.

"I don't think we know yet what's the outlier. I think other teams probably didn't find that because Mercedes still have a massive advantage," he said.

"We are going to work towards that and analyse the data to understand what's going on."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton almost makes contact with Red Bull's Max Verstappen during the second practice session at the Qatar Grand Prix

Norris: Mercedes not even worth thinking about

McLaren were predicted to be very competitive in Qatar due to their strength in the high-speed corners but Norris and Piastri were never close to matching the pace of Mercedes.

On Saturday, McLaren are expected to put the new floor they ran in Las Vegas on the car but Norris does not think it will make a big enouch difference to catch Mercedes who are in "a different category".

"I don't know how much that will help around here compared to Vegas," said last year's world champion.

"But obviously tonight [Friday] we will see how much we can gain from that. It's not going to be the gap we need.

Sports.title: Taylor says he is quitting darts for good after comeback
Sports.content:
Phil Taylor says he is quitting competitive darts for good and has no plans to come out of retirement again.

The 16-time world champion was lured back to the oche for this year's MODUS Super Series International Pairs Tournament in Portsmouth alongside his long-time friend Adrian Lewis.

The English duo lost all five of their matches on Thursday but rebounded on Friday, winning three and losing two matches, to finish second-bottom in the Group C standings.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Taylor and Lewis lost all five of their group matches on Friday

Taylor, 67, retired from the competitive circuit in 2018, five years after winning his final world crown, and when asked if he would make another comeback, the 14-time PDC World Championship winner told Pluto TV: "[This is] proper retirement."

A heartwarming moment unfolded after Taylor and Lewis were beaten 4-3 in their final group match against Scotland, as each of the other nations arrived to give Taylor a guard of honour, as he walked away from the oche.

"I mean I'm 67, I get my pension next February," Taylor said, when asked if this would be his last competitive appearance. "I'm a pensioner now, officially!"

"I'll still do personal appearances, more having a chat with people, talking about my career, that kind of thing."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Taylor said people like to call him the GOAT, but added: "I'm the old goat now!" / Credit: @MSSdarts

Taylor and Lewis, who teamed up to win four World Cup of Darts titles between 2012 and 2016, finished Thursday at the bottom of Group C. Friday started poorly for the Englishmen, losing to Denmark's Ivan Springborg-Poulsen and Andreas Toft Jørgensen 4-2.

Speaking on his retirement U-turn this week, Taylor said: "I was dreading it to be honest with you because I know I wasn't playing like I can do, but now I've been here and it's all over, I've loved it."

The pair hit back on Friday with a 4-3 win against Germany, then beat Switzerland and Sweden, both 4-2.

The Englishmen would tie Scotland at three legs apiece in his final competitive match, before Taylor missed a checkout for 48 for victory, in what would have been a fairy-tale finish.

"Looking back now, it's like it never happened," Taylor said, reflecting on his glittering career.

"I've said to other people who have been on stage and retired: 'How do you feel now?'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Taylor explains why he has decided to come out of retirement to join Lewis for the Modus Super Series

"'It's like you've never been there'. It's ever so weird. And you come up on YouTube and you just go: "No, I know. I know I was there, but I can't remember it."

"It's very, very strange because, mentally-wise, you move on. That was your former life and now my life is different."

Instead of flying around the world competing, Taylor says retirement has allowed him to spend more time with his grandchildren.

"I've got 11 grandchildren," Taylor said. "So I spend a lot of time with them now.

"[I do] things I've never done before. Go to bed when I want; I go to bed early. For me, 9pm would be like, I'd be asleep two hours before 9pm, and it's great.

"I love getting up early as well. We can do all the chores. We can go shopping and get everything done, and it isn't even 11am. It's great!

"People say I'm the GOAT [Greatest of All Time]-I'm an old goat now!"

Sports.title: Don't sleep on the NFL 'uncs' - can they finally win a Super Bowl?
Sports.content:
Kyle Shanahan's San Francisco 49ers are the best team in football. Is this finally the season they win a Lombardi Trophy? Their next test is against the champions.

Most offenses in the NFL look and function the way they do because of the Shanahan. His fingerprints, and still that of his father, have long been ingrained in trends, wrinkles and schematic interpretations dominant across the league as fans know it.

He tops the tree that has shaped modern football. And he is beating them all at his own game. He has done so for some time, minus the shiny reward at the end.

In that sense he sits alongside Josh Allen, even Joe Burrow and Lamar Jackson, in likely believing he would have a ring were it not for Patrick Mahomes, Andy Reid and the Kansas City Chiefs' Super Bowl dynasty, which twice have taken down Shanahan's 49ers in the season finale.

But the Niners look good for another Championship run. And few deserve it quite like Shanahan.

Week 12 results so far Green Bay Packers 13-26 Los Angeles Rams (Thanksgiving Eve)

Chicago Bears 39-35 Detroit Lions (Thanksgiving)

Philadelphia Eagles 39-38 Dallas Cowboys (Thanksgiving)

Kansas City Chiefs 10-13 Buffalo Bills (Thanksgiving)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the San Francisco 49ers against the Minnesota Vikings from Week 11 of the NFL season

It would be a staggering case study were he not to win a Super Bowl at some stage in San Francisco, bearing in mind not only the number of close calls for a team he has led to four NFC Championship Games - two of which he won - in nine seasons, but also the genius football brain that has governed sidelines and film rooms across the nation.

His 49ers sit 9-1 in pole position for the No 1 seed in the NFC heading into Sunday night's matchup with the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. They do so having just dismantled the Minnesota Vikings and their league-leading scoring defense 35-10 in Mexico City; only twice this season had teams put up more than 20 points against Brian Flores' defense. Shanahan torched them with ease.

It was a message to teams across the league, many of which had been foiled by Flores, his blitz bombardments and camouflaged coverages. It, too, was further evidence of an expertly drilled operation that stormed past the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia in kickoff week before making Mexico home in famously tricky high-altitude conditions. Should they win a Super Bowl, the NFL's 'are they really world champions?' debate loses some substance; the Niners have gone global.

Shanahan's offense entered Week 12 ranked second in yards per game, sixth in passing, fourth in rushing and No 1 in scoring while topping all teams in EPA/play and success rate as the most prolific attack in football.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tom Brady expressed his disappointment in how Aaron Rodgers handled his benching and exit from the Pittsburgh Steelers

At the heart of it is Brock Purdy, who Shanahan both identified and cultivated from Mr Irrelevant to undeniable MVP candidate. Non-Purdy believers had deemed him the product of the Shanahan system; to admit that could be partly true would be a deserved nod to what San Francisco's head coach does as one of football's masterminds. Nonetheless, Purdy has proven he is more than a mere puppet surrounded by stars.

Purdy is 206 of 290 passing (71 per cent) for 2,624 yards and 23 touchdowns to just five interceptions with a league-high passer rating of 118.2. It should be noted he has missed practice this week due to an ankle issue. So stay tuned.

He is wildly accurate, underrated as a creator outside of the pocket, clinical in decision-making, aggressive enough to attack downfield and an outstanding diagnostician. The win over Minnesota in Mexico was the newest addition to his MVP resume, behind which Shanahan has been phenomenal.

Purdy was 16 of 18 for 195 yards and two touchdowns when facing the blitz, while finishing eight of nine for 100 yards when pressured during blitzes, according to NextGen Stats. It would contribute to an offensive display that saw the Vikings managed an EPA per dropback of 0.613; no other team had surpassed 0.037 EPA per dropback against Minnesota entering Week 11, per Pro Football Focus. His head coach is putting him in positions for success, and Purdy is executing.

"He's the best player in the game right now. He's super dialled in, the way he prepares, the way he competes," said wide receiver Mike Evans. "He's tough. I always thought he's been underrated, his precision. Super smart player."

Purdy may not win MVP with Joe Burrow around. And Shanahan probably will not win Coach of the Year. That doesn't mean he isn't the best coach in the NFL.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brooke Pryor reports on the Steelers' Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy saga plus the reaction around town

In many ways he and Purdy are a match made in heaven, perfectly suited to one another. They are also thriving together in the face of seemingly never-ending injury obstacles.

They lead an old guard of veteran weapons, who sense another championship campaign.

George Kittle has been Purdy's most targeted pass catcher with 47 catches for a team-high 591 and seven touchdowns, while Christian McCaffrey has over 1,000 yards from scrimmage with a second-most 14 total touchdowns. Mike Evans is the big-bodied one-on-one target Purdy and Shanahan have been missing, but has missed time through injury, and Deebo Samuel is channelling his wide back days again, but has missed time through injury.

"You have to at some point put Purdy in the MVP conversation with what he's been able to do for this 49ers team," said Sky Sports NFL's Phoebe Schecter.

"I think it's hard not to look at what happened in Mexico City and not feel like this team is unstoppable, even with a litany of injuries that are going on."

The next test comes against the champions, whose defense leads the NFL in yards allowed and passing while ranking fourth in scoring and second in pressure rate.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Jason Bell and Ndamukong Suh react to the recent accusations Aaron Rodgers made about Mike McCarthy

"This Seattle defense have been so fun to watch all season long, and I think you couldn't ask for someone better in terms of Mike Macdonald," said Schecter. "They are gonna come after Brock Purdy. I know we saw the Vikings come with what felt like 90 per cent blitz rate, but I think this Seahawks team will come with a different attitude because Purdy picked them apart."

"This is a battle where the NFC West is kind of in the hands of Seattle and San Francisco."

Is this finally Shanahan's time? With the Seahawks, Los Angeles Rams and Chiefs coming up over the next month, their Super Bowl credentials are about to be put to the test.

5 things to watch live on Sky:

San Francisco's 'Unc' package

Mike Evans is 33. Keenan Allen is 34. They are two of the NFL's greatest wide receivers, and now find themselves with instrumental roles to play in San Francisco's Super Bowl hunt. Evans arrived in the offseason and Allen more recently ahead of the trade deadline, playing 19 snaps together in the 49ers' 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City. Behold the "unc package".

"We mix in so many guys, and I know everybody's name, but when I'm thinking about football and stuff, I don't always just spit out names fast. So sometimes it's just easier for me to say unc," said head coach Shanahan. "Everyone knows who I'm talking about. "I hope they like it. I think it's cool. They're not, like, really uncles. They're in their 30s. They're still young."

The nickname stemmed from George Kittle as he declared the 49ers' veteran-heavy offense "Unc city", the criteria for which is being over the age of 30. Evans is in his 13th season and Allen his 14th, both still one-on-one headaches for defenders across the league and crucial pairs of hands for Purdy come January playoff football.

Sleep is a sensitive subject in the NFL this week. But don't sleep on those uncs. Kittle, for the record, insisted he is not part of 'Unc city', despite being 33.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni had to be dragged away after reacting to a fan who had been trash-talking him

NFC East race continues

The state of things in the NFC East. No, quite literally - the state of things!

The truly dreadful standard of the NFC South is letting the East off the hook a little, but the 'battle' for supremacy among four of the NFL's most storied franchises isn't much better.

The New York Giants (6-3-1) hold the advantage, having secured arguably the best win of their season over the Jacksonville Jaguars last week, but their schedule down the stretch - following a winnable trip to the Indianapolis Colts this Sunday - looks rough, and so they could conceivably still be caught.

Whether the Dallas Cowboys (5-7), Washington Commanders (4-5-1) and Philadelphia Eagles (4-7) are capable of chasing the Giants down, though, is another matter entirely!

The Commanders could gain some ground with wins against the lowly Arizona Cardinals and Tennessee Titans over the next two weeks, plus they hold the head-to-head tiebreaker with New York.

As for the Cowboys, a season already rich with embarrassing lows reached a new nadir when blowing a Thanksgiving-record 21-point lead (with little more than a quarter left) to the Eagles, who are surely already out of contention despite that stunning comeback.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the NFL game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Buffalo Bills in Week 12

Cousins out for revenge?

Kirk Cousins doesn't exactly scream somebody who chases revenge, but how he would love to stick it to the franchise that cast him aside as he leads the Minnesota Vikings (7-3) out against the Atlanta Falcons (3-7) this weekend. Cousins signed a bumper four-year $180m deal with Atlanta in 2024 after six seasons in Minnesota, only to see the Falcons go and select another quarterback in Michael Penix Jr with the eighth overall pick in the Draft that same year. Cousins was benched ahead of Week 16 before beginning the 2025 season as backup and starting just eight games until he was released this past offseason. He has since prolonged his days as a starter in the NFL with the Las Vegas Raiders, and recently returned to the Vikings via a trade in a bid to ignite Kevin O'Connell's slumping offense. Once deemed something of a final piece route back to prominence for the Falcons, Cousins is now intent on plunging Kevin Stefanski's side further towards trouble.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jeff Reinebold believes that Kirk Cousins will be 'firing on all cylinders' when he faces his former team, the Atlanta Falcons

Darnold pressure?

Sam Darnold has come a long way from "seeing ghosts" during his early struggles with the woeful New York Jets, returning a superb 28-6 record as a starter over the past two seasons which culminated in a Super Bowl ring with the Seattle Seahawks back in February.

As such, you'd have thought his expected return this week for a key NFC West divisional clash with the San Francisco 49ers would be greeted with great fanfare. Not quite…

Darnold has struggled to replicate his championship-winning form of last season, and that of 2024 with the Minnesota Vikings, with his record 3-4 this year. Meanwhile, backup QB Drew Lock has won all three of his starts, in which he's thrown for 837 yards, seven TDs and zero interceptions, completing 73.1 per cent of his passes.

Seattle's playoff hopes, and Darnold's job might both be on the line this Sunday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chicago Bears' Rome Odunze scored the game-winning touchdown during their Thanksgiving match against the Detroit Lions

Richardson returns for Colts

He was the most athletically-gifted quarterback to ever test at the position coming into the NFL, but between persistent accuracy issues and injury setbacks, it has never quite happened for Anthony Richardson since being selected as the fourth pick of the 2023 Draft. He has an arm capable of the otherworldly throws some quarterbacks could only dream of making, and yet an arm prone to botching the most routine plays. At his best there is box office talent, but consistency has tripped him up. Richardson gets a chance to begin rebuilding his career as starter this weekend when he takes the reins for the Indianapolis Colts against the Giants - his first start since the 2024 season. It comes following the release of Daniel Jones amid an outright rebuild in Indianapolis. Awaiting him is a Giants defense ranked seventh in yards and fifth in passing.

Latest news

The Pittsburgh Steelers released Aaron Rodgers following his stunning claims that head coach Mike McCarthy fell asleep in team meetings

Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington was ruled out of Sunday's game against the Titans with a shoulder injury

Former 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk signed with the Washington Commanders practice squad

Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons made his season debut in a return from his knee injury in Wednesday's loss to the Rams

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he would not fire Brian Schottenheimer as head coach after they blew a 21-point lead in a Thanksgiving loss to the Eagles

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Philadelphia Eagles' DeVonta Smith scored a much-needed touchdown against Dallas Cowboys

Key stats:

With a completion percentage of 70-or-higher against the Saints, Joe Burrow can become the first player in NFL history with a completion percentage of 70-or-higher in nine consecutive games (minimum 25 attempts per game)

With a passer rating of 110-or-higher against Seattle, Purdy can join Russell Wilson (34 games) and Patrick Mahomes (30) as the only quarterbacks with a passer rating of 110-or-higher in 30 games within their first five seasons in NFL history

With 100 receiving yards at San Francisco, Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba can become the first player in NFL history with at least eight receptions and 100 receiving yards in five consecutive road games

Cardinals tight end Trey McBride needs three receptions against Washington to become the fourth tight end in NFL history with at least 90 receptions in three career seasons, joining Travis Kelce (seven), Tony Gonzalez (five) and Jason Witten (four).

Sports.title: Wesley Fofana ‘lost his head’ after being booed by own fans as pressure heaps on Xabi Alonso
Sports.content:
Wesley Fofana ‘lost his head’ after being booed by own fans as pressure heaps on Xabi Alonso

Wesley Fofana copped brutal chants from his own fans as he conceded a penalty and was hooked during Chelsea's 3-2 defeat to Nottingham Forest.

The Frenchman followed up his bizarre midweek interview with a shocking performance that saw him taken off after 55 minutes at the City Ground.



3 Fofana was having a nightmare, and then, he gave away a penalty

And Sam Matterface believed 'he lost his head' as the central defender was withdrawn to be replaced by Levi Colwill.

Given the widely condemned interview, it was a surprise that he even started, but Xabi Alonso partnered him alongside Moises Caicedo.

Every touch he had was booed, while the Blues fans subjected him to chants of, 'F*** off Fofana, you're not wanted here.'



And as he was taken off, the travelling supporters yelled: "W*****."

Reacting to the defender's forgettable few minutes on talkSPORT's commentary, Matterface and Stuart Pearce were left baffled by Fofana as he bundled into Liam Delap and gave away a spot kick.

Matterface said: "Fofana has brought him down with the clumsiest challenge you will ever see and his nightmare week gets worse and worse.



"He gives away a penalty. Delap ran at Fofana and ruined him as far as the physical battle was concerned, and I haven't a clue what Fofana was trying to do.

Pearce then said: "Delap has turned him, and he's got back into the box and Fofana has just launched himself in the year and bodied him.



"It's a ludicrous challenge and ludicrous defending. Dear oh dear."

Matterface added: "Fofana did an interview this week in which he claimed his penalty miss didn't stick around in his conscience for too long.

3 Fofana claimed that he didn't care about his missed penalty in the Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool earlier in the season Credit: Getty

"He laughed it off. If he laughs this one off too, I don't think he'll be too popular with the Chelsea fans, who booed him every time he touched the ball in the first half."

And later on before he was taken off, he said: "Fofana looks like he's lost his head."



What did Fofana say?

In an interview with YouTuber Zack Nani, without Chelsea's permission, the defender made light of his penalty miss.

He said: "It's fine; it doesn't matter. I couldn't care less. I know there's another match in three days.

Laughing, Fofana added: "I sent a real beauty of a shot way over the bar. Did you see my shot? I really blasted it high [laughs]. I remember a fan, way up high, he actually managed to catch the ball."

Alonso claimed pre-match that the situation had been dealt with, but after a shambolic period of time on the pitch, the Spaniard had no choice but to take him off.



3 Forest made it back-to-back home wins against Manchester City and Chelsea

Night to forget

It was three defeats in a row for Chelsea as Forest lifted themselves away from the relegation zone, and Alonso has now lost as many Premier League games as Liam Rosenior in fewer fixtures.

The home side made a very bright start and opened the scoring early on as Daniel Munoz curled a cross into the box.

Igor Jesus was free, and he hooked a stunning volley into the corner.

Forest then made it 2-0 early into the second half as Fofana bundled Delap over, and Morgan Gibbs-White stepped up to slot home the penalty.



Not long after Fofana was hooked, half-time substitute Emmanuel Emegha cut the deficit with a smart finish after a deflected shot fell into his path.

But Chelsea's inability to defend reared its ugly head again when Gibbs-White sealed the three points as he got on the end of Xaver Schlager's pass and hooked the ball over Emiliano Martinez.

Emegha did score again from Pedro Neto's cross, but it was too little too late.

Sports.title: Southampton star sparks instant scuffle after taunting Middlesbrough fans with Spygate celebration
Sports.content:
Southampton's Finn Azaz saw his opportunity to channel his inner Emmanuel Adebayor and took it.

The Saints star put his side 2-0 up with 10 minutes to go when he pounced on a mistake from Middlesbrough's Aidan Morris and slotted past Radek Vitek from just inside the 18-yard box.

2 Azaz made himself public enemy number one among Boro supporters Credit: Getty

But rather than celebrate with his own fans, Azaz decided to run the length of the field and poked fun at the Boro supporters who had travelled to the opposite end of the country.

Azaz, who spent two seasons at Boro before moving to Southampton in August last year, wiped his eyes and pretended to cry in front of the away end.

The celebration earned Azaz an immediate yellow card, but more chaos was to come.

Boro striker Will Lankshear led the charge of white shirts who weren't going to let Azaz face no repercussions for his actions as a heated scuffle broke out.

Eventually the players from both sides were separated by officials.

Finn Azaz explains celebration

Speaking after the match, Azaz explained why he made a beeline for Boro fans.

"They (Boro fans) sang about my familoy home and away last season, so I was just waiting for my moment to get one back," Azaz told Sky Sports following the match.

And when asked if he had any regrets about the celebration, the Ireland international simply said: "None whatsoever."

As Azaz conducted his interview, Oasis' 'Stop Crying Your Heart Out' was played on the speakers at St Mary's.

Why was there so much emotion between Saints and Boro?

The emotionally-charged scenes stemmed from the Spygate scandal that rocked last season's play-offs, where a junior Saints staffer was caught spying on a Boro training session.

2 Saints' Ryan Manning even brought out the binoculars as both sides scrapped Credit: Getty

Southampton, who beat Boro across the two legs in their play-off semi-final, were subsequently booted out of the play-offs.

Saints' expulsion then allowed Boro to take their place in the final, but they were beaten 1-0 by Hull City.

Being booted out of the play-offs was not the only punishment Southampton copped, as they received a four-point deduction while manager Tonda Eckert was handed a suspended six-week ban for his role in the Spygate scandal.

Saints have the last laugh

Despite the hefty sanctions, Southampton put it in the rear-view mirror with a big three points against fellow high-flyers Boro.

Ryan Manning broke the deadlock in the 59th minute when he side-footed James Bree's low cross from seven yards out.

Azaz doubled the home side's advantage to send Saints fans into delirium.

Despite Boro's best efforts, they could not break a stubborn Southampton resistance.

Sports.title: Why there are so few Premier League fixtures this Saturday
Sports.content:
Why there are so few Premier League fixtures this Saturday

The beginning of the festive period of Premier League fixtures starts this weekend, but there isn't much going on Saturday.

Usually, there are plenty of games to get stuck into, but the top-flight only has three this weekend.



3 The first Merseyside derby of the season will be on Sunday, and live on talkSPORT Credit: Getty

And there is no early game on Saturday either, with that being moved to Sunday.

We also have a spate of 2:05pm kick-offs on Sunday as well.

Here, talkSPORT.com looks into why there are not many Premier League matches this Saturday.

Why are there so few Premier League fixtures on Saturday?

The Merseyside derby between Everton and Liverpool at Hill Dickinson was scheduled for Saturday.



But it had to be moved due to Liverpool's involvement in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

Premier League rules stipulate there should be a 60 hour window between fixtures for teams, and that wasn't possible if it had been on Saturday.



It could have taken place at 8pm on Saturday, but police and other authorities wanted the kick-off time to be as early as possible to reduce the chance of crowd trouble, so that game is at 12pm on Sunday, November 29.

We have that game live and exclusively on talkSPORT with Reshmin Chowdhury serving as your presenter.



Commentary will come from Sam Matterface and former Scotland striker Andy Gray.

The next issue comes from the amount of teams that are in the Europa League and Conference League.

3 Sunderland were one of several English teams involved in European action in midweek Credit: AFP

The Premier League has three Europa League representatives in Bournemouth, Sunderland and Crystal Palace, and there is one Conference League side, which are Brighton and Hove Albion.



So, due to the 60 hour window, all four of those must play on Sunday or Monday, and there are no Monday fixtures this gameweek due to a midweek fixture list.

All four of those teams are kicking off at 2:05pm, and that is purely to accommodate any overlap from the Merseyside derby.

Then we have Arsenal taking on Manchester City at 4:30pm on Sunday.

Now, this could be played at a different time, but it is the flagship fixture of the weekend and has been selected for coverage by Sky Sports in that slot.

The 4:30pm slot would never be left empty, so Arsenal taking on Man City is in that one.



3 Man United's home game against Brentford is one of three Premier League Saturday games Credit: Getty

Sports.title: ‘Very fascinated by it’ – Virgil van Dijk drops major hint to World Cup winner over his future
Sports.content:
‘Very fascinated by it’ – Virgil van Dijk drops major hint to World Cup winner over his future

Virgil van Dijk would be interested in playing in Serie A.

That is according to 2006 World Cup winner Fabio Cannavaro, who revealed the latest on Van Dijk as his Liverpool contract ticks down.

4 Van Dijk might be advancing in years, but he is still a key player for Liverpool Credit: Getty



The Dutchman signed a one-year contract extension last season, but it means he will have just six months of his deal left in January.

That means he will soon be able to sign pre-contract agreements with clubs abroad.

It comes amid links to AC Milan for the Liverpool legend as his time at Anfield potentially comes to a close.

Speaking to Gazzetta dello Sport, Cannavaro said: "I saw him (Van Dijk) at the World Cup and he told me that he would like to have an experience in Italy.



"He is very fascinated by it. It would be nice to see Van Dijk at Milan."

Fabio Cannavaro's praise for Virgil van Dijk

Cannavaro was once one of the best defenders in the world and captained Italy to the 2006 World Cup.



And he is a huge fan of Van Dijk.

Speaking about the Dutchman, he said: "In recent years, he has combined great physical strength with outstanding speed.

"Once, a coach said to Paolo Maldini: 'You turn badly.' And he replied: 'Mister, as long as I get to the ball.'"



"It was the same for me.

4 Van Dijk has two Premier League titles and a Champions League title to his name from his time with Liverpool so far Credit: Getty

"When you are very fast, you can afford a technical error. The problem comes when that speed is no longer there."

What has Van Dijk said?

The 35-year-old knows that his time at Liverpool might be coming to an end.

However, he doesn't believe that he is anywhere close to being done as a professional footballer.



"The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion," Van Dijk said during the latest international break.

"Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see.

"At this moment of time, if anyone says that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either.

4 Andoni Iraola has shown a lot of trust in Van Dijk, leaving him out of just one game so far Credit: Getty

"But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game. Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the new year coming, we'll see then.



"But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a big part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years.

"If it's getting extended, we'll see then.

"If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer."

If that were to happen, it would be very emotional for Van Dijk after joining the club in January 2018 and becoming a club legend.

On that potential departure, he said: "Well, yeah, probably for me the most and the family because it's been an incredible time.

4 Andoni Iraola has shown a lot of trust in Van Dijk since taking over Credit: Getty



"But I don't look too far in the future and that's been, in my opinion, also a little bit of a success. I won't change it now either.

"Whatever happens, happens. Let's see."

One person who clearly likes Van Dijk is manager Andoni Iraola, with the Spaniard starting him in ever Premier League game so far.

The captain has played every minute in the top-flight and has missed just one match, which was against Tottenham Hotspur in the Carabao Cup.

Recently, he praised his captain's leadership and praised him for helping him settle in.



Iraola said: “It’s not just helping me it’s helping the teammates a lot. He knows what it takes to be successful here, especially the ones who play around him, he’s a big big help, sometimes demanding when he has to be.

"But also understands he has to put the bar high because of the high demands here. If you want to deliver, you have to accept those challenges and Virgil helps me and also his teammates.

“That is almost the legacy that he will leave. How good the teammates are going to be and still we hope he continues with us for a lot of time, but he’s not thinking in terms of helping others a lot.”
