Sports.title: Chelsea nab teenage wonderkid from sister club before a ball was even kicked
Sports.content:
Chelsea nab teenage wonderkid from sister club before a ball was even kicked

Chelsea are reportedly set to sign 17-year-old midfielder Mohamed Zongo.

The Blues have agreed a deal to sign the Burkina Faso international from SF Cascades.



3 Chelsea have agreed a deal to sign Burkina Faso international Zongo Credit: Getty

Zongo will officially join Chelsea after he turns 18 in November 2027.

Clubs in England cannot sign players from overseas before their 18th birthday.

As a result, Zongo will arrive at Stamford Bridge at the start of the 2028 January transfer window.



The teenager had previously been expected to move to Strasbourg before joining Chelsea.

Zongo has now been pictured holding up the Blues' shirt at their facilities, though.



Chelsea agree Zongo deal

According to Fabrizio Romano, BlueCo had won the race to sign the in-demand youngster back in December last year.

The consortium own both Chelsea and Ligue 1 side Strasbourg, with their plan for Zongo to initially head to France upon arriving in Europe.



However, he will now move to the Premier League without playing a minute of senior club football.

Despite that, Zongo has already been capped by Burkina Faso, having made his debut against Argentina in October.

He came off the bench in a 7-0 loss to the three-time World Cup winners in Buenos Aires.

3 Zongo will join Chelsea after turning 18 in November 2027 Credit: Getty



Zongo previously starred for the Stallions at the 2025 Under-17 World Cup before BlueCo swooped for his signature.

The playmaker scored twice and provided three assists in six appearances at the tournament.

His performances helped Burkina Faso reach the quarter-finals before suffering a narrow defeat to Italy.

BlueCo's Chelsea ownership

Zongo's transfer is the latest instance of a player moving between Chelsea and Strasbourg under BlueCo.



They include the likes of Andrey Santos, Mike Penders, Ben Chilwell and Filip Jorgensen, who have all moved either on loan or permanently from Chelsea to their French sister club.

In contrast, the west London outfit completed the signings of both Emmanuel Emegha and Valentin Barco from Strasbourg this summer as well as hiring former boss Liam Rosenior in January.

3 Zongo had initially been expected to join Strasbourg after BlueCo agreed a deal for the teenager Credit: Getty

BlueCo first purchased the Blues from Roman Abramovich in May 2022.

Their football portfolio was expanded a year later by becoming shareholders at Strasbourg before acquiring close to a 100 per cent stake.

Sports.title: I had $1million offer to buy Premier League club rejected in the 1970s for bizarre reason
Sports.content:
I had $1million offer to buy Premier League club rejected in the 1970s for bizarre reason

Composer and musician Rick Wakeman once tried to buy Brentford in the 1970s, only to be turned down by the club.

Wakeman was signed up by jazz music producing duo the Ertegun brothers, and with their backing, they submitted a huge offer of $1million to buy the Bees, who were in the lower regions of the English football pyramid.

2 Griffin Park was Brentford's home until very recently, and Wakeman could have been the owner Credit: Getty

But Brentford's owners at the time decided that it was a no for Wakeman, who is now on the board with the Bees.

The 77-year-old joined Paul Hawksbee and Aaron Moore to talk about his book, The Wizard of Prog: The Truth and Something Like The Truth.

Hawksbee asked Wakeman about his attempts to buy Brentford, and he said: "Yeah, I did.

"You have to go back to the 1970s. There were two wonderful brothers (the Erteguns).

"We were signed to their label, and they had New York Cosmos and had brought in Pele and all sorts.

"I remember getting a phone call from Ahmet, and he said: 'Rick, we've got a chance to buy this guy called Peeley'. I said, 'It's Pele', and he asked if he was good. 'Oh yes, rather brilliant,' and I asked if he could afford him, and he said: 'Of course I can'.

"So, they encouraged me and my manager and a few other people to buy the franchise Philadelphia Fury.

"But Sebuhi phoned me and asked to come and see me, and he was very knowledgeable about football, and he told me to buy Brentford.

"We were struggling in the lower regions of the third division, might have even been the fourth, and he said we'd start with $1million, which was a fortune back then.

"He told me to put together a good team to run the club, and I asked him why did he want Brentford, and he wanted the roof."

2 Wakeman's offer to buy Brentford was very serious and would have been a staggering amount of money

Hawksebee then jumped in and said: "Oh, yes, it used to be KLM, so you'd fly into Heathrow and see the roof of Griffin Park."

Wakeman continued: "So, he wanted to rent the roof and offered Brentford a huge chunk of money, but the club turned me down, which was quite upsetting."

Eventually

Thankfully, Wakeman is now involved with Brentford.

The late Dan Tana made Wakeman part of the board during his time as Brentford chairman before he passed away in 2025.

Reflecting on that, he said: "Later on, I became a director through the wonderful Dan Tana, so I've been very lucky with the clubs I am involved with."

Sports.title: Premier League clubs make feelings clear on how Man City should be punished
Sports.content:
Premier League clubs make feelings clear on how Man City should be punished

Manchester City's owners should be forced to sell the club for breaching Premier League Financial Fair Play (FFP) rules.

That is reportedly the stance of senior figures at fellow top-flight clubs ahead of sanctions being announced.

3 Premier League clubs believe City's owners should be forced to sell as punishment for FFP breaches Credit: Getty

The Premier League announced in September that City had been found guilty of almost all charges against them.

It came after the club were first charged with 115 breaches of FFP rules in February 2023 for alleged offences between 2009 and 2018.

City have since appealed the verdict, with a hearing scheduled for December.

If their challenge against the ruling fails, sanctions are expected to be handed out in the new year.

Rivals call for City to be sold

According to the BBC, officials at rival Premier League clubs believe City's owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group, should be made to sell the club.

It is seen as an appropriate sanction for their rule breaches and failure to co-operate with the subsequent investigation.

The Abu Dhabi United Group purchased City in September 2008, before the start of their alleged financial offences.

United Arab Emirates vice-president and deputy prime minister Sheikh Mansour is the founder and owner of the private equity group.

City's owners could be forced into selling by the Independent Football Regulator (IFR).

The IFR has the power to remove directors at clubs if they are deemed unsuitable.

3 Sheikh Mansour's Abu Dhabi United Group bought City in September 2008 Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, in the most serious cases, the IFR can even force a club to be sold.

A selection of potential sanctions are understood to be on the table for an Independent Commission ahead of the appeal hearing.

They include fines, points deductions and possible expulsion from the Premier League.

Legal cases against City

Fellow Premier League giants are also preparing legal cases against City.

Manchester United, Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Arsenal have all reserved the right to seek damages.

Their preparations to bring legal action against the Etihad Stadium outfit have stepped up since the verdict was announced.

3 City are set for an appeal hearing against their guilty verdict next month Credit: Getty

City qualified for the Champions League in eight of the nine seasons when their FFP breaches occurred.

They also won three Premier League titles in the 2011/12, 2013/14 and 2017/18 campaigns.

Sports.title: Southampton star sparks brawl after sprinting length of pitch to mock Middlesbrough fans with 'crying' celebration as Tonda Eckert's men beat bitter rivals in first meeting since Spygate scandal
Sports.content:
Southampton’s Finn Azaz ran the length of the pitch to confront the Middlesbrough fans as the Saints beat them 2-0 in their first meeting since Spygate.

Going full Emmanuel Adebayor, former Boro attacker Azaz found the bottom corner before idiotically and classlessly sprinting towards the travelling support to goad them.

It prompted an unnecessary fracas between the two teams as Azaz and Will Lankshear - who wasn't even at Boro last season - squared up, while travelling fans tried to get over the barricade.

'They sang about it (Azaz leaving) home and away last season, so I was just waiting for my moment to get one back,' Azaz said post-match. 'I have no regrets whatsoever.'

The scenes calmed post-match with teams celebrating and consoling their own fans respectively. Southampton, though, rubbed it in over the speakers when they played Oasis' Stop Crying Your Heart Out. Shamelessly, a box of tissues were put on the podium in the press conference room too.

Saints beat Middlesbrough in last season’s play-off semi-final but were booted out by the EFL four days before the final after Daily Mail Sport revealed Southampton had sent their very own Johnny English to spy on Boro’s training sessions.

In a bitter reunion, Ryan Manning tucked James Bree’s neat cutback past Radek Vitek on 58 minutes before Finn Azaz added a second as Southampton remained unbeaten at home in 10 months. The Saints players, though, were needlessly provocative.

Considering Southampton started this season on minus four points for the breaches, their staggering endorsement of the cheating was as indiscreet as the espionage itself.

Southampton's Finn Azaz mocked Middlesbrough's fans by pretending to cry after scoring

His celebration - in their first meeting since last season's 'Spygate' - sparked a brawl, with Azaz being booked

‘We’ll spy when we want,’ sang the Southampton fans – a reminder of when their spy kid tried to conceal himself behind a tree near Middlesbrough’s training ground to film their training session. The EFL discovered three further spying missions on investigation.

Both managers called for an armistice before the match, but that memo clearly hadn't reached the Southampton marketing team, who posted an inflammatory video on social media. Eckert and Boro boss Kim Hellberg remained cordial throughout, but it was otherwise hostile.

The classless 79-second film mocked Boro, with the narrator declaring, ‘they got another go, their story continued’ over footage of Oli McBurnie’s winning goal for Hull City in the play-off final.

It was also projected onto the big screen just eight minutes before kick-off. That wasn't the last reference to their play-off final defeat, either, with Saints fans repeatedly singing: ‘We saw you cry on the tele’.

Saints even took a leaf out of Chelsea's book before kick-off, playing The Liquidator and chanting: ‘f*** off Boro, the Saints’.

The visitors sang: 'What the f****** hell was that?' while Saints fans unfurled a banner depicting their manager, who was handed a suspended ban for his undercover directive.

Meanwhile, the Boro players were subjected to a vehement chorus of boos every time they entered the pitch, from the pre-match warm-ups to the start of the second half.

The atmosphere inside St Mary's was electric. Southampton fully embraced their cheats tag as they claimed three points, responding to chants of ‘you cheating b*******, you know what you are’ with sarcastic applause.

And the victory moves them to within four points of Middlesbrough, who remain top of the table going into the weekend but could slip down as far as fifth.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso is CONFUSING his Chelsea stars: Blues boss must take his share of the blame as chaos threatens to engulf the club again after deserved defeat by Nottingham Forest, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
It is not yet December and already chaos threatens to engulf Chelsea once more.

A bright start to the season under Xabi Alonso was, it transpires, merely a hazy, late summer mirage. Winter, it seems, will bring only a new version of a classic modern Chelsea discontent.

A coach who has started to do strange things – Alonso selected midfielder Moises Caicedo at centre-half here for the first time in his seven-year club career – a fanbase turning on everyone from the owners to the players and a team slowly getting disorientated on a dismally familiar carousel of selection changes.

It is Chelsea rebooted but just with the same stories written by and for different people. How dismal it must feel for those with this great club in their hearts.

Here on a misty and rainy night at the City Ground, nobody suffered more in Chelsea colours than central defender Wesley Fofana.

Harangued throughout by his own travelling fans for a foolish and unauthorised midweek YouTube interview in which he seemed to make light of missing a penalty in the Carabao Cup defeat at Liverpool, the Frenchman was hauled off soon after conceding a penalty that allowed Morgan Gibbs-White to stretch Nottingham Forest’s lead to two goals early in the second half.

Wesley Fofana was hauled off soon after conceding a penalty that allowed Morgan Gibbs-White to stretch Nottingham Forest’s lead to two goals early in the second half

Fofana was harangued throughout by his own travelling fans for an unauthorised interview in which he seemed to make light of missing a penalty in the Carabao Cup defeat at Liverpool

‘You are not wanted here,’ sang the Chelsea fans and after this they may get their wish. For his own sake, it may be a while before we see the young defender again.

At that stage of the night, Chelsea actually still had hope. Half-time substitute Emmanuel Emegha had just pulled a goal back with his team’s first shot on target of the whole night. He was to get another right at the death, too.

But having started the game with a fabulous fifth minute volley from the Brazilian Igor Jesus – it came off his shin but that doesn’t matter – Forest had the look of a team with their opponents’ measure all evening and that was how it played out. And when Gibbs-White scored his second of the game to make it 3-1 with less than 20 minutes left, Chelsea’s night was pretty much over.

Alonso must certainly take his share of the blame here. Caicedo is his best midfielder but was played out of position with England’s Levi Colwill left on the bench.

Put simply, it backfired. Chelsea’s defending did not improve on recent efforts and in midfield, where they were outplayed by Forest’s Xaver Schlager and James McAtee, they missed the Ecuadorian desperately.

More widely Alonso’s Premier League record – six wins from 12 games – is now worse than that of Liam Rosenior when he was sacked back in April. Their six defeats are one more than Manchester United. And this at a time when Chelsea are playing but once a week. No European competition and out of the Carabao Cup, the Spaniard has plenty of time with his players on the training field. What is he doing with it? Confusing everybody, it would seem, for what Chelsea presented here was a jumble. How they lost by only a goal was a miracle in itself. They deserved nothing.

Forest had come in to the game with issues of their own. Their coach Oliver Glasner had accused his international squad of not making enough effort with their English. Early on their football spoke for them as McAtee spread the play with a wonderful fifth minute pass, Daniel Munoz crossed and Jesus rose to volley his second league goal of the season high past Emiliano Martinez quite wonderfully.

Caicedo is Alonso's best midfielder but the Ecuadorian was played out of position by the Chelsea manager with England’s Levi Colwill left on the bench

Alonso’s Premier League record – six wins from 12 games – is now worse than that of Liam Rosenior when he was sacked back in April

What followed for the rest of the first half did not match that quality. Over time, Alonso’s team did find a way into the game territorially but a free-kick routine that ended with Morgan Rogers ballooning ten yards over the bar perhaps summed their efforts up as indeed did the fact they ended the opening period having managed only three touches inside the Forest box.

Replacing the ineffectual Danny Welbeck with Emegha at the interval brought Chelsea some shape at least. Welbeck had been peripheral. Forest were the team to kick on, though, and when Fofana slipped catastrophically to allow Liam Delap through in the 50th minute, he then brought him down. Gibbs-White slotted in the penalty and Chelsea were in big trouble.

With the away end threatening revolt, Alonso’s team somehow fashioned a lifeline goal from nowhere within four minutes. Pedro Neto’s speculative shot struck Forest defender Jair Cunha on the thigh and when the ball dropped to Emegha, he controlled it instinctively and found the corner.

With Fofana soon withdrawn to doubtless protect his own sanity, Chelsea’s fans now had nothing else to do but support their team. The visitors’ sense of desperation certainly made it a better game but what followed only served to damn Chelsea even more.

Far from the goal imbuing them with the impetus and belief to rescue the game, Alonso’s players somehow allowed Forest to take the initiative once more. There was a fatuous and unsuccessful penalty appeal for handball against Cunha – he had his arms clamped to his side when Rogers’ cross struck him – but precious little else.

And when the generally excellent Austrian Schlager threaded the needle to find Gibbs-White through a crowd with 17 minutes left, the England forward lifted the ball over the advancing Martinez to present a two-goal margin once again.

Chelsea subsequently offered almost nothing only to score – this time with an Emegha header – with two minutes left. Had they added an equaliser it would have been wholly unjust. They didn’t.

Sports.title: Professional golfer MJ Daffue diagnosed with brain tumor weeks after earning his tour card as he shares heartbreaking statement
Sports.content:
Professional golfer MJ Daffue diagnosed with brain tumor weeks after earning his tour card as he shares heartbreaking statement

Professional golfer MJ Daffue has shared that he has been diagnosed with cancer just weeks after gaining his tour card.

Daffue, 37, earned his card for the DP World Tour earlier this month after finishing fifth in the HotelPlanner Tour standings with a third-place finish in the Road to Mallorca Grand Final.

However, his career will now have to take a backseat after the South African was diagnosed with a brain tumor.

Daffue revealed that he was given the brutal diagnosis after he was hospitalized with a mystery infection around 10 days ago.

While doctors could not determine the source of the infection, they did discover a tumor in his brain and liver.

Following testing, it was determined that the tumor on his liver was benign but the one in his brain is more severe.

Professional golfer MJ Daffue has shared that he has been diagnosed with cancer

The South African player, 37, earned his card for the DP World Tour earlier this month

Daffue is currently on strong medication to attack the brain tumor but he admitted that he was 'struggling a bit physically.'

'It's taken a while to post anything about this year because of the difficult time the past 2 weeks has been,' he wrote on Instagram. 'This year has been incredible and we have been so blessed with good golf.

'Unfortunately i ended up in the hospital with an infection about 10 days ago and after lots of tests they could not find the source. However they did find a Tumor on my brain and my liver.'

He added: 'I am in great spirits and the care team and neurosurgeon has a perfect plan. I feel very confident that this is something that i will also kick butt and be ready to go soon.

'I appreciate all the messages so far and can't wait to be fully healthy and attacking the top of the leaderboards again soon. Happy thanksgiving to everyone. Enjoy a great time with your loved ones.'

Daffue enjoyed a resurgent year on the golf course in 2026. He started the year outside the world top 800 but secured two victories on the HotelPlanner Tour to clinch a DP World Tour card.

He also earned three top-10 finishes on the DP World Tour this year.

'Starting the year with no ranking meant I had to take every playing opportunity I got,' he said after earning his card. 'This meant it was hard to plan a schedule and so I spent weeks on the road, away from family and friends, which was hard.

'Most importantly, thanks to my wife for the love and being my rock — I can't be anything without you. So I'm super proud to come through the other side and it all be worthwhile.'

Sports.title: Tyson Fury is CLEARED to fight Anthony Joshua: Gypsy King clears medical checks after Netflix schizophrenia claim threw $150m bout into jeopardy
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury has been given the medical all clear for his British bonanza fight against Anthony Joshua.

The mega millions world heavyweight title battle at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on December 11 was in jeopardy following claims that the Gypsy King is suffering from schizophrenia.

British Boxing Board of Control general secretary Robert Smith accelerated a review by doctors who found him fit late last night.

Smith says: 'All up to date medicals satisfactory and the promoters informed this morning.'

US streaming giant Netflix have deleted the panic inducing portion of their Fury documentary in which his wife Paris was pushed to suggest he was schizophrenic as well as bipolar.

Such a condition would have obliged the Board's medics to deny permission for the Gypsy King to enter the ring.

Tyson Fury has been given the medical all clear for his British bonanza fight against Anthony Joshua

The mega millions world heavyweight title battle at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on December 11 was in jeopardy

In which case hundreds of millions of dollars would have been lost by all involved in this huge promotion.

Fury's wife tried desperately to row back on her original claims, saying Tyson 'doesn’t have' schizophrenia and 'has never received a diagnosis'.

Netflix confirmed that Paris's suggestion has been removed from the documentary.

A statement read: 'Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.'

After that 'new information' was received, Paris said: 'I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary.

'I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word "schizophrenic".

'Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis.

'Mental health is complex, and it isn’t always easy to find the right words, especially when you’re living it with someone you love.

'I’m so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we’ve received as a family.'

His wife Paris now insists that he is not schizophrenic having originally claimed he had 'mild schizophrenia'

Fury had no chance of being allowed to fight Joshua unless doctors were convinced he is mentally stable

Smith, the general secretary of British Boxing's Board of Control, confirmed Fury had no chance of being allowed to fight Joshua unless doctors were convinced he is mentally stable.

'Only one thing is certain,' he said. 'That Tyson will not be allowed to enter the ring unless our doctors are satisfied there is no risk to his health.

'We are reviewing all the information about his mental condition and will come to a decision about authorising the fight in the next few days.'

In the 90-minute documentary, Fury opens up on his mental health, admitting: 'Words can’t explain the darkness I was in.

'It was like the living version of the pits of hell’s fire. I 100 per cent thought I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked and that scared me so much.'

Fury and AJ are in line to bank $150million between them for the night's work, while the Principality Stadium, Saudi Arabian backers under His Excellency Turki Alalshikh and hotels, bars and restaurants in Cardiff would also have been stung if the fight was unable to go ahead.

Netflix want to use the all-British showdown to cement their move into major boxing.

The start time of the fight was moved to the early hours of the morning at Netflix's request in a bid to cater to an American audience and maximise the numbers tuning in.

That meant Cardiff Council had to grant special dispensation for a 1.30am UK fight time on December 11 and locals complained the extended curfew could cause issues in the surrounding area.

Despite early reports of an 80,000-plus sell-out in just an hour on the day tickets went on the market, there are still hundreds of seats for sale. Some being pushed with an offer of beer being thrown in.

This raises further concern about the impact of alcohol on the traditionally rowdy Friday night in Cardiff when the Stadium empties the crowd onto the street at around 3am. So much so that the police are considering breathalysing late arrivals at the fight.

HEARN GIVES IT THE THUMBS-UP Eddie Hearn has given the British Boxing Board of Control full support for taking scrupulous care that Tyson Fury is mentally fit to face his man, Anthony Joshua, in their blockbuster world heavyweight title fight, writes Jeff Powell. An element of panic followed the Netflix documentary on Fury which suggested the Gypsy King is schizophrenic. Joshua's long time promoter backed Board General Secretary Robert Smith's prompt call on their medical specialists to provide a proper diagnosis. An adverse diagnosis would have cost him and all the other major players in the huge promotion millions. Joshua, Fury, the Saudi backers, and Cardiff's Principality Stadium and Netflix are included in that list. Hearn says: 'Obviously Tyson should not have gone into the fight if he is schizophrenic. Fortunately we have the best Board of Control in the world. They always look fully into every problem that comes before them and come to the proper decision. No matter what the pressures on them.' Hearn is one of many questioning the role of streaming giant Netflix in the affair which could have pulled the plug on the richest fight in British boxing history. After Netflix redacted the portion of the documentary in which Tyson's wife, Paris, was prompted to suggest her husband had schizophrenia as well as being bipolar, Hearn said: 'There comes a point when such programmes are driven by the entertainment need rather than the sport. They are looking for headlines that scream "WOW, what a story".' The documentary focused far more on Fury's mental health crises than the sport. Netflix engaged a director who, although talented, admitted she knew nothing about boxing before the project was developed and later confessed she had never heard of Oleksandr Usyk, even though the Ukrainian legend is the greatest boxer of his generation and has defeated Fury twice in becoming the undisputed world heavyweight champion. Might it have been better for Netflix to engage someone with at least a rudimentary knowledge of the subject? Mrs Fury has recanted her vague words and Hearn is sympathetic towards Tyson's long and well-documented struggles with depression. He adds: 'Tyson has his battles with mental health and sometimes lapses into confusion about what he says. Of course we're pleased he's been properly and medically cleared to fight.' Fury has used his fame to help and counsel countless mental health sufferers but would have been at risk of more acute depression himself had he, along with Joshua, been denied what will be in many ways the defining fight of their illustrious careers.

Sports.title: David Raya MISSES training ahead of Arsenal's crunch clash with Man City in blow for Mikel Arteta
Sports.content:
David Raya MISSES training ahead of Arsenal's crunch clash with Man City in blow for Mikel Arteta

David Raya didn’t take part in Arsenal’s training session today, plunging into doubt his availability for Sunday’s Premier League showdown against Manchester City.

Raya appeared to be in agony as he was forced off in the 70th minute of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw at Newcastle last Saturday, hurting his left shoulder in an accidental collision with William Osula.

There were initial fears the goalkeeper could be facing an extended spell on the sidelines, with Kepa Arrizabalaga playing in Tuesday’s Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund.

Raya appeared in agony after hurting his left shoulder in a collision with William Osula

Yet Mikel Arteta this afternoon alluded to there being a chance Raya would be fit enough to play on Sunday, replying ‘yeah’ when asked if he was hopeful of the goalkeeper’s availability.

He also said: ‘Yeah, they're all training. Bukayo (Saka) as well is training…’, alluding to the individual work the winger is doing away from the main group.

When asked, ‘is he (Raya) diving around?’ Arteta replied: ‘(On) that, I'm not sure.’

His absence from the training session doesn’t rule the goalkeeper out of Sunday’s fixture, but significant doubts remain over whether Raya will be fit to face Man City.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca's ref rage: Man City boss claims recent decisions are worst he has 'ever seen' as he becomes latest manager to hit out at officials
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca's ref rage: Man City boss claims recent decisions are worst he has 'ever seen' as he becomes latest manager to hit out at officials

Enzo Maresca has echoed Mauricio Pochettino’s punchy criticism of refereeing displays by claiming that some recent decisions against Manchester City are among the worst he has ever witnessed.

The absorbing rivalry between titans Erling Haaland and Gabriel – a battle renowned for excessive physicality - returns when City go to Premier League champions Arsenal on Sunday.

And Maresca suggested that key calls in City’s recent winless run have contributed to them falling six points behind Mikel Arteta’s leaders.

Asked whether Haaland is treated unfairly by officials, the Italian said: ‘I can see that, to be honest. I can see also more things in the last four or five games - probably since the international break.

‘I’ve never seen in my life a player touch the ball with both arms and no penalty. For instance against Brighton, (Lewis) Dunk. I never seen it in my life. If you remember, both. No penalty. The other one was like volleyball.’

The second complaint from that Brighton defeat was an appeal for handball against Lukas Vuskovic, when Diego Gomez headed into the defender’s outstretched arm. The league’s Key Match Incidents panel voted 3-2 in favour of Craig Pawson’s decision not to award a penalty for Dunk’s handball.

Maresca suggested that key calls in City’s recent winless run have contributed to them falling six points behind Mikel Arteta’s leaders

New Manchester United boss Pochettino said last weekend that with VAR, the league possesses ‘the best car but we need to drive it in the right way’ following Leny Yoro’s sending off at Liverpool.

Maresca’s analysis also partly centred on how VAR is being used as he raised Haaland’s disallowed goal against Fulham at the weekend, when the striker was adjudged to have fouled Bernd Leno and VAR stuck with the on-field decision.

‘The last game against Fulham, if you just stop (the image) when the goalkeeper has the ball there, it looks like (a foul), but the dynamic is he is not catching the ball,’ Maresca added.

‘Even the keeper does not believe that he was. Yes, there are fouls for Erling, but I can see also in the last games from the international break things that I don’t like, that for me are clear. But the referee is there, they decide, so we need to adapt.’

Haaland has talked up his enthusiasm for going up against Gabriel this week and should be reinvigorated for the challenge after cutting a forlorn figure during and after the 2-2 draw with Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday.

The 26-year-old appeared downbeat during media interviews immediately after the game, sparking a discussion over his current frame of mind.

Maresca insisted that the striker’s mood is in line with other players as they strive to break free of a disappointing set of performances.

‘Erling is a winner,’ the City manager said. ‘It's normal that he's not happy when we don't win games but it’s not just Erling, it's everyone. Don't forget that two weeks ago or three weeks ago he was dancing inside the pitch (after beating Brighton in the Carabao Cup).

Asked whether Haaland is treated unfairly by officials, the Italian said: ‘I can see that, to be honest. I can see also more things in the last four or five games'

‘You can write or think many different things, but the reality is sometimes much easier: Erling is upset, like I'm upset because we're not winning games. And when we were winning games everyone was happy. But this is our job, this is football, that's why we need to maintain the balance.’

Haaland has admitted that he needs to improve in front of goal after scoring just once in his last five club games, yet Maresca believes the problems instead lie in quality consistent service.

‘I think he is gesticulating in the same way when we were winning games and he was not receiving balls,’ he said. ‘Erling is a No 9, the No 9’s live day by day for goals.

‘When we drop the opposition inside the box and he is inside the box, he is the king there. The problem is that most of the teams now, because they are so aggressive, they come higher on the pitch, so you need him also to link a little bit. We need him in different ways.

‘I'm not a magician, there is a transition here. It's normal. We have eight, nine new players, manager is new - you need time. You see at different clubs when they had transitions, how complicated it is.’

Sports.title: Revealed: The numbers that show Man United are NOT too good to go down - they have the worst defence in Europe, are constantly outrun by opponents and are one of the most wasteful teams in the Premier League
Sports.content:
Manchester United are not too good to go down and absolutely are in a relegation battle. They aren’t good, let’s start there. Getting heavily beaten away to Liverpool was not at all surprising to Manchester United fans. If anything, many feared an even heavier scoreline. Not since 1973-74 have Manchester United been relegated and on that occasion that rag-tag group had won three of its first 11 matches. This time around, the side Mauricio Pochettino has inherited has just one win to its name. Former players and pundits believe that eventually, yes, United will get their act together and that relegation isn’t really something to be preoccupied with right now. Fools gold. Chief executive Omar Berrada claimed with a straight face that the club is heading in the right direction only last week. As staggering a statement last Friday as it was by the time the final whistle sounded on Sunday. By that point, it was insulting. Slumped in 19th and it will be 90 days since their last league win by the time they host Brentford at Old Trafford in a bid to stop the rot on Saturday, United’s problems are threatening to engulf Pochettino and his staff - even though they showed positive signs in the battling draw in Lisbon on Wednesday. Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the stats that condemn this sorry United squad and why burying their heads in the hand at talk of a relegation battle is the last thing they can afford to do… Manchester United are not too good to go down and absolutely are in a relegation battle

Your browser does not support iframes.

EUROPE’S WORST DEFENCE Trust Manchester United to be top of the table for the very worst statistic, officially having the worst defence in Europe’s top five leagues. Luis Suarez's late goal for Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday made it 36 goals conceded in total by United across all competitions, taking them ahead of Lens (35), Crystal Palace (34), Getafe (34) and Union Berlin (33). That’s a Lens side that conceded nine in one match in the Champions League. That’s an Union Berlin side who has conceded five or more goals three times already this campaign, including a 7-0 drubbing at the hands of Bayern Munich. Individually and collectively United lack any sort of structure, any sort of desire to do the basics, any sort of solidity that will have opposition forwards thinking twice. Open it up to the top four leagues in England and United are one of only two teams yet to manage a single league clean sheet this season, with fellow Premier League outfit Ipswich Town. League Two side Barnet was on that list until they kept their first clean sheet of the season against Crawley on Tuesday. Specifically in the Premier League, United rank 19th for Big Chances Against (22.2), rank 19th for Expected Goals Against (xGA). They have the sixth-worst Expected Goals differential in the league. The Red Devils have the worst defence in Europe’s top five leagues, conceding 36 goals so far

Your browser does not support iframes.

Matthijs de Ligt looked all at sea in his first league start in 357 days away to Liverpool to the point whereby Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher said they ‘felt sorry’ for him. Leny Yoro continues to make costly mistakes. Diogo Dalot no longer looks up to the level. Noussair Mazraoui has regressed massively. Patrick Dorgu looks uncomfortable defending. Harry Maguire lacks recovery pace to go toe-to-toe with top defenders. Ayden Heaven is raw. Lisandro Martinez is a shadow of the best version previously seen at United. And Luke Shaw is injured. It a defence that is majorly short on quality, discipline and leadership and that’s underscored by the amount of times they concede in bunches. United shipped two goals in eight minutes away to Como and conceded two in five minutes a few days later against Bournemouth. Twice in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa they conceded in bunches with two first half goals in three minutes, followed up by two Villa goals in five minutes in the second. Add in the two goals in six minutes at home against Roma – a game where the attack bailed out the defence in a 3-2 win – and the two goals shipped at Anfield in three minutes against Liverpool, this United rearguard is not fit for purpose. Put these defenders in a neutral kit and unanimously they’d be seen as relegation candidates. Mauricio Pochettino must sort out Manchester United's leaky defence as a top priority

Your browser does not support iframes.

SET-PIECE DISASTER That’s what set pieces are to United, a complete disaster. Poor sides in the Premier League often must hang their hats on scoring timely goals and grinding out vital wins through the means of set-pieces. United do not look capable of doing that. In the Premier League, they are joint-20th for set-piece goals conceded so far this season with seven, while they rank 19th for set-piece goals scored (1). Only Nottingham Forest (0) are performing worse in this area than United. Set-piece xG places United 19th in the league with 2.6, only marginally ahead of Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich Town, who are 20th with a set-piece xG of 1.6. Hull City boss Sergej Jakirovic hinted after the opening weekend’s 2-0 win over United that the Red Devils are easy to prepare for when it comes to set pieces, the area which created both goals. Last season United ranked second, only behind champions Arsenal, for set-piece goals scored and 11th for set-piece goals conceded. Pochettino took issue with Chelsea’s hierarchy when they went over his head to appoint a dedicated set-piece coach and there is no suggestion one such guru is heading United’s way. But make no bones about it, United have regressed massively in this area and it’s a slide without an easy fix. Luis Suarez capitalises on Senne Lammens' error to equalise for Sporting Lisbon late on NOT UP TO SPEED One of the biggest concerns right now is the ease at which teams are cutting United open. Bournemouth are a very good team but their win at Old Trafford looked like a training game at times. Against Villa, John McGinn strolled through the game, even if they went on to draw 4-4. There are too many examples of this. At 111.5km on average per game, United rank 19th in the league for distance covered per match, with only Sunday’s victors Liverpool clocking in further ground coverage. Worse than that, United badly lack pace and athleticism in the middle of the park as well as in wide areas. Where Liverpool fans marvel at the likes of Rio Ngumoha and Bradley Barcola, United have built a squad severely lacking pace in all areas. Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha are better inside and lack blistering pace. Diogo Dalot and Luke Shaw have both been exposed defensively for pace this season. Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans are technically very good operators but both lack athleticism and are therefore losing the midfield battle too often. Pochettino’s predecessor Michael Carrick scoffed at the fixation on running stats before he was sacked and there is some merit to it not being the be-all-and-end-all – look at Liverpool. But only Aston Villa (10) have been outrun by opponents more through the opening 11 games than United (9) and that, factored in with a porous defence and a soft underbelly at set pieces has United out there like a lamb for slaughter a lot of the time. The appointment of Sam Wilson as first-team fitness coach, a move agreed long in advance of Pochettino’s hiring, from Arsenal will look to address the serious levels of underperformance in this area. But with so little time on the training pitch and free moments in the schedule to fix months of fitness regression, it’s a gargantuan task. Man United badly lack pace and athleticism in the middle of the park as well as in wide areas

Your browser does not support iframes.

BELIEF (AND TIME!) IN SHORT SUPPLY As Pochettino had his head in his hands at Anfield he’d have been forgiven for wondering just how he was actually going to stop this sinking ship from fully going under. He was back at Carrington at 6:30am on Monday morning staring at a schedule that promises 10 games in 39 days. Players were back in for recovery sessions on Monday and training on Tuesday ahead of flying to Lisbon to face Sporting on Wednesday. Despite picking up a first point under Pochettino, there were plenty of individual errors in the 2-2 draw, namely with Senne Lammens conceding a needless penalty and later gifting Sporting an equaliser after failing to gather the ball in the air. With recovery on Thursday, it means there is only time for a light Friday session pre-Brentford on Saturday, when it will have been 90 days since United’s last league win. For all of the reasons outlined above, United are like a boxer on the ropes that is just trying to hang in there for the remainder of the year as the blows keep raining down. There are problems aplenty in defence and athleticism is one of the biggest worries. But mentality and belief is what Pochettino and his staff need to inspire as soon as possible. With a busy schedule of games, Pochettino and his coaching team don't have time on their side United are the only team in the Premier League not to win a single game across the last seven, while they are one of only two teams in the 92 in the Football League to have just one domestic win this season, along with Burnley. Having fallen behind eight times in the league, United have gone on to win just once, beating Ipswich Town. That was the anomaly. From winning positions, they rank 19th for points won, taking just six points from the four games in which they held the lead. And, ultimately, what are United’s players and fans clinging to? They rank 17th for home form and 19th away from home, where they have scored just four goals, while they are 18th in the league for shot conversion (5%) having taken the most shots (280) in the league. Only Sunderland and Nottingham Forest are more wasteful. United still have to travel to Newcastle United and Arsenal before the year is out, both daunting trips for sides low on confidence, while Champions League hopes hang in the balance against Sporting and RB Leipzig. Pochettino has a list as long as his arm with what he needs to fix but he has to get players believing again. It’s November and things are bad now, but they cannot throw in the towel when the going gets tough. ‘MODEST’ JANUARY AWAITS At this stage, indications are that the budget to be afforded to Pochettino in January will be ‘modest’ and is not set to be the splurge United likely need it to be. Calvin Bassey and Nathan Collins are on a list of targets, while Jarrad Branthwaite has been admired for a long time, albeit would be a player who would prove very expensive to get out of Everton mid-season. United need to add at least two high-quality defenders in January, if not three, to give them a chance of salvaging a season that is threatening to get away from them. The likes of Maguire, De Ligt, Dalot and Mazraoui are not suddenly going to improve and while there is a belief among former players that they won’t go down and it’s not a conversation to be had, those upstairs, who have failed miserably to date, cannot afford to show the same level of flippancy in what is set to be the most critical transfer window in decades for United. Get it wrong and they could run out of road come May. Indications are that the budget to be afforded to Pochettino by Sir Jim Ratcliffe (left) and Omar Berrada (right) in January will be ‘modest’, despite Manchester United needing reinforcements

Your browser does not support iframes.

HISTORY TELLS A STORY It raised alarm last Sunday night when it was pointed out that Tottenham Hotspur, who finished 17th and survived by the skin of their teeth last season, had 18 points after 11 games last season, 10 points more than United currently have. In fact, since 2019-20, 20 different teams have had eight or fewer points after 11 Premier League games and 14 have gone down. Two seasons ago both Crystal Palace and Wolverhampton Wanderers sat with fewer points than United after 11 games and both survived comfortably. But the general trend is those there now will be there when all is said and done.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland 'absolutely certain' to leave Man City as Enzo Maresca admits he's 'upset'
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland 'absolutely certain' to leave Man City as Enzo Maresca admits he's 'upset'

Gary Neville reckons Manchester City striker Erling Haaland will be at Real Madrid within 18 months

View 2 Images Erling Haaland had a goal ruled out against Fulham (Image: Getty Images)

Erling Haaland is "absolutely certain" to leave Manchester City within the next 18 months.

That's according to Gary Neville, who reckons there is a cloud hanging over Man City after they were found guilty on 114 of the 115 charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.

City deny the charges and have appealed, but results have started to go against the eight-time Premier League winners, with Haaland hitting out at the uncharacteristic performances.

He admitted that something isn't "clicking fully" following their 2-2 draw with Napoli in the Champions League, though his boss, Enzo Maresca, has no concerns about his unhappy demeanour, despite confirming the striker is currently "upset".

Mikel Arteta shows true colours with response to Man City charges question READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta shares cryptic David Raya injury update ahead of Man City clash READ MORE :

Speaking on The Overlap, Neville said: "It feels like something has changed in these last few weeks with City; it feels like maybe that mood, that cloud, is just starting to [impact].

"I don't think Haaland is going to be here. I think he will be at Real Madrid in the next, maximum 18 months, maybe even at the end of the season. I can see Vinicius leaving; I can see [Kylian] Mbappe going a bit to the left and Haaland going up there [down the middle].

"If you look at Florentino Perez, he goes and signs the best strikers in the world, the best players in the world. I just think because of what has happened to City, I think Haaland is going to Real Madrid. I am absolutely certain he will be in a Real Madrid shirt in the next 18 months."

View 2 Images Gary Neville can see Erling Haaland leaving Manchester City (Image: (Photo by James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images))

Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

Prior to the draw with Napoli, Man City dropped points at home to Fulham in the league and were soundly beaten 3-1 by Nottingham Forest before the international break.

In fact, City's last Premier League win came as far back as October 17 against Ipswich. Maresca is confident that Haaland is simply downbeat about the Citizens' poor run of form and made no mention of the Norwegian looking for a way out.

"Erling is a winner player," Maresca said. "It's normal that he's not happy when he's not winning games, but don't forget a few weeks ago he was dancing inside the pitch. Erling is upset just like I am upset. It's not a sprint, it's a marathon. We are building something for the future.

"I think he is gesticulating in the same way when we were winning games, and he was not receiving balls. Erling is a (number) nine, and the nines live day by day for goals and winning games. If they don't score or win games, they are upset. I don't think that affects his game. I don't see any problem at all with Erling."

Sports.title: Leny Yoro red appeal is very dangerous - we now have THREE layers of refereeing on top of VAR
Sports.content:
Leny Yoro red appeal is very dangerous - we now have THREE layers of refereeing on top of VAR

Will we start seeing more VAR decisions appealed by clubs in the neverending litigation of subjective decisions? It's an utter farce

View 3 Images

A very dangerous thing happened in football this week. No-one should underestimate the ramifications.

‌



The row over Manchester United defender Leny Yoro’s red card has opened up a very messy can of worms.

‌



And it is no wonder the suspension being overturned has caused shockwaves throughout the game because this is pretty unprecedented territory here.

‌



Don't miss John Cross' exclusive newsletter every Friday - just for Mirror+ subscribers - CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP

Let’s go back to the start.

Manchester United were successful in their appeal against Yoro’s sending-off for a foul on Alexander Isak at Liverpool last weekend.

At the time, referee Sam Barrott sent off Yoro because he deemed that Isak could have got to the ball and therefore was denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

‌



The Video Assistant Referee team, led by John Brooks, did not overrule that decision because they clearly felt it was not an obvious error.

That decision was effectively made on the pitch - and ratified by VAR.

‌



What happened next was United appealed to the FA and a three-man panel - Stuart Ripley, Mick Kearns and Tony Agana - believed otherwise and they overturned the suspension.

View 3 Images Leny Yoro saw red against Liverpool after being adjudged to have denied a goalscoring opportunity

‌



But what it has done is introduce a THIRD layer of decision makers because all this is just opinion.

United sent a letter, including data based on AI technology, that even at top speed Isak would have ended up being 1.8 metres short of getting to the ball.

‌



That does not allow for variables like United keeper Senne Lammens retreating and going back in his goal. Did you see his shaky performance at Sporting Lisbon?

The Key Match Incidents panel - which reviews big decisions from Premier League games - ruled 5-0 in favour of Barrott making the right decision.

‌



Again, it is just opinion.

United submitted a letter with that information and data and said the technology could prove “within minutes” that Isak was not getting to the ball so therefore Yoro should not have been sent off.

‌



How will Mauricio Pochettino handle the Man Utd Media Mafia and the relentless content machine? READ MORE :

What is the biggest complaint about VAR? The delays. Should we have just twiddled our thumbs at Anfield until that 'data' could be sought - and from where?

The referee and VAR are going by what is in front of them. Anything else introduced into the conversation afterwards was unavailable to the officials in the moment - and should not be admissible. It really is that simple.

‌



The FA panel has crossed a line and introduced a third layer of decision makers - and it is wrong.

We used to get weekly appeals about decisions. Now they are rare by comparison. Why? Because of VAR. It’s dealt with at the time.

‌



United said in their letter they had data which showed it was not a subjective decision. Sorry, but it was the very essence of a subjective decision. It was the referee’s view at the time which was backed up by VAR.

View 3 Images Sam Barrott's decision was overturn (Image: Martin Rickett/Press Association)

‌



This has opened the floodgates for every club and every manager to appeal every decision - and hope that someone on the FA panel has a different opinion.

The Yoro case has completely undermined referees, the whole process and has opened the door to games being re-refereed.

‌



Will referees make mistakes? Of course. Let’s be clear. Howard Webb, the chief refereeing officer of Pro Ref, has already issued an apology to United this season because the officials allowed Erling Haaland’s winning goal to stand in the Manchester derby when it was clearly offside.

There can be no argument there. It was not subjective. It was just plain wrong. An apology was issued. Rightly so.

‌



Howard Webb shuts down Arsenal v Liverpool penalty debate after Andoni Iraola complaint READ MORE :

Alejandro Garnacho's Aston Villa snub is latest step in slow demise as managers all agree READ MORE :

Yes, the Key Match Incidents Panel ruled there were six on-field errors in match round ten which is the joint highest it has recorded in one weekend. Clearly, Pro Ref knows that is not good enough.

But this time, the FA is at odds with Webb, Barrott and Brooks in saying that the Yoro red card was wrong. Fast forward two or three years and those three could be on a panel and rule the red card was correct.

‌



Honestly, it’s just all about opinion. Being a ref and operating as a VAR is hard enough without being completely undermined by this utter farce.

So much of decision making has to be down to opinion. That’s the point and beauty about football - everyone has an opinion.

‌



Trying to dress up opinion as fact is just a nonsense and now let’s see every club in the country start appealing every decision. And undermining a referee’s opinion is just plain ridiculous.

We used to have weekly appeals before VAR. Video technology did away with most of that. It was refreshing to have more definitive decisions.

Article continues below

This is a dangerous and unprecedented path and means we now have three layers of referees. The ref on the pitch, VAR and the FA panel if we don’t like it. The floodgates have been opened.

Sports.title: Value Scope: Each way horseracing tips from Steve Jones for Saturday on ITV
Sports.content:
Value Scope: Each way horseracing tips from Steve Jones for Saturday on ITV

Our ace gets stuck into the main race of the day, the Coral Gold Cup at Newbury, and has three other selections from a quality ITV racecard

View 2 Images Steve Jones with his picks for Saturday

Tune into THE JUKEBOX KID (3.00) in the Coral Gold Cup. Ben Pauling is carving out an impressive record in jump racing’s bigger prizes and his runner looks well suited to the demands of this prestigious Newbury handicap.

‌



‌



This lightly-raced seven-year-old took well to fences last season. His defeat of useful Montregard at Ascot in January was a particularly good effort and he returned to the Royal track to easily land the Grade 2 Reynoldstown Novices’ Chase the following month. The Irish Grand National proved a step too far but it’s not hard to excuse that disappointing performance.

‌



Although his return to action was also underwhelming, it came over hurdles and he was caught wide when ridden more patiently than usual.

‌



That run should have put the edge on him. Have 1pt each-way at 25-1. Most bookies are paying out on five places.

Consistent ROYAL JEWEL (1.10) should find the 2m6f trip ideal in the Coral Sir Peter O’Sullevan Memorial Chase. He won first time out last year and he went on to run some sound races later in the season.

‌



Most of those efforts – including a win at Taunton in February – came in small fields and he looks the type to do even better in today’s more competitive contest. He’s done his winning on softer ground but today’s quicker conditions suit him just as well. Have 1pt each-way at 25-1. Most firms are offering five places.

View 2 Images The Jukebox Kid: Value Scope's selection (Image: Alan Crowhurst/Getty Images)

‌



CALIFET EN VOL (1.40) lost his way over fences but he is dangerously handicapped if he enjoys the return to hurdling. He was a smart novice hurdler a couple of years ago. His only two defeats in four starts came when runner-up behind The New Lion at this meeting and when sixth in the Grade 1 Sefton Hurdle at Aintree’s Grand National meeting.

He didn’t run badly on his first run of the season, considering his jumping of Ascot’s fences was a bit deliberate and he was caught wide for much of the way. With Nicky Henderson starting to hit form, he is worth supporting. Have 1pt each-way at 16-1. Most bookies go five places.

Article continues below

A fast-run 2m is what WRECKLESS ERIC (3.38) wants and that’s what he gets in the final race. He made an excellent debut over fences against experienced chasers at Ffos Las and he should be spot on for this. Have 1pt each-way at 12-1. Most firms offer four places.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua challenges Tyson Fury to punch machine showdown
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua challenges Tyson Fury to punch machine showdown

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury will fight in two weeks' time but key details of the clash have not been ironed out

View Image Anthony Joshua will take on Tyson Fury (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Anthony Joshua wants to challenge Tyson Fury on an punch machine to determine who walks to the ring first.

‌



‌



Joshua and Fury will clash in Cardiff on December 11 but the order of the ring walks has not been decided. The first bell will ring at around 1.30am, meaning whoever walks first could be left waiting in the cold. And promoter Eddie Hearn said: "AJ's request, and Netflix loved the idea as well, was that the person who scored the highest on the punch machine would walk second.

‌



"AJ felt, and Netflix felt, that would be a great bit of TV, so we told [fight organisers Sela], 'This is what we'd like to do.' They went away and said they loved it and they signed the contract that the ring walk will be determined in that fashion. So we are expecting to punch the punch machine on fight week to see who will walk second. But we have been told that Tyson Fury is not willing to take part in that, so, I guess the alternative for that is probably a coin toss."

‌



Tyson Fury cleared to fight Anthony Joshua after schizophrenia claim READ MORE :

Meanwhile, Fury has been cleared to fight Joshua next month despite concerns about his mental health. The British Boxing Board of Control (BBBoC) indicated earlier this week that it would investigate comments from Fury’s wife Paris that the boxer had been diagnosed with schizophrenia, and had the powers to deny him a licence to fight.

However, Paris Fury retracted her claim in a statement issued on Thursday night, and the BBBoC’s general secretary Robert Smith told Sky Sports: “Fury cleared last night. All up to date medicals cleared. Promoter told this morning.”

Paris Fury said in an initial version of a Netflix documentary due for release today that Fury was diagnosed with schizophrenia just months after beating Wladimir Klitschko to win the world heavyweight title in Dusseldorf in November 2015.

‌



She said in Thursday’s statement: “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary. I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis.

“Mental health is complex, and it isn’t always easy to find the right words, especially when you’re living it with someone you love. I’m so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we’ve received as a family.”

‌



Netflix indicated it had edited the footage as a result, saying in a statement: “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.”

‌



Fury has been open about his mental health struggles since beating Klitschko, after which he took a near three-year hiatus from boxing, with his weight ballooning to 27 stone, while he battled suicidal thoughts and alcohol addiction.

Fury admitted hearing “voices in my mind” following his win, adding: “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in.

Article continues below

“I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100 per cent thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.”

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola shares triple Liverpool injury update as he sweats on stars for Everton clash
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola shares triple Liverpool injury update as he sweats on stars for Everton clash

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has officially ruled one key player out of Sunday's Merseyside derby - but the door has been left ajar for two other stars who have been struggling

View 2 Images Cody Gakpo has been ruled out of the Merseyside derby (Image: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola says Liverpool's Victor Munoz is hoping to return to training on Saturday and hasn't ruled out the winger featuring against Everton in the Merseyside derby.

Munoz was substituted during the opening period of Wednesday's 3-0 victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League following a knee injury, with a stretcher initially prepared for the Spaniard in Belgium.

Nevertheless, Munoz managed to leave the pitch on foot with assistance from medical staff, and early concerns about a serious knee problem were dismissed by his manager.

Speaking ahead of Sunday's Merseyside derby at his press conference, Iraola revealed Munoz could be available for the match at Hill Dickinson Stadium, though Cody Gakpo remains sidelined.

Sports.content:
Man Utd trigger new Bruno Fernandes contract extension - but he could still leave this summer

Manchester United have used a club option to extend Bruno Fernandes' contract for a further year to avoid losing their influential captain for nothing in the summer

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes of Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have triggered an option in Bruno Fernandes' contract to extend the playmaker's terms by a further 12 months, it has emerged.

‌



‌



Fernandes, 32, was due to become a free agent at the end of this season, though United's actions mean that will now no longer be the case.

‌



But the Portugal international could theoretically still quit Old Trafford this summer after recently revealing he had put contract talks on ice following the latest managerial change at the club, with United currently in the relegation zone after a poor start to the season.

‌



Manchester Evening News have confirmed that United triggered their option to keep Fernandes on their books beyond this season and into 2028.

Should talks over a new contract fail to yield an agreement when they resume then it remains a possibility that Fernandes could still be sold in the summer transfer window, particularly if United receive substantial offers for their talisman.

It's understood Fernandes remains a player with plenty of admirers both within Europe and further afield. He was courted heavily by clubs from Saudi Arabia last summer and interest from the Middle East has not waned.

‌



Fernandes confirmed last week that he had been offered a new contract by United. "No, there's no negotiations ongoing," he told Sky Sports. "But I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years.

Sports.title: Basher Watts rebuked by racecourse body over ‘unauthorised badge resale’
Sports.content:
Basher Watts rebuked by racecourse body over ‘unauthorised badge resale’

The social media influencer, who runs his own racehorse syndicates, was told he would be breaching terms and conditions if he gave away four tickets to Huntingdon

View 2 Images Basher Watts: offered spare tickets for the races (Image: YouTube)

Social media influencer Basher Watts has been rebuked by Britain’s racecourse body after offering free spare tickets to a race meeting.

‌



‌



Watts runs his own racehorse syndicate and regularly films his experiences in the sport through his social media platforms. The operation, which has a team of 19 racehorses, was named ROA Small Syndicate of the Year for 2025.

‌



On Monday at Huntingdon, My Mate AJ was due to run for the syndicate in a maiden hurdle. Watts posted on X, “I’ve had 4 owners unfortunately not able to make it to Huntingdon today, I’d hate for them to go to waste. Just comment if you’d like them!”

‌



Police recover part of 2003 Melbourne Cup stolen in robbery and 2kg of melted gold READ MORE :

On Wednesday he received an email from the Racecourse Association under the headline, ‘Re: Unauthorised Badge Resale’.

The letter, which Watts shared on X, said: “Owners and trainers and associated benefits such as restaurant tables, may only be used by the named owner/trainer for whom it was intended, and their invited guests.

“No badges, tickets or other benefits may be sold, given away or otherwise transferred unless any such sale or transfer has been approved in advance by the relevant racecourse.”

‌



View 2 Images Basher Watts with Shes Perfect

The correspondences added the practice would breach terms and conditions and tickets offered in this way would be voided.

‌



It added: “These badges are made available by racecourses to owners with runners, for use by them and their genuine guests and should not be reoffered to third parties either by the owner, or the trainer on their behalf.”

An unhappy Watts responded: “Welcome to horse racing. A sport on its knees and should be doing all it can to try and get new owners onboard and also keeping owners who support the game as happy as possible.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

“I had 4 owners cancel on Monday at Huntingdon so I wanted to offer out the experience of being an owner to people who might’ve never experienced it. I think there is nothing which looks more sad than an empty parade ring or horses going back to the winners enclosure to no owners.

Article continues below

“That tweet reached over 20,000 people who might’ve taken up my offer and experienced ownership and decided to get involved and support horse racing in whatever capacity. Surely this should be encouraged not a governing body of the sport trying to punish you for it.

“This is the email I receive from the Racecourse association. The mind boggles.”
