"The idea comes from the belief that consent for sex is implied in marriage, that marriage is a threshold where consent ends," Silwal told the BBC.

"But it shows a lack of awareness, it shows we are still treating women as property, that we are still very patriarchal."

The report comes amid renewed debate over marital rape across the region.

In India, 10 petitions challenging the law are pending before the Supreme Court, which is due to begin final hearings on 9 December.

Courts have delivered contradictory rulings over the years, with some judges acknowledging the law's archaic nature and urging parliament to criminalise marital rape.

There was outrage last year when a court let go a man whose wife had died after he brutally raped her.

But the Indian government, religious organisations and men's rights activists have opposed petitions in the top court, saying criminalisation of marital rape would be "excessively harsh".

Rights groups in Bangladesh have also challenged the marital rape exception, arguing it violates constitutional rights to life, liberty and protection from torture and cruel treatment, the report says.

"Those who oppose criminalising marital rape say it would undermine the family unit and break them apart. And family is very important in our countries," Silwal says.

"They say it will affect our religious and cultural values and worry that there would be false accusations against men."

Also a change in law, she says, may not necessarily mean justice for survivors.

Silwal points to Bhutan where marital rape is a criminal offence but it's treated as a petty misdemeanour and is punishable by one month to one year.

In Nepal, the punishment for rape is between six and 20 years, but it's only up to five years for a husband who rapes his wife.

World.title: Four PREMIUM TIMES journalists emerge finalists for 2026 Wole Soyinka Investigative Reporting Award
World.content:
Four journalists from PREMIUM TIMES have emerged as finalists for the 2026 Wole Soyinka Award for Investigative Reporting, alongside nine others from media organisations across Nigeria.

The four PREMIUM TIMES journalists are Folashade Ogunrinde, Oladeinde Olawoyin, Qosim Suleiman and Ekemini Simon.

The Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism (WSCIJ), in a statement signed by its Executive Director, Motunrayo Alaka, on Friday, said the 13 journalists were selected from 238 entries submitted for the 21st edition of the award.

Other finalists are Dayo Oyewo of The Punch, Omolabake Fasogbon of ThisDay, Juliet Buna of Crest 91.1FM, Gift Ufuoma of BBC News, Chukwuemeka Emenike of New Telegraph, Atsahyel Aaron of Trust TV, Olayide Soaga of The Guardian, Francis Esenwa of News Central, and Patience Yerima of Production House.

According to the statement, the finalists were selected by the 2026 WSAIR Judges’ Board, chaired by Dayo Aiyetan, Executive Director of the International Centre for Investigative Reporting.

The statement did not provide details of the stories submitted by the finalists and the categories they were shortlisted for.

Lifetime achievement awards

The 2026 edition will also honour veteran journalists Ray Ekpu and Taiwo Obe with the Lifetime Award for Journalistic Excellence.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The WSCIJ said Mr Ekpu was being recognised for his pioneering contributions to investigative journalism in Nigeria, particularly his role in co-founding Newswatch magazine and his editorial leadership across major media organisations.

Mr Obe will receive the award for his contributions to editorial excellence, professional journalism practice and the development of successive generations of journalists.

Also, Yemi Adamolekun, founder of Enough is Enough (EiE), will receive the Human Rights Defender Award.

The centre said Ms Adamolekun was being recognised for her work in strengthening democratic accountability, promoting active citizenship and civic participation, and championing citizens’ rights and responsibilities in Nigeria.

“The Lifetime Award for Journalistic Excellence recognises individuals whose professional contributions have significantly shaped journalism and its practice over time,” the statement said.

Award ceremony

The finalists and honorary recipients will be honoured at a ceremony on 9 December at the NECA Event Centre, Alausa, Ikeja, Lagos.

The ceremony, scheduled for 6 p.m. to 8 p.m., will be part of the 2026 Amplify In-Depth Media Conference and Awards (AIMCA), which will hold from 8 to 10 December at the same venue. The red carpet begins at 5 p.m.

ALSO READ: PREMIUM TIMES journalists win at 35th DAME Awards

The conference, themed ‘Truth. Power. Rights. Journalism at the Heart of Democracy,’ will bring together journalists, media leaders, policymakers, development partners and other stakeholders to discuss journalism, accountability and democracy.

About the award

Established in 2005, the Wole Soyinka Award for Investigative Reporting recognises outstanding journalism across print, radio, television, photography, online media and editorial cartoons.

Over the years, the award has introduced specialised categories covering areas such as local government, climate change, Report Women and sports.

“In recognition of the connection between investigative journalism, anti-corruption efforts and human rights, the WSAIR presentation ceremony has been held annually on 9 December, International Anti-Corruption Day, on the eve of International Human Rights Day, since 2009. This tradition underscores the important role of investigative journalism in exposing corruption, defending rights and advancing democratic accountability,” the statement added.

World.title: Presidency hails Rarara’s new Tinubu campaign song, says APC has ‘support’ across north
World.content:
The Presidency has applauded a new campaign song by popular Hausa political singer, Dauda Kahutu, popularly known as Rarara, in support of President Bola Tinubu, describing it as another musical endorsement of the president from Northern Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Bayo Onanuga, Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, described the song as “another banger from Northern Nigeria for President Tinubu” in a post on his verified X @aonanuga1956 account on Friday.

Mr Onanuga also expressed confidence in the All Progressives Congress (APC)’s growing campaign activities, dismissing earlier suggestions that the ruling party would struggle to mobilise support in Northern Nigeria.

“Remember the pre-electioneering propaganda that said the APC couldn’t campaign up north, erect billboards, or wear APC or Asiwaju symbols. The APC’s intense campaign has put them all to shame, not only in the North but nationwide,” he wrote.

He further predicted that Mr Tinubu will win the January 16, 2027 presidential election by a “very comfortable margin”.

The presidential spokesperson also shared a video posted by an X user, [@Ayofe], showing a female supporter enthusiastically singing along to the new track while driving in her car.

The video offered a glimpse into how campaign music is being circulated and embraced by supporters through social media platforms as political activities gather momentum ahead of the elections.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Rarara’s growing influence in political campaigns

Rarara has become one of the most recognisable voices in Northern Nigeria’s political music scene, particularly through his campaign songs for the APC and its prominent political figures.

The Kano-based musician rose to national prominence through his politically themed Hausa songs, which played significant roles in mobilising support for former President Muhammadu Buhari during the 2015 and 2019 elections.

His musical influence has continued under the Tinubu administration, with several songs dedicated to the president, including the popular Omo Ologo, a Yoruba expression meaning a glorious or fortunate child.

His political music has, however, not been without controversy, particularly when his lyrics target opposition politicians and other public figures.

Mixed reactions trail new song

Onanuga’s post had attracted about 186,000 views and 420 comments as of the time of reporting, with supporters and critics expressing contrasting opinions about Rarara’s latest release and the APC’s campaign.

While Àdùnní TMO (@adunni_tmo) praised the enthusiasm of Northern supporters of Mr Tinubu, saying their passion for the president was unmatched across the country, other users were less impressed.

Jamilu Bin Salih (@jamilubinsalih) argued that Rarara’s songs no longer enjoyed the popularity they once commanded in the North, predicting that the APC would face electoral difficulties in 2027.

Another commenter, Muofunanya Chizoba (@CMuofunanya), used the opportunity to remind Nigerians of campaign promises Mr Tinubu reportedly made to people in the North-east during an APC campaign rally in Jos in November 2022.

The reactions reflect differing perceptions of Rarara’s influence, the APC’s popularity in Northern Nigeria and the performance of the Tinubu administration ahead of the 2027 elections.

Election ahead

The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for 16 January, 2027, according to the revised timetable of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

The APC’s campaign strategy has increasingly incorporated music and entertainment as tools for communicating political messages, building campaign identity and sustaining enthusiasm among supporters.

Rarara’s latest song adds to the growing collection of musical releases supporting Mr Tinubu as the 2027 presidential contest approaches.

World.title: Court reserves judgement in N3.1bn fraud case against Suswam
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja has reserved judgement in the alleged N3.1 billion money laundering case involving former Benue State Governor Gabriel Suswam and a former Commissioner for Finance in the state, Omodachi Okolobia.

The trial judge, Peter Lifu, announced on Friday that the date for judgement would be communicated to the parties after their lawyers adopted their final written addresses.

Mr Suswam and Mr Okolobia, through their respective lawyers, urged the court to acquit them, while the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) asked the judge to find that the prosecution had proved its case against them.

Mr Suswam’s lawyer, Chinelo Ogbozor, told the court that the defence filed its final written address in December 2025. She added that the defence submitted a reply on points of law in April after receiving the commission’s final address.

Adopting the submissions, Ms Ogbozor urged the court to discharge and acquit Mr Suswam on counts one to seven of the 11-count amended charge, which contain allegations against the former governor.

The counts centre on the alleged misappropriation of N3.1 billion, said to have come from the sale of shares owned by the Benue State Government through the Benue Investment and Property Company Limited.

Mr Okolobia’s lawyer, Paul Erokoro, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), also asked the court to acquit his client. He said the defence filed its final written address in January and later submitted a reply on points of law in June, following receipt of the prosecution’s address.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“I adopt these two processes as our final address in urging your lordship to discharge and acquit the second defendant of all the counts in the amended charge,” Mr Erokoro told the court.

He argued that the prosecution had failed to prove the allegations against Mr Okolobia in counts eight to 11, which concern the former commissioner alone.

The commission’s lawyer, Rotimi Jacobs, SAN, urged the judge to uphold the prosecution’s case. He adopted the commission’s final written address, filed in March.

Mr Jacobs described the case as “a straightforward case” and outlined the prosecution’s allegations that the defendants diverted funds belonging to Benue State.

The 11-year corruption trial

Mr Suswam is a lawyer and politician who represented Katsina-Ala/Ukum/Logo Federal Constituency of Benue State in the House of Representatives between 1999 and 2007. He was elected governor in 2007 and served two terms until 2015. He later represented Benue North-East Senatorial District in the Senate from 2019 to 2023.

The allegations in the case relate to transactions carried out during his second term as governor. The EFCC accused him and his then Commissioner for Finance, Mr Okolobia, of diverting N3.1 billion from proceeds of the sale of shares owned by the state government.

The shares were held through the Benue Investment and Property Company Limited (BIPC). According to the prosecution, part of the proceeds from their sale through Elixir Securities Limited and Elixir Investment Partners Limited was diverted between August and October 2014.

Abubakar Umar, a bureau de change operator who operated Fanffash Resources Limited, testified that he converted the money into $15.8 million and delivered the dollars to Mr Suswam. His account of where he delivered the money changed during the trial.

The commission also accused Mr Okolobia of conducting transactions totalling N578 million in four tranches between December 2014 and January 2015, in breach of the cash transaction limit under the money laundering law. Both defendants denied the allegations.

The commission first arraigned the duo before the Federal High Court in November 2015. They pleaded not guilty to the charges, which were later amended to 11 counts. The case passed through three judges before it was reassigned to Mr Lifu in 2023. The defendants were re-arraigned before him in March 2024 and again pleaded not guilty.

During the trial, Junaidu Sa’id, an EFCC investigator, testified about the investigation and the alleged transfer of the money. Brigid Shiedu, then managing director of BIPC, gave evidence about the sale of the shares and the governor’s authorisation.

Mr Umar, the fourth prosecution witness, described how he converted the money into dollars. In January 2018, he told the court that his earlier evidence about delivering the money to Mr Suswam’s Maitama residence was wrong. He also alleged that people close to the former governor had pressured him to change his account.

The prosecution called nine witnesses and tendered documentary evidence before closing its case. One of the witnesses, Adewale Agunbiade, a compliance officer with Guaranty Trust Bank, testified about Mr Suswam’s naira and dollar accounts.

He told the court that more than $200,000 entered the dollar account in installments between August 2014 and July 2015, while Mr Suswam personally paid $175,000 in cash.

During cross-examination, however, Mr Agunbiade said the inflows were not unusual and that he had not noticed any breach of banking regulations. Appea Sunday, an EFCC investigator, also testified for the prosecution.

The defendants then asked the court to dismiss the charges without requiring them to present a defence, arguing that the prosecution had failed to establish a case against them. Their lawyers, Ms Ogbozor and Mr Erokoro, said the evidence was insufficient to sustain the charges, but the prosecution opposed the application, insisting that the evidence linked the defendants to the alleged offences.

In July 2025, Mr Lifu dismissed the application and directed the defendants to present their defence. He held that the prosecution had presented enough evidence to require them to respond to the allegations.

Mr Suswam subsequently testified as the sole defence witness, while Mr Okolobia did not testify or call any witness. They concluded their defence in November 2025, after which the judge directed the parties to file and exchange their final written addresses.

Although he gave the prosecution 14 days to file its address and allowed the defendants 14 days to respond after receiving it, the adoption took almost a year.

Series of adjournments over final addresses

The court initially fixed a day in January this year for the adoption of the addresses, but the proceedings were postponed several times. The matter was later moved to May and then to July before another adjournment to September.

At the July proceedings, the judge adjourned the case after the prosecution informed the court that Mr Suswam and his lawyer, Mr Erokoro, were indisposed.

The matter suffered another delay in October when Mr Suswam’s lead lawyer, Joseph Daudu, was absent. The prosecution told the court that Mr Daudu had written to say he would be travelling to Denmark for the International Bar Association’s annual conference.

The prosecution described that request as a deliberate attempt to frustrate the trial but agreed to the adjournment to avoid any question of denying the defence a fair hearing, while the judge subsequently adjourned the case to November.

The lawyers have now adopted their arguments, while Mr Lifu said the date would be communicated to the parties.

World.title: NUJ sets Nine December for annual blood donation in honour of late journalist
World.content:
The Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Council, has designated 9 December every year as blood donation day in Abuja in memory of late journalist Rafat Salami, seeking to sustain her commitment to voluntary blood donation.

The initiative, known as the Rafat Salami Voluntary Blood Donation Drive, aims to encourage journalists to donate blood regularly and raise public awareness of the need for voluntary donations to save lives.

The decision was reached on Thursday when a delegation of the NUJ FCT Council visited the National Blood Service Agency (NBSA), where both organisations agreed to work together to promote voluntary blood donation.

The Council’s delegation was led by Felix Ojo, who represented its Chairperson, Grace Ike.

Speaking during the visit, Mr Ojo said the initiative was a way of preserving the memory of Ms Salami through an act of service she championed during her lifetime.

“We are immortalising the legacy of donor champion, late Comrade Rafat Salami, who lived a life of sacrifice and responsibility,” he said.

He said the Council would mobilise journalists to participate in voluntary blood donation, raise awareness about its importance and advocate regular donations.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Ojo added that journalists should go beyond reporting public health campaigns and demonstrate their commitment by participating in activities that benefit society.

The Media Cell for Safe Blood, a platform established by the International Society of Media in Public Health in partnership with the NBSA, is also expected to support the initiative through advocacy and public awareness.

Receiving the delegation, the Director of Blood Services, Sani Abubakar, welcomed the initiative and described Ms Salami as a consistent blood donor and advocate.

“Rafat Salami was a consistent donor and advocate. It is sad we lost her,” he said. “It is a good thing that the NUJ wants to immortalise her by her legacy.”

Mr Abubakar said the agency was responsible for regulating and coordinating the provision of safe blood across the country and welcomed partnerships that could strengthen voluntary donation.

He said activities for National Blood Donation Day would begin on 8 December, with a week-long advocacy campaign to encourage more Nigerians to donate blood.

He also assured journalists that adequate blood bank facilities would be available for members participating in the exercise.

READ ALSO: Police arrest lab technician running illegal blood bank in hair salon

While the NBSA would provide technical and material support, Mr Abubakar urged the NUJ FCT Council to take ownership of the initiative’s sponsorship to encourage sustained commitment.

He said the agency would incorporate the Rafat Salami donation drive into its annual activities every December.

The annual exercise is expected to give journalists in Abuja an opportunity to honour Ms Salami through voluntary blood donation while highlighting the importance of maintaining a reliable supply of safe blood.

World.title: Adeleke sworn in for second term as Osun governor
World.content:
Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke has been sworn in for a second term, pledging to transform the state’s economy from one largely dependent on the civil service into an industrialised economy, while expressing confidence that President Bola Tinubu’s intervention would resolve the prolonged local government crisis within a week.

Mr Adeleke took the oath of office on Friday at the Osogbo Township Stadium, where the Chief Judge of the state, Adepele Ojo, administered the oath. His deputy, Kola Adewusi, had earlier been sworn in.

The inauguration marks the beginning of another four-year tenure for Mr Adeleke, who won the 15 August governorship election on the platform of the Accord Party.

He polled 511,067 votes to defeat his closest challenger, Bola Oyebamiji of the All Progressives Congress (APC), who secured 444,815 votes. The margin of victory was 66,252 votes.

In his inaugural address, Mr Adeleke described his re-election as a “triumph of the people’s will”, thanking residents for what he called their commitment to democracy.

Vice-President Kashim Shettima led the federal government’s delegation to the ceremony on behalf of President Tinubu.

Industrialisation, jobs top second-term agenda

Outlining his priorities for the next four years, Mr Adeleke said his administration would focus on citizens’ welfare, infrastructure expansion, industrialisation, agricultural transformation, the digital economy, tourism and youth and women’s development.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the government would prioritise completing ongoing projects while embarking on new ones, with the broader objective of creating jobs and expanding the state’s economy.

“My vision is to move Osun from a civil service economy to an industrialised one. We are open to partnership with private organisations and economic advisory groups,” he said.

The governor listed agro-processing factories, industrial parks across the state’s districts, free trade zones and tourism development among the projects his administration intends to pursue.

He also announced plans to establish a digital hub in each of Osun’s three senatorial districts to promote job creation and participation in the digital economy.

On electricity, Mr Adeleke said his administration would immediately establish the Osun State Electricity Regulatory Commission in line with the state’s power sector law, which he said he signed earlier this year.

He described a steady electricity supply as essential to economic growth.

The governor also promised to rehabilitate major waterworks across the state and find a lasting solution to the long-standing Ilesa water project.

LG crisis to be resolved in the next week

A major issue in the governor’s address was the prolonged dispute over the administration and funding of Osun’s local governments.

Mr Adeleke said President Tinubu had intervened in the dispute and expressed confidence that it would be resolved within a week.

“I am glad to announce that Mr President has intervened in the local government matter and in the next week, the crisis will be fully resolved,” he said.

The dispute, which has persisted since 2022, involves rival claims over the leadership of the state’s 30 local government councils and control of their statutory allocations.

The crisis followed disagreements over the legality of the October 2022 local government election, which produced APC chairpersons, and the February 2025 election conducted by the Adeleke administration, which produced PDP-backed council officials.

The federal government withheld allocations to the councils amid the dispute. In December 2025, the Supreme Court struck out a suit by the Osun State Government seeking the release of the funds, ruling that the state government lacked the legal standing to institute the action on behalf of the local councils. The court, however, faulted the seizure of the funds.

The dispute has affected the administration and financing of local government services, including primary healthcare and grassroots development.

Mr Adeleke said his administration had rehabilitated and equipped 232 of the state’s 332 primary healthcare centres with solar and power facilities during his first term. He blamed the withholding of local government allocations for preventing the completion of the remaining facilities.

He promised to complete the outstanding rehabilitation once the dispute was resolved.

The governor also pledged to upgrade general hospitals, recruit more health workers and expand the supply of drugs across the state.

READ ALSO: Adeleke presents 2027 budget to Osun Assembly

Education, infrastructure and reconciliation

In education, Mr Adeleke promised to recruit more teachers, accelerate the rehabilitation of schools, expand bursaries and scholarships, maintain affordable tuition and revive technical colleges.

He also pledged to tackle cultism in schools and strengthen opportunities for young people.

The governor called on political leaders and residents to put aside their differences and work towards the development of the state.

“Fellow citizens, we must heal the wounds of the past and unite for our collective good. I charge the Osun political class to embrace elite consensus, transparency, good governance and local content,” he said.

Before outlining his second-term priorities, Mr Adeleke observed a minute of silence in honour of victims of recent political violence in the state.

The ceremony attracted Vice-President Kashim Shettima, former Osun Governor Bisi Akande, former Senate President Bukola Saraki, serving and former political office holders, traditional rulers and other dignitaries.

Traditional rulers in attendance included the Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, and the Olubadan of Ibadan, Oba Rasidi Ladoja.

World.title: Nigeria must improve production to compete under AfCFTA – Finance Minister
World.content:
The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, said Nigeria must improve its production capacity and competitiveness to take advantage of opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

Mr Oyedele stressed that access to the continental market alone would not guarantee economic gains without the capacity to produce quality goods, fulfil orders and retain customers.

“Market access creates an opportunity. Our competitiveness will determine how much of it we convert into prosperity,” he said.

He made the remarks at a stakeholder forum organised by the Nigerian Export-Import Bank (NEXIM) in Abuja, themed “Leveraging the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) for Enhanced Nigerian Export Competitiveness and Economic Diversification”.

The minister explained that the government’s economic reforms, including the removal of the petrol subsidy, foreign exchange reforms, and changes to the tax and fiscal system, aim to move Nigeria away from dependence on a narrow range of commodities toward a diversified, production-driven economy.

According to him, expanding exports would generate foreign exchange and create jobs across sectors, including agriculture, manufacturing, transportation, and professional services.

He illustrated this with the example of an agricultural processor supplying products to a new market, which could create additional demand for farmers, while Nigerian technology and service businesses expanding abroad could open opportunities for young people.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Oyedele described AfCFTA as an important platform for Nigerian businesses to expand into markets across Africa, particularly in technology, manufacturing, agricultural processing, solid minerals, creative industries and services.

However, he emphasised that businesses needed more than market access to succeed, noting that their ability to meet buyers’ specifications, deliver products consistently and secure repeat orders would determine their competitiveness.

“The promise becomes real only when a Nigerian business secures a customer, fulfils an order, gets paid and wins a repeat order,” he said.

He argued that processing agricultural products into finished goods, rather than exporting raw commodities, could generate greater economic value and create more opportunities across the production chain.

The minister identified inadequate financing, infrastructure gaps, high transaction costs, delays in certification and transportation, and other trade barriers as challenges confronting Nigerian exporters.

He said the government was working to improve trade facilitation, streamline documentation and customs procedures, harmonise standards, and expand access to financing for viable export businesses.

Mr Oyedele urged financial institutions to structure export financing around businesses’ transaction cycles and expected foreign exchange earnings to prevent repayment obligations from creating unnecessary pressure on exporters.

He also called for stronger collaboration between NEXIM Bank and commercial financial institutions through guarantees, insurance, and other financing arrangements. At the same time, businesses should receive support to meet export standards, maintain proper records, and access market information.

The minister maintained that AfCFTA should also benefit smaller businesses that supply goods and services to larger exporters, noting that producers within export supply chains contribute to the country’s export economy even when they do not sell directly to foreign buyers.

He urged participants at the forum to identify specific challenges facing exporters, the institutions responsible for addressing them and practical solutions that could be implemented.

READ ALSO: Senate confirms Taiwo Oyedele as minister

Mr Oyedele called for collaboration among the government, financial institutions, businesses and development partners to improve production, remove trade barriers and strengthen Nigeria’s competitiveness in African markets.

The AfCFTA, which commenced trading on 1 January 2021, seeks to create a single continental market for goods and services across African Union member states, expand intra-African trade, and strengthen the continent’s position in global markets.

Nigeria signed the AfCFTA Agreement on 7 July 2019 and ratified it in 2020, formally joining the continental trade framework.

Nigeria’s participation in the agreement is expected to give businesses opportunities to expand beyond the domestic market, increase intra-African trade, and support economic diversification.

World.title: CBN urges banks to expand financing for exporters
World.content:
The Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Olayemi Cardoso, has urged commercial banks and development finance institutions to expand financing for Nigerian exporters, saying limited access to credit prevents businesses from taking advantage of opportunities in international markets.

He said businesses with confirmed export orders often lacked the working capital to purchase raw materials, obtain certification, expand production or finance shipments, making it difficult to fulfil orders despite having willing buyers.

Mr Cardoso spoke on Thursday in Abuja at a stakeholder forum organised by the Nigerian Export-Import Bank (NEXIM), themed “Leveraging the AfCFTA for Enhanced Nigerian Export Competitiveness and Economic Diversification”.

Represented by Isa Yuguda, the CBN Deputy Governor in charge of Financial System Stability, Mr Cardoso said, “A Nigerian firm may have a confirmed order but lack the working capital to purchase inputs, obtain certification, expand production, or finance shipment.”

He urged commercial banks to work more closely with development finance institutions to bridge the financing gap, stressing that the latter should complement commercial lending rather than replace it.

“The objective should not be for development finance institutions to replace commercial banks, but to crowd them in,” he said.

He called on NEXIM Bank to deploy its financing, guarantees, insurance and risk-sharing instruments to make viable export transactions more attractive to commercial lenders and encourage private capital into the sector.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The call comes as Nigeria seeks to diversify its economy away from crude oil and expand non-oil exports through the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which provides businesses with opportunities to access markets across the continent.

However, limited access to finance, high production costs, infrastructure deficits and difficulties meeting export standards continue to constrain Nigerian businesses’ ability to compete in international markets.

Mr Cardoso warned that Nigeria’s dependence on a narrow range of export commodities exposed the economy to external shocks, stressing that diversification must translate into increased production, employment and sustainable foreign exchange earnings.

“Our ambition must extend beyond increasing export volumes. Nigeria must increase the value, sophistication, and competitiveness of what it exports,” he said.

He advocated greater investment in manufacturing, agricultural processing, solid minerals, technology, services and the creative economy to strengthen Nigeria’s participation in the AfCFTA.

CBN outlines forex reforms, export compliance

Mr Cardoso said the CBN is committed to improving foreign exchange market transparency, liquidity, price discovery, and efficiency to help businesses plan cross-border transactions.

He, however, warned exporters against violating foreign exchange regulations, particularly requirements for documenting transactions and repatriating export proceeds.

“Exporters are expected to comply with applicable documentation requirements and repatriate export proceeds within prescribed regulatory timelines,” he said.

He said monitoring export proceeds, verifying prices and maintaining appropriate documentation were necessary to curb import over-invoicing, export under-invoicing and illicit capital flows.

The CBN governor added that digitising trade documentation and integrating it with the National Single Window would reduce processing times and transaction costs for businesses.

He also pledged continued collaboration with financial institutions to facilitate cross-border transactions through regional payment arrangements, including the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System.

Mr Cardoso said the CBN would focus on monetary and financial stability, while commercial banks would provide scalable private financing and development finance institutions would deploy specialised risk-sharing instruments.

NEXIM reports support for exporters

Earlier, NEXIM Bank Managing Director Abubakar Bello said the bank had financed more than 1,300 exporters since its establishment in 1991, supporting the creation and sustenance of about 110,000 industrial jobs.

He said NEXIM Bank, in collaboration with the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN), had mobilised N42 billion to support small businesses operating within the export value chain.

Mr Bello added that the bank was pursuing a non-interest financing window in partnership with the Islamic Development Bank, alongside dedicated financing facilities for women and young entrepreneurs.

The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, cautioned financial institutions against providing loans that do not align with exporters’ transaction cycles and foreign exchange earnings.

He said businesses could lose export opportunities when financing arrived late, certification was delayed, or transportation costs became unpredictable, even when their products and buyers were ready.

“A business may have a good product and a willing buyer, yet lose the order because financing arrives late, certification is delayed, or transport costs become unpredictable,” he said.

He urged financial institutions to strengthen cooperation through structured financing, guarantees and insurance while maintaining sound lending standards and preparing businesses to meet export requirements.

Also, speaking at the event, the Minister of State for Industry, John Enoh, identified the shortage of patient capital as a major constraint to industrial development, urging lenders to finance productive infrastructure rather than concentrate on individual export transactions.

“Finance the factory and not the shipment. Trade finance moves what already exists. Industrial finance creates what does not yet exist,” Mr Enoh said.

He advocated financing for regional trade and product certification, noting that limited access to credit and electricity shortages had left a significant proportion of Nigeria’s industrial capacity idle.

AfCFTA opportunities

The National Coordinator of the Nigeria AfCFTA Coordination Office, Patience Okala, disclosed plans to organise a financial boot camp for women and young entrepreneurs in the first quarter of 2027 to connect businesses with funding opportunities.

She said certificates of origin issued between December 2025 and November 2026 increased by 500 per cent, while processing time declined from five days to 24 hours.

Certificates of origin are documents used to establish the country where goods were produced, enabling exporters to meet trade requirements and access preferential tariffs under applicable trade agreements.

Meanwhile, the Special Adviser to the President on Economic Affairs, Tope Fasua, called for investments in productive capacity, technology, skills, and infrastructure to prevent Nigeria from becoming a market for foreign goods.

“Market access without productive capacity is an invitation to import, not an assurance of export success,” Mr Fasua said.

The African Development Bank, in its trade finance report released in May 2026, estimated Africa’s unmet trade financing demand at between $74 billion and $92 billion in 2024.

The report also disclosed that commercial banks financed an average of 23 per cent of African trade between 2020 and 2024, down from 40 per cent between 2011 and 2019.

World.title: NCDMB commissions Monarch Alloys’ concrete weight coating plant
World.content:
‎The Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB) has reaffirmed its commitment to supporting local companies to expand in-country capacities for the oil and gas industry as Monarch Alloys Limited commissioned its Concrete Weight Coating (CWC) plant in Ikorodu, Lagos State.

‎The facility, commissioned by the Director, Monitoring and Evaluation, NCDMB, Esueme Kikile, who represented the Executive Secretary, Felix Omatsola Ogbe, is the second phase of Monarch Alloys’ pipe coating investment, adding to its existing 3-Layer Polyethylene (3LPE) coating facility commissioned last year.

‎Speaking at the ceremony on Thursday, Kikile said the completion of the second phase, within about 12 months of the first commissioning, demonstrated the impact of the Board’s interventions on the industry and the country.

‎He congratulated Monarch Alloys on the facility, describing it as a significant contribution to the oil and gas industry, particularly as several projects expected to come on stream from 2027 would require coated pipes for offshore, onshore and gas transmission operations.

‎Kikile reaffirmed NCDMB’s mandate under the Nigerian Oil and Gas Industry Content Development Act 2010 to build the capacity of Nigerian companies and people to participate in the oil and gas industry. He said the Board remained focused on its 10-year strategic roadmap and continued to improve its delivery mechanisms to ensure that the Nigerian economy benefited more from its interventions.

‎“NCDMB was set up to be a business enabler, supporting the value chain efficiencies and project delivery,” he said, adding that the Board had continuously simplified its processes and accelerated approval timelines to enable business delivery. He assured Monarch Alloys of the Board’s continued support, noting that its responsibility was to ensure the availability of in-country capacities that contribute to economic development.

‎Kikile also urged industry leaders to patronise local facilities to grow the economy and support the Federal Government’s target of producing three million barrels of oil per day by 2030. He said the Board would continue to ensure fair and transparent bidding processes and provide opportunities for local companies domiciled in Nigeria to participate in industry activities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

‎Chairman of Monarch Alloys Limited, Mr Atul Chaudhary, said the company had invested about $80m in the industry and planned to expand its capacity through additional specialised facilities. He said the company had successfully completed several 3LPE coating projects, delivering within schedule and meeting required quality standards, while the new concrete weight coating facility was its second phase of investment.

‎Chaudhary said the company’s initial plan was to establish a pipe mill but it decided to begin with coating services before moving into local pipe manufacturing.

‎“Our original plan was to set up a pipe mill because there’s no pipe mill in Nigeria for oil and gas pipes. But then we thought, let’s start with the coating of pipes first, and then eventually we will get into manufacturing of pipes locally. That’s our plan,” he said.

‎He explained that concrete weight coating adds weight to pipes laid in water to prevent them from floating, while other coating processes protect pipes against corrosion and extend their service life.

‎The company currently provides 3LPE, three-layer polypropylene (3LPP), fusion-bonded epoxy (FBE) and concrete weight coating services, with plans to introduce five-layer polypropylene (5LPP) coating for thermal insulation of deep offshore pipelines.

‎He added that the company planned to establish an API threading facility and a plant for Oil Country Tubular Goods (OCTG), while also expanding its coating capabilities.

‎Chaudhary said the company was employing about 150 Nigerians, including engineers, technicians and skilled workers, noting that local content was about building industries, creating jobs, developing skills, transferring knowledge and retaining value within the Nigerian economy.

‎The commissioning ceremony was attended by representatives of oil and gas companies, including SNEPCo, Nigeria LNG and other industry stakeholders. Renaissance Africa Energy Company commended Monarch Alloys for keeping its promises and delivering work to industry standards, citing its experience with the company’s pipe-coating services.

SNEPCo said it was impressed with the progress made at the facility and expressed hope for future engagement, while Nigeria LNG Limited said it encouraged local companies making efforts to build a better Nigeria and would partner with and support Monarch when opportunities arose. It also urged the company to maintain quality and prioritise safety.

‎Former Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment and former Governor of Ekiti State, Mr. Adeniyi Adebayo, said the facility demonstrated that some services previously sourced outside the country could be provided locally. He said local pipe coating would create jobs, conserve foreign exchange and support the development of Nigeria’s oil and gas industry, particularly with the country’s planned increase in oil production and expansion of gas infrastructure.

‎Adebayo commended the Chairman, Board and management of Monarch Alloys for the investment, expressing optimism about the company’s planned expansion into additional technologies and services.

World.title: Meet Emmanuel Emegha, Chelsea’s new striking sensation who has Nigerian roots
World.content:
By Enitan Abdultawab

Chelsea’s latest attacking prospect, Emmanuel Emegha, is already giving supporters reasons to pay attention after scoring against Nottingham Forest on Friday.

While the Blues trailed by two goals to nil, the 23-year-old striker, who joined Chelsea from French side Strasbourg, came off the bench to replace Danny Welbeck, found the net in the 54th and 89th minutes, and offered the Blues a lifeline in their Premier League encounter.

However, his goals were not enough as Forest held unto their lead after Morgan Gibss-White had extended it immediately after, bringing the game to a 3-2 full-time result.

Before the Forest clash, Emegha put Chelsea ahead at home when they hosted Leeds United last week. Unfortunately, he could not save the team from capitulating to a 1-4 defeat in the game.

But beyond his growing reputation in England, Emegha has an interesting connection to Nigeria.

Born in The Hague, Netherlands, to a Togolese father and a Nigerian mother, the powerful forward has West African roots.



His Nigerian heritage makes him a player of interest to Nigerian football fans, particularly those following the growing number of players of Nigerian descent making waves in European football.

However, Emegha has chosen to represent the Netherlands internationally. He made his senior debut against Poland in November 2025, explaining that the Netherlands is his country and that he is proud to be Dutch.

Although Nigeria missed out on having him represent the Super Eagles, his progress at Chelsea gives Nigerian fans another reason to follow his career closely.

At 23, Emegha has the physical presence, pace and goalscoring instincts to make an impression in English football.

His latest goals against Nottingham Forest are another early signs of what he could offer Chelsea.

World.title: Chelsea beaten at Nottingham Forest as poor run continues
World.content:
Nottingham Forest claimed a memorable 3-2 victory over Chelsea at the City Ground on Friday night, November 27, piling further pressure on Blues manager Xabi Alonso after another disappointing performance from his side.

Forest made a flying start to the encounter, taking the lead just five minutes into the game through Igor Jesus, who produced a superb volley from Daniel Muñoz’s cross to put the hosts ahead.

Chelsea struggled to find their rhythm in the opening half, with Forest looking more dangerous and organised in attack. Despite enjoying more possession, the visitors failed to turn their dominance on the ball into meaningful goalscoring opportunities.

The hosts doubled their advantage shortly after the restart when Morgan Gibbs-White converted from the penalty spot in the 51st minute. The penalty was awarded after Wesley Fofana brought down Liam Delap inside the Chelsea box.

However, Chelsea responded three minutes later through substitute Emmanuel Emegha, who pulled one back after Pedro Neto’s effort took a deflection and fell kindly into his path.

The goal briefly offered Chelsea hope of mounting a comeback, but Forest remained dangerous and restored their two-goal cushion in the 72nd minute when Gibbs-White grabbed his second of the evening.

Chelsea refused to surrender, with Emegha scoring again in the 89th minute to reduce the deficit to 3-2 and set up a tense finish.

However, Forest held on through the closing moments to secure all three points and condemn Chelsea to another painful defeat.

The result represents another setback for Alonso, whose team have struggled for consistency in recent weeks.

Chelsea’s defensive weaknesses and inability to control crucial moments once again proved costly.

For Nottingham Forest, the victory provides a significant boost and a valuable reward for their determination and attacking efficiency.

Chelsea must now turn their attention to their next Premier League fixture against Crystal Palace as they look to recover from another frustrating night.

World.title: Mock ballot papers won’t feature party names, logos – INEC
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has explained that sample ballot papers for its nationwide mock accreditation exercise will not carry political party names or logos because the exercise is designed to test election technology rather than promote any political party.

INEC Deputy Director of Voter Education and Publicity, Wilfred Ifogah, gave the explanation during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, ahead of the exercise scheduled for Saturday, November 28.

Ifogah said the mock accreditation was a non-partisan exercise intended to assess the commission’s preparedness for the 2027 general elections.

He explained that the exercise would allow INEC to test its equipment and give voters an idea of what the accreditation and voting processes would look like during the elections.

“This is a mock exercise; we are not using it for any partisanship event. It is just something for those who come out to feel a sense of participation”, he said.

According to him, election materials have already been deployed to the selected polling units across the country.

The exercise will take place in 17,676 polling units, covering two polling units in each of Nigeria’s 8,838 registration areas.

INEC is expected to deploy the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and its electronic results upload technology to assess their reliability ahead of the general elections.

The mock accreditation will run from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., with the commission hoping that the exercise will strengthen public confidence in the electoral process.

The 2027 general elections are scheduled to begin with the presidential and National Assembly polls on January 16, while the governorship and state Houses of Assembly elections will hold on February 6.

The commission’s mock exercise forms part of its preparations for the polls, allowing it to test its technology and electoral procedures before election day.

World.title: Ogun 2027: Court dismisses Hunye’s suits against Adeola’s APC candidacy
World.content:
Senator Solomon Adeola Olamilekan Yayi.

…Adeola hails judgment

…as Hunye heads to Court of Appeal

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

The Federal High Court sitting in Abeokuta, Ogun State, on Friday dismissed two suits filed by Hon. Abayomi Semako Hunye challenging the emergence of Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, as the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 election.

Delivering judgment in the two consolidated suits, Justice Okeke held that the cases lacked merit and consequently dismissed them.

The suits, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1127/2026 and FHC/AB/126/2026, were instituted by Hunye against the APC, Senator Adeola and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), challenging the process through which Adeola emerged as the party’s governorship candidate.

Reacting to the judgment, Adeola commended the judiciary, describing the decision as a vindication of the rule of law and the judicial process.

In a statement issued by his media adviser, Chief Kayode Odunaro, the senator expressed satisfaction with the outcome while appreciating his legal team for what he described as their painstaking efforts in defending the suits.

Adeola said, “I want to commend the Honourable Justice for his erudite judgment in these cases challenging my overwhelming and widely accepted victory in our party primary. I also commend my legal team for the painstaking defense put up during the process.

“This victory is yet another milestone in our quest for equity and justice in the Ogun State 2027 election. To God be the glory once again.”

The senator said that despite the legal challenges, he had remained focused on consolidating support for his candidacy across the state through engagements with political stakeholders and other interest groups.

He added that his engagements had also included the presentation of his nine-pillar ITESIWAJU Agenda, which he described as his development blueprint for Ogun State.

According to him, the court’s decision would allow him to concentrate more fully on preparations for the 2027 governorship election and take his campaign message to voters across the state.

Adeola also urged APC members and his supporters, irrespective of their political affiliations, to remain united and focused, stressing that his ambition was driven by a desire to serve the people and contribute to the development of Ogun State.

However, Hunye has rejected the outcome of the proceedings and indicated his intention to appeal the judgment.

In a statement titled, “Our Legal Journey Continues to the Court of Appeal,” Hunye described the Federal High Court as the first stage of the judicial process, insisting that the appellate court would provide another opportunity for his legal team to pursue the issues raised in the suits.

He reaffirmed his commitment to constitutional due process, internal party democracy, and the rule of law, saying his decision to continue with the litigation was informed by the need to ensure fairness and strict compliance with established legal and electoral procedures.

“The Federal High Court is just the first court of hearing, while the Court of Appeal is the next port of call,” Hunye stated.

He expressed confidence in the appellate process, adding that his legal team was prepared to present its arguments before the Court of Appeal.

“Where questions of fairness, legality, and electoral compliance remain unresolved, our legal team is fully prepared to test every issue before the Court of Appeal. We have faith in the appellate process and remain confident that, in time, truth and legality will prevail,” he said.

Hunye further appealed to his supporters, APC members, and the general public to remain calm, peaceful, and law-abiding as the legal process continues.

He maintained that his decision to pursue the matter was not merely about political ambition but also about defending due process, strengthening internal party democracy, and ensuring that political parties adhere to constitutional and electoral requirements.

World.title: Two Nigerians arrested over romance scam in Thailand
World.content:
Two Nigerian men have been arrested in Thailand over their alleged links to an international romance scam network targeting victims across Southeast Asia.

The suspects, aged 41 and 30, were arrested on November 18 at a condominium in Ban Mai, Pak Kret district, Nonthaburi, following an investigation by Thailand’s Immigration Division 3 and Provincial Police Region 1.

According to local media outlet, The Thaiger, undercover police officers disguised themselves as food delivery workers to gain access to the suspects’ apartment.

With the help of security guards, the officers approached the condominium and pretended to have a parcel for delivery. When one of the men opened the door, they identified themselves as police officers and moved in to arrest both suspects.

A search of the apartment reportedly led to the recovery of laptops and mobile phones containing messages linked to fake online identities posing as US military personnel.

Investigators suspect the identities were used to establish romantic relationships with potential victims as part of an international scam operation. Police also reportedly found social media accounts allegedly created to deceive Thai residents.

The arrests followed an earlier investigation on November 12, when police detained another Nigerian man, aged 37, at Owl Market in Nonthaburi over suspected links to the same network.

Investigators later searched a condominium in Bang Kraso, Mueang Nonthaburi, where suspected members of the group had reportedly stayed. However, the men had left before the search.

Police subsequently traced the two suspects to another condominium in the Muang Thong Thani area, where they were believed to have stayed for two to three days before their arrest.

The Thaiger reported that both men confessed during questioning. However, the charges publicly reported against them are immigration-related offences, including illegal entry and unauthorised residence.

One of the suspects, aged 41, had reportedly overstayed his permitted stay in Thailand by 411 days.

Authorities revoked their permission to remain in the country and transferred them to Pak Kret Police Station for further legal proceedings ahead of deportation.

The investigation into the suspected romance scam network is ongoing. Thai police have not disclosed the identities of the alleged victims, the amount of money involved or the specific roles the two men allegedly played in the operation.

The reported immigration charges do not amount to convictions for romance fraud.

World.title: CBN targets $1.5bn monthly diaspora dollar inflows
World.content:
— Vows to deploy external reserves against FX shocks

To unveil regulatory rule book next year

By Babajide Komolafe

The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) is targeting $1.5 billion monthly diaspora remittance inflows by the first half of 2027, following the achievement of its $1 billion monthly target, while pledging to deploy external reserves to cushion the economy against external shocks.

CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, disclosed this at the 61st Annual Bankers Dinner organised by the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN) in Lagos.

Speaking on the foreign exchange market and the country’s external buffers, Cardoso said: “I am pleased that this milestone has actually been achieved, towards increased monthly remittances of $1 billion. Our next target is $1.5 billion by the end of the first half of 2027.”

He said Nigeria was considerably better equipped to manage external shocks than it was three years ago, following reforms that strengthened macroeconomic fundamentals and external buffers.

“The external buffers we have built provide greater resilience, and the Central Bank of Nigeria stands ready to deploy its reserves when necessary to address disorderly market conditions and mitigate the impact of shocks,” he said.

According to him, the CBN’s responsibility was not to target a particular exchange rate level but to safeguard market stability, deepen liquidity and support orderly price discovery.

“Recent short-term movements should be viewed in the context of strengthened macroeconomic fundamentals and the outlook for 2027,” he said, adding that volatility was an inherent feature of global financial markets.

Cardoso also announced plans to introduce a regulatory rule book next year as part of efforts to strengthen the financial system, improve accountability and ensure that financial institutions operate within a clear and consistent regulatory framework.

He said the financial system required governance, transparency, accountability and decision-making grounded in clear analysis and consistent application of regulatory standards.

The CBN governor urged banks to strengthen treasury expertise, expand hedging and risk management products, support exporters and provide more effective services to businesses engaged in international trade.

He also announced plans to deepen Nigeria’s financial market infrastructure, saying the apex bank would work with market participants to launch interbank repo and overnight interest rate swap markets in the first quarter of 2027.

“To further deepen liquidity and improve market efficiency, we will work with market participants to launch the interbank repo and overnight interest swap markets in the first quarter of 2027,” he said.

Cardoso said Nigeria’s removal from the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) grey list in October 2025 reflected sustained efforts across government, regulatory authorities and the financial sector to strengthen the country’s framework against money laundering, terrorist financing and related financial crimes.

World.title: Adesua Etomi celebrates negative cancer test
World.content:
Nollywood actress Adesua Etomi-Wellington has celebrated testing negative for cancer after months of medical procedures, hospital visits and uncertainty over her health.

The actress announced the development on Friday in an Instagram video, expressing gratitude to God following the latest result from her medical tests.

“The doctor just called me back with the result from the lab, no cancer… God is good,” she said.

The video showed some of the medical procedures she underwent, while other pictures revealed bruises on her body and redness beneath one of her eyes.

Etomi-Wellington also shared a video of friends and well-wishers celebrating the result with her.

Reflecting on her experience, the actress described 2026 as one of the most difficult periods of her life, explaining that her reduced public appearances were linked to her health struggles.

“2026 really tried it. I know I’ve been quieter than usual this year (and that’s saying something), but behind the silence were some of the most difficult months of my life,” she wrote.

She disclosed that the ordeal involved several medical procedures, scans, injections and hospital visits, adding that she received treatment from medical teams in Nigeria and the United States.

“This year threw everything at me, but by the grace of God, I am NOT EASILY BROKEN,” she added.

The actress also expressed appreciation to her husband, singer and politician Bankole Wellington, popularly known as Banky W, their children, friends and family members for supporting her throughout the difficult period.

“To my friends and family who prayed for me, stood in the gap and held me through some of my darkest days, I will never take your love for granted,” she wrote.

The health update comes two days after the couple released a gospel song, On My Way, on November 25 to celebrate their ninth wedding anniversary.

The track, credited to Etomi-Wellington, who performs under the musical name Susu, and Banky W, is the lead single from their forthcoming joint album, Not Easily Broken, expected in 2027.

The actress described the song as “the soundtrack to our testimony and thanksgiving”, linking its message to their personal experiences.

The couple have previously spoken about their health challenges. In May 2024, Banky W disclosed that he had undergone his fourth surgery for cancer after earlier procedures to remove cancerous tumours.

Etomi-Wellington also revealed in March 2025 that she battled hyperemesis gravidarum, a severe form of pregnancy sickness, during her second pregnancy. The condition left her ill for months and required hospitalisation before she underwent an emergency Caesarean section.

World.title: Meet Moyin Odeniran, 22-year-old who won UK’s top baking competition
World.content:
By Enitan Abdultawab

Twenty-two-year-old Moyin Odeniran has emerged winner of the 17th season of Britain’s popular amateur baking competition, The Great British Bake Off, after defeating fellow finalists Mo Mahir and Tom Whittaker.

Odeniran, an Essex-based student of political economy, clinched the title during the grand finale on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, following a series of baking challenges judged by Paul Hollywood and Nigella Lawson.

The final featured three challenges, beginning with a citrus celebration cake, followed by crème brûlée doughnuts in the technical round. The contestants then faced the task of creating elaborate showstopper cakes inspired by iconic British landscapes.

Odeniran impressed the judges with his creations, earning the championship as hosts Noel Fielding and Alison Hammond announced the result.

Hollywood praised the young baker’s improvement throughout the competition, noting that he had struggled during the early stages before gradually establishing himself as one of the strongest contestants.

“The reaction from his family, I have never seen anything like it. It was pure magic! He has done an amazing job because out of all the bakers, he struggled at the beginning, and he actually got better and better,” Hollywood said.

He also singled out Odeniran’s signature challenge cake, describing it as one of the best cakes he had tasted in a long time.

Co-judge Lawson also commended the finalists, acknowledging the quality of the creations presented by Mahir and Whittaker despite Odeniran taking the overall prize.

The 22-year-old recorded several impressive moments during the competition, including his first Hollywood handshake during Friends and Family Week, when he baked alongside his mother, Kike.

He also secured the Star Baker award during the eighth week of the competition, themed Caramel Week.

Odeniran later described baking with his mother as one of his most memorable experiences on the show. The pair received a Hollywood handshake together during Audience Choice Week.

His victory was celebrated by his family and fellow contestants, including Nikki, Medwin and Joshua, who joined in the excitement after the announcement.

His victory adds another milestone to the 2026 edition of The Great British Bake Off, which continues to showcase amateur bakers competing for recognition through a series of demanding culinary challenges.

World.title: Adeleke Sworn in for Second Term, Promises Economic Transformation
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Governor Ademola Adeleke of Osun and his deputy, Kola Adewusi, were on Friday sworn-in for a second term in office.



The Chief Judge of the state, Justice Oyebola Adepele-Ojo, administered the oaths of office to the governor and his deputy at the Osogbo Township Stadium.



Adeleke took the oath of office at 11:37 a.m., while Adewusi was sworn in at 11:23 a.m.



The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that President Bola Tinubu was represented at the event by Vice-President Kashim Shettima.



Speaking after his inauguration, Adeleke thanked the people of the state for giving him the mandate and opportunity to continue in office.



He pledged to prioritise citizens’ welfare, infrastructure development, the digital economy, agricultural growth, job creation and youth employment.



The governor also reviewed the achievements of his administration in the last four years and outlined his plans for the next four years.



“My vision is to move Osun from a civil service economy to an industrialised one. We are open to partnership with private organisations and economic advisory groups.



“Specifically, we will target agro-processing factories, industrial parks across districts, free trade zones, sports and tourism development, and a better business environment,” he said.



Adeleke said President Tinubu had intervened in the lingering local government crisis in the state, expressing optimism that the crisis would be fully resolved within the next one week.



He, however, said he would address the people of the state in greater detail on his agenda for the next four years.



The governor, thereafter, inspected the police parade mounted for the inauguration.



NAN reports that dignitaries at the event include former Senate President Bukola Saraki; 2023 Labour Party vice-presidential candidate, Datti Baba-Ahmed; National Chairman of the Accord Party, Maxwell Mgbudem; and APC National Leader, Chief Bisi Akande, among others.



Traditional rulers present include the Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi; the Olubadan of Ibadan, Oba Rashidi Ladoja; the Soun of Ogbomoso, Oba Ghandi Olaoye; and the Alaafin of Oyo, Oba Abimbola Owoade, among others. (NAN)

World.title: Adeleke’s Second Term Mandate, Defining Milestone for Osun’s Devt, Says Adigun
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

The Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Sammya Nigeria Limited, Engr. Adigun Sammy Oreoluwa, has described Governor Ademola Adeleke’s renewed mandate as a defining milestone in the socio-economic development of Osun State.

Adigun, in a congratulatory statement made available to journalists in Osogbo, said Adeleke’s re-election and inauguration for a second term represented an opportunity to consolidate the achievements of his first tenure and accelerate the state’s development.

He noted that over the past four years, the Adeleke administration had established enduring partnerships in critical areas, including public infrastructure, civil service reforms, grassroots welfare and private-sector collaboration.

According to him, the governor’s second-term inauguration was a moment worthy of celebration by his associates, business partners, political leaders, development partners and other stakeholders who had identified with his journey in public service.

Adigun said the renewed mandate was not only a national political milestone but also a reflection of the confidence reposed in the governor and the shared commitment of stakeholders to the growth and prosperity of Osun State.

He urged Adeleke to sustain his people-oriented approach to governance while expanding the delivery of infrastructure, social services and other development initiatives capable of improving the living conditions of residents.

He also called on the governor to remain committed to the principles of a government of the people, by the people and for the people, stressing the need for inclusive governance and policies that would positively impact all sections of the state.

The Sammya Nigeria Limited chairman, on behalf of the company’s management and staff, also extended his goodwill to the Chief of Staff, members of the State Executive Council, cabinet members, political appointees, aides, supporters and other members of the governor’s team.

He described the inauguration as a significant milestone in the political and developmental journey of Osun State, expressing confidence that the governor and his team would make the second tenure more impactful.

Adigun further prayed for divine guidance, wisdom, strength and good health for Adeleke and members of his administration as they continue their service to the people.

He expressed optimism that the governor’s second term would usher in greater development, peace, unity, progress and prosperity across the state.

World.title: Osun IPAC Urges Adeleke to Appoint Competent Cabinet, Reduce Aides, Recruit Teachers
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

The Osun State Chapter of the Inter-Party Advisory Council, (IPAC), has congratulated Governor Ademola Adeleke on his inauguration for a second term, while charging him to deepen good governance and deliver more impactful dividends of democracy to the people of Osun State.

In a statement issued in Osogbo on Friday by the state chairman of IPAC, Dr Tosin Odeyemi, the council described the Governor’s re-election as an expression of confidence by the electorate in his first-term performance and a mandate for consolidation, noting that the second term offers a fresh opportunity to correct lapses, strengthen institutions and leave a lasting legacy.

IPAC urged the Governor to ensure that appointments into his new cabinet are based strictly on competence, experience and character.

It cautioned Adeleke against the use of appointments as political compensation and insisted that only round pegs should be placed in round holes.

“The re-election of Governor Ademola Adeleke shows the will of Osun people. However, history will not remember the fanfare of inauguration. It will remember what this second term delivers to the ordinary citizen. This is the time to raise the bar.

“The Governor must put round pegs in round holes. Osun State needs commissioners who understand their portfolios, who can initiate policies, drive implementation and be held accountable for results,” the statement noted.

IPAC also called for a robust monitoring and evaluation mechanism for all government projects to guarantee quality delivery and value for money, stressing that no project should be abandoned or poorly executed.

It stated that contractors must be held to contractual standards, advising the administration to always ascertain the needs of communities before siting projects, saying development must be demand-driven and not imposed.

“Government must feel the pulse of citizens before siting projects in any area. Development must be demand-driven, not imposed. When people are consulted, they own the project and protect it,” IPAC said.

The council urged the Governor to carry stakeholders along in major policy decisions, noting that inclusive governance promotes peace, trust and sustainable development.

It also recommended a reduction in the number of political aides as part of efforts to cut the cost of governance and free resources for critical sectors.

“We urge the Governor to reduce the number of aides in the interest of sound financial management. Resources saved from the cost of governance should be redirected to roads, schools, hospitals and job creation,” the statement said.

The statement further called for equitable distribution of developmental projects across the three senatorial districts, warning that no part of the state should feel marginalised, and specifically demanded massive recruitment of teachers to address shortages in public schools and recruitment of health workers to strengthen primary healthcare delivery.

“Osun needs massive recruitment of teachers and health workers. Our classrooms are overstretched, and our health centres are understaffed. This second term must decisively address these gaps,” IPAC said.

The council concluded by expressing optimism that faithful implementation of the agenda would make Adeleke’s second term a defining era in the development of the state.

“The people have given the Governor a second mandate. He must repay that trust with a second term that posterity will remember,” it added.

World.title: QNET Terminates 141 Accounts over Illegal Cross-border Activities, Records 298 Disciplinary Actions
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

● Warns Nigerians against fake job, visa, guaranteed income offers, steps up anti-fraud campaign, product innovation in Nigeria

James Emejo in Abuja

QNET, an international lifestyle and wellness company, has disclosed that it terminated 141 distributor accounts linked to facilitating illegal cross-border movements between 2025 and 2026, as it intensified efforts to curb fraudulent activities involving its brand in Nigeria and other African markets.

The company also recorded 298 disciplinary actions against non-compliant distributors across its sub-Saharan operations in 2024, underscoring the scale of its efforts to enforce ethical standards within its direct-selling network.



QNET disclosed these figures during a media engagement in Abuja yesterday, where it outlined measures to address the activities of individuals and groups allegedly exploiting its name to defraud Nigerians through fake employment, overseas travel, visa and guaranteed income offers.

The company’s General Manager for Nigeria, Ayokunmi Solesi, said QNET was neither a recruitment agency nor an employment provider, stressing that its business model was based on the sale of products rather than the recruitment of individuals.



He explained that independent distributors earn commissions from qualifying product sales, not from bringing new members into the network.



Solesi warned Nigerians against individuals who demand money or personal documents under the guise of securing employment, visas or relocation opportunities through QNET.

He also cautioned members of the public against borrowing money to participate in schemes promoted under the company’s name, noting that earnings from direct selling were not guaranteed and depended on individual sales activities.

Partnership with security agencies

To strengthen its consumer protection framework, QNET said it had stepped up collaboration with Nigerian authorities, including the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), the Nigerian Army, the Department of State Services (DSS) and the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC).



The company said its enforcement measures were complemented by international collaboration with INTERPOL to tackle fraudulent networks operating across borders and misrepresenting its business.

It also identified its QNET Against Scams, Say NO! and Mama campaigns as key components of its public awareness strategy, designed to educate communities on fraudulent schemes and the risks associated with misleading business propositions.



Solesi said the company had also introduced an accreditation framework for independent distributors seeking to operate offices, with the objective of ensuring compliance with its operational standards.

QNET further urged the media to rely on verifiable information in reporting its activities, noting that it had facilitated visits by Nigerian journalists to its global headquarters in Malaysia to provide first-hand exposure to its operations.

Product exhibition, innovation drive

Beyond its anti-fraud campaign, the company is seeking to strengthen public understanding of its product portfolio through a two-day exhibition scheduled for November 27 and 28 at the Merry Makers Event Centre, Wuse 2, Abuja.



The exhibition will showcase products across health and wellness, home and living, personal care, beauty, watches and jewellery.



Featured products include LifeQode nutritional supplements, Amezcua wellness devices, HomePure air and water purification systems, Physio Radiance skincare products, as well as Swiss-made timepieces from Bernhard H. Mayer and Cimier.



Solesi said the exhibition would provide an opportunity for consumers to examine the products and better understand the company’s product-based direct-selling structure.

He added that QNET’s product development process was supported by a scientific board comprising experts, including Professor Abiodun Adebayo, a Professor of Biochemistry and former Vice-Chancellor of Covenant University.



The company said its product portfolio was developed to address different lifestyle and consumer needs, while maintaining quality standards.

Youth empowerment, financial literacy

QNET also highlighted its FinGreen financial literacy programme, which it said had reached more than 200,000 young Nigerians, equipping them with knowledge to identify fraudulent investment propositions and make informed financial decisions.



The company said the initiative formed part of its broader youth empowerment interventions and efforts to promote responsible entrepreneurship.



It reiterated that customers could purchase its products for personal use or, subject to its policies, become independent distributors and earn commissions from qualifying sales.

However, it emphasised that the business did not constitute salaried employment or offer guaranteed earnings, migration or relocation services.



QNET urged Nigerians to verify any business proposition attributed to the company through its official communication channels and report suspicious activities.

World.title: How AAPSCOMMS Can Boost Public Administration In Africa, By Olaopa
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

The Chairman, Federal Civil Service Commission, Prof. Tunji Olaopa, has proposed measures for the Association of African Public Service Commissions (AAPSCOMS) to make more impact on the African continent in the area of public administration and strengthen civil service commissions (CSCs).

Olaopa spoke on Friday at the AAPSCOMMS Non-Elective, General Assembly and Conference holding in Nairobi, Kenya, from 27 to 28 November, 2026.
