World.title: “Hemos sido siempre una empresa soñadora y valiente”
World.content:
Juan José Hernández, presidente ejecutivo de Hospiten, habla de la vocación de crecimiento de una empresa que acaba de realizar una inversión cercana a los 200 millones de euros para poner en marcha un centro hospitalario de 55.000 metros cuadrados en Madrid

Habla

De abrir su primer hospital en Puerto de la Cruz (Tenerife) a finales de los años sesenta a contar hoy con centros hospitalarios en varias ciudades españolas y en países como México, Jamaica, República Dominicana o Panamá. Pese a la extraordinaria expansión de Hospiten en algo más de medio siglo, su presidente ejecutivo, Juan José Hernández Rubio, asegura que uno de los rasgos distintivos de la empresa sigue siendo su carácter familiar, según explica en esta en esta entrevista del espacio Hablan las marcas, con motivo del 50º aniversario de EL PAÍS.

“En algún momento hemos tenido algún socio financiero, pero el control siempre lo ha tenido la misma familia”, detalla. Esta característica, defiende, ha dado al grupo “una vocación de permanencia y una visión en el medio y en el largo plazo”, que, alimentada por un equipo directivo con “una sensación de pertenencia muy fuerte”, les ha permitido convertirse en líderes en el sector sanitario, con cerca de tres millones de pacientes atendidos cada año.

“Hemos sido siempre una empresa soñadora”, argumenta Hernández, quien destaca la apertura este mes de noviembre de Hospiten Madrid Boadilla, un hospital de 55.000 metros cuadrados, 80 consultas, 45 especialidades y 17 quirófanos que incorporará “la máxima tecnología en todos los sentidos, desde cirugía, robótica u oncología” y detrás del cual hay una inversión récord de cerca de 200 millones de euros. “Como dice nuestro presidente de honor, el doctor Pedro Luis Cobiella Suárez, a nosotros no nos gusta poner límites. Hemos sido valientes y así es como me gustaría que continuáramos en el futuro”.

World.title: Puig compra la marca francesa Parfums de Marly por 1.200 millones de euros
World.content:
Puig ha anunciado en la noche de este viernes la adquisición de Artessence, una compañía francesa de perfumes, propietaria de las marcas Parfums de Marly e Initio Parfums Privés. La operación valora la firma, fundada en 2009, en 1.900 millones de euros, según ha informado la compañía a la Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV).

Este acuerdo supone que Puig se haga con el 75% de la firma, por lo que pagará 1.200 millones de euros. El 25% restante seguirá en manos de sus actuales propietarios, que venden la mayoría de las acciones. Se trata de un holding participado por el fondo Advent, el fundador, Julien Sprecher, y otros socios minoritarios. Spercher, que es el director creativo de la marca, se mantendrá en el grupo.

Además, las partes han acordado que Puig podrá adquirir ese 25% que no estará en sus manos, y se queda el holding del fundador, en un plazo de cuatro años. El precio de esta participación restante dependerá de la evolución de la compañia comprada en este tiempo y se prevé que la empresa comprada opere con independencia de Puig en el medio plazo. Esta es exactamente la misma estructura que Puig ha realizado en operaciones previas, como las adquisiciones de Byredo (en 2022) o Charlotte Tilbury (en 2020), especializadas en cosméticos de alta gama y maquillaje, respectivamente.

La adquisición, según informa la compañía catalana, se financiará con una mezcla de deuda y recursos propios. Prevé mantenerse dentro de su umbral de apalancamiento, de dos veces, contando también con la adquisición del 50% que no controlaban en ISDN, que compartía con la familia Esteve, por lo que paga otros 1.200 millones de euros, de los cuales 900 millones se pagarán al cierre de la operación, y 300 millones en el primer trimestre de 2029. En suma, las dos adquisiciones suponen un desembolso de 2.400 millones de euros en apenas unos meses. De acuerdo al cierre de Bolsa de este viernes, Puig tiene una tasación cercana a los 3.700 millones de euros

Las previsiones de Puig —que saltó a Bolsa en la primavera de 2024, en lel mayor debut en el parqué español en los últimos años— pasan por que Artessence genere unas ventas netas de aproximadamente entre 420 y 440 millones de dólares (entre 380 y 400 millones de euros) y un ebitda de entre 180 y 190 millones de dólares (entre 160 y 170 millones de euros) en el ejercicio fiscal 2026-27, que finaliza el 31 de marzo de 2027.

Las partes esperan que la operación se cierre durante el segundo trimestre de 2027. Para ello necesitan obtener las autorizaciones regulatorias pertinentes, así como la aprobación de la junta de accionistas de Puig. La familia fundadora, primer accionista de la empresa, se ha comprometido a votar a favor.

“Parfums de Marly e Initio son marcas excepcionales que combinan deseabilidad con una impresionante trayectoria de crecimiento rentable. Son altamente complementarias con nuestro portfolio y encarnan el tipo de Love Brands singulares que aspiramos a impulsar en Puig. Esta operación refleja nuestro enfoque selectivo en M&A: invertimos en marcas atractivas, con un claro encaje estratégico, que complementan nuestro crecimiento orgánico, preservando al mismo tiempo nuestra flexibilidad financiera. Incluso tras completar esta adquisición y la operación de ISDIN anunciada anteriormente, prevemos mantenernos dentro de nuestro umbral de apalancamiento de 2,0x al cierre del ejercicio 2027″, ha indicado el presidente de la compañía, Marc Puig, en una nota de prensa.

La operación sirve a Puig para reforzarse en el segmento de perfumes, el más grande la compañía. Y en su gama alta. Adquiere los portfolios de Parfums de Marly, inspirada en las fragancias francesas del siglo XVIII, e Initio Parfums Privés, creada en 2015. Ambas cuentan con un importante peso en el mercado estadounidense.

La transacción encaja con el plan estratégico que presentó la compañía hace un mes. Esta hoja de ruta, a cumplir hasta 2032, prevé alcanzar los 8.000 millones de euros de facturación a través del crecimiento de las marcas de su portfolio y con la puerta abierta a adquisiciones, como la que acaba de realizar. Un lugar destacado en este plan estaba reservado para crecer con fragancias niche en el mercado estadounidense, uno de los objetivos que se aceleran con la adquisición de Artessence. También afirmaba que buscaba enfocarse en fragancias prestige femeninas.

Todo ello se produce tras los meses de negociaciones con Estée Lauder para una fusión con la que crear un gigante de la cosmética a nivel mundial. Las dos empresas anunciaron a inicios de año, en marzo, que abrían negociaciones para esta operación, que les permitiría competir con los grandes del sector, como L’Oreal. La suma de ambas compañías habría arrojado un gigante con una valoración bursátil cercana a los 40.000 millones de dólares, sumando los 30.000 millones de capitalización de la estadounidense y los 9.000 de la compañía española, y unas ventas agregadas superiores a los 17.000 millones de euros (12.336 de Estee Lauder y 5.042 de Puig).

Apenas unos meses después, en mayo, comunicaron la ruptura de las negociaciones. Entre los factores en contra estaba la delicada situación de la compañía estadounidense. En su último año fiscal se anotó una pérdida neta de 1.133 millones de dólares y sus ingresos cayeron un 8,2% anual, así como se encuentra inmersa en un plan de reestructuración que pasa por despidos de 7.000 empleados. Tampoco favorecieron el acuerdo las demandas que afronta Estée Lauder por algunos accionistas y el complicado encaje que podían tener algunas de las marcas de Puig, como Charlotte Tilbury. Los catalanes aplazaron entonces la presentación de su plan estratégico por estas negociaciones, que no llegó hasta octubre. Y ahora quieren dar muestra el barco ha virado de rumbo y navega a toda vela.

World.title: El Santander se concentra en crecer en banca de empresas y remodela al equipo en España
World.content:
El Santander ha decidido realizar cambios en siete de sus direcciones territoriales, según ha informado este viernes en un comunicado. En concreto, ha dcidido sustituir a los responsables de Madrid, Andalucía, Galicia, Castilla-La Mancha, Baleares, Castilla y León y Canarias. Los siete nuevos directores dependerán del director de Territoriales, Manuel Iturbe, que a su vez reporta al responsable al propio Oyarzábal.

La medida se toma apenas unos meses después de que el banco nombrase a Borja Oyarzábal como responsable de todo el área, una de las figuras en ascenso en el banco, compartiendo la responsabilidad sobre todo el potente área de retail con Matías Sánchez. El movimiento demuestra el foco que ha puesto el banco en crecer en este área.

Desde el 1 de diciembre, el director territorial de la Comunidad de Madrid será Jaime Uscola, en sustitución de Alberto Delgado, mientras que en Andalucía asumirá el cargo David Casado, en sustitución de Manuel de la Cruz. Francisco Piña será el director territorial de Galicia, en lugar de Rocío Pazos, que se incorpora al área de Seguros del banco. Francisco José Rubio será el nuevo director territorial de Castilla-La Mancha, cargo que hasta ahora ocupaba el propio Piña.

Lorena Álvarez pasa a ser la directora territorial de Baleares, sustituyendo a Celia Torrebadella; Belén Sánchez Sanjuan sucederá a Javier Martín Clavo como directora territorial de Castilla y León, mientras que Jafet Hassan Abrante estará al frente de Canarias, donde hasta ahora era directora Beatriz Martínez Ruiz.

La entidad afirma que nuevos perfiles están orientados a reforzar un modelo de gestión segmentado y más adaptado a las nuevas necesidades de las empresas, sus planes de crecimiento y el diferente grado de especialización que requieren. Ha explicado, además, que el director territorial no solo será el representante institucional en el territorio, sino que también se refuerzan con capacidades comerciales y de banca corporativa. La estrategia estará centrada en el asesoramiento empresarial para mejorar la respuesta a la “creciente demanda” de nuevas soluciones de financiación e inversión, ha explicado el banco.

Los cambios vienen a potenciar el negocio de Banca de Empresas con un nuevo modelo de segmentación que tiene en cuenta no solo el tamaño de las empresas, sino las características y necesidades financieras. El banco cuenta con una cuota de negocio de pymes del 25% y 450.000 empresas clientes.

El mero nombramiento de Oyarzábal ya supone una pequeña revolución en este ámbito. Procede de la gestora de capital privado Tresmares, cuyo modelo se basaba en la financiación con fondos de deuda. Aportaba ayuda financiera a pequeñas y medianas empresas de una forma híbrida, con deuda y con capital. Tresmares contó desde un primer momento con el apoyo del Santander, que entró como inversor de sus fondos y accionista de la firma. Tanto es así que ha terminado recomprándola e integrándola en el banco, de modo que Oyarzábal entró en la entidad.

“Con estos nombramientos, reforzamos un modelo de asesoramiento que combina la escala y las capacidades globales con la cercanía y el conocimiento del territorio. Partimos de una posición de fortaleza gracias a quienes han liderado nuestras direcciones territoriales durante estos años”, ha afirmado Oyarzábal en ese comunicado.

World.title: Cómo lograr el equilibro entre medio ambiente, sociedad y economía a través de una gestión responsable
World.content:
La estrategia de ElPozo Alimentación se basa en la creación de valor a largo plazo, el desarrollo de las personas y una gestión responsable.

La mayor planta solar fotovoltaica para autoconsumo industrial de España del sector de la alimentación se encuentra en Alhama de Murcia, en la sede central de ElPozo Alimentación. Sus 27,8 MWp suministran el 20% de la electricidad que consume la compañía y contribuyen decisivamente a avanzar en la reducción de sus emisiones de Alcance 2, las que se generan indirectamente por la producción de la energía necesaria para poder operar. Las emisiones directas verificadas de la compañía descendieron un 34% –nueve puntos más del objetivo establecido en su hoja de ruta– gracias a una estrategia de eficiencia energética sustentada en dos iniciativas: la instalación de un sistema de recuperación de calor residual que reutiliza la energía térmica generada en los procesos industriales, y el aprovechamiento de biogás generado en la depuradora para la producción de calor.

Según la base de datos EDGAR (Base de Datos de Emisiones para la Investigación Atmosférica Global), el sistema alimentario representa una parte significativa de las emisiones globales de gases de efecto invernadero. Con esta realidad en mente, ElPozo Alimentación comenzó a analizar toda su cadena de valor y a preguntarse cómo podía optimizar cada etapa productiva. “Nos dimos cuenta de que crecer como empresa tenía que ir de la mano de hacer las cosas mejor”, admite Rafael Fuertes, director general de ElPozo Alimentación.

ElPozo Alimentación cuenta con dos estrellas Lean & Green, concedidas por AECOC (Asociación de Fabricantes y Distribuidores), como reconocimiento por haber reducido más de un 30% las emisiones de su transporte logístico

El proceso arrancó, hace ya años, trabajándose en aspectos muy concretos y con un impacto directo: reducir consumos de agua y energía, minimizar residuos, bajar emisiones y hacer más eficientes los procesos. El agua fue desde el principio un insumo clave. ElPozo Alimentación había nacido, en 1935, como un pequeño negocio familiar en la Región de Murcia, donde este recurso escasea y su gestión se convierte en un desafío especialmente relevante. La empresa, hoy, ha desarrollado un modelo de aprovechamiento circular que permite depurar la totalidad de sus aguas residuales y destinarlas al riego de terrenos próximos a sus instalaciones.

A lo largo de los años, la compañía ha tomado conciencia de que, aprovechando los recursos, gestionaría mejor su actividad. Fue la antesala de la economía circular, modelo en el que hoy desarrolla su actividad. Su tasa de valorización actual roza el 90%, lo que minimiza el volumen de residuos destinados al vertedero. Fue la primera empresa del sector alimentario en obtener la certificación Retray, de la Fundación Ecosense, que garantiza la recuperación del plástico usado en envases de lámina y bandejas de PET. También fue la primera en valorizar el intestino de cerdo para la producción de heparina, a través de Hepabiotic, una joint-venture entre Grupo Fuertes y Horizon Products.

Transparencia y ética

La innovación y la tecnología han jugado un papel fundamental en la optimización de los recursos y la reducción de los impactos ambientales. Pero la clave estriba, a juicio de la compañía, en haber sabido entender que estas políticas generan valor mucho más allá de la eficiencia, el ahorro o la mejora en la gestión. Hasta el punto de haber ido calando, aguas arriba en la organización, hasta llegar a su misma gobernanza. “Impulsamos un modelo basado en la transparencia, la ética empresarial y el cumplimiento de buenas prácticas, alineando la gestión con las expectativas de nuestros grupos de interés”, indica el director general.

La planta fotovoltaica de ElPozo Alimentación genera electricidad para el autoconsumo de sus instalaciones. ELPOZO

“La actividad alimentaria es estratégica, dinámica y comprometida con el futuro, y su crecimiento solo tiene sentido si avanza de forma sostenible. La sostenibilidad no es solo una cuestión ambiental, sino también social y económica, y el equilibrio entre estas tres dimensiones es la clave para seguir evolucionando”, reflexiona Rafael Fuertes. Impulsadas por esta convicción, las políticas ESG han ido creciendo en ElPozo Alimentación indisolublemente unidas a la propia expansión de una marca que hoy exporta a más de 80 países y está presente en millones de hogares españoles.

La firma ha puesto en marcha proyectos como Lab19 y Graduate Program, que “promueven la formación continua y favorecen el crecimiento interno de sus profesionales”. La primera es un laboratorio experimental de inteligencia artificial y tecnologías emergentes creado en sus instalaciones centrales; la segunda, un programa estratégico de captación de talento joven, para recién graduados universitarios o estudiantes de máster con menos de dos años de experiencia profesional. Comunycar, por su parte, es una app corporativa de movilidad para compartir coche y gastos entre compañeros para desplazamientos más sostenibles al trabajo.

ESG de círculos concéntricos

La idea de ElPozo es extender su visión y propósito a proveedores y socios estratégicos. Y a los consumidores, con quienes reafirma su “fuerte compromiso”. En este punto, ElPozo Alimentación ha sido pionera en el sector al adaptar su packaging a la tecnología NaviLens para personas con discapacidad visual. Desde hace una década participa, junto a Acción contra el Hambre, en la campaña Restaurantes contra el Hambre: una iniciativa destinada a facilitar el acceso a la alimentación a colectivos vulnerables. Y apoya a la Fundación Never Surrender con la creación y equipamiento de centros deportivos oncológicos gratuitos para mejorar la calidad de vida de pacientes con cáncer.

“Hemos impulsado proyectos de economía circular, mejora de envases y optimización de procesos. Hemos intensificado nuestra ayuda social y desarrollado buenas prácticas en toda la organización, extendiéndolas a nuestra cadena de valor. Pero, sobre todo, hemos conseguido integrar la sostenibilidad de forma estratégica en toda la compañía como una manera de trabajar”, concluye el director general de ElPozo Alimentación.

World.title: Un amor que no se ve:  el compromiso silencioso de  quienes cuidan de nuestros mayores
World.content:
El estrés afecta a dos de cada tres personas cuidadoras y la ansiedad, a la mitad, según el II Estudio del Observatorio Cinfa de los Cuidados, que analiza las consecuencias de atender a familiares mayores.

El II Estudio del Observatorio Cinfa de los Cuidados analiza el impacto mental, físico y social que el cuidado tiene en la familia, una red de apoyo que sostiene el bienestar de los mayores, con el propósito de ampliar el conocimiento sobre esta realidad en la sociedad española

La primera señal de que algo no iba bien llegó con una inesperada llamada de teléfono de su padre, que necesitaba ayuda para vender su casa del pueblo porque “ya no quería vivir allí”. Cuenta Alba Muñoz (Madrid, 1987) que la pandemia y el confinamiento pudieron desembocar en una espiral de apatía y aislamiento. “Mi padre quería vender su casa y venir a Madrid, pero no teníamos un plan B, ni lo que obtuviera de la venta le permitiría comprar otra. Así que, durante un tiempo, se vino a vivir conmigo y mi marido. Fue cuando empecé a percibir esos cambios, esa apatía, problemas de movilidad… Arrastraba los pies, estaba muy bajo de peso y tenía la vitamina B12 por los suelos. En vez de ir a la cocina, iba al baño con los platos. Estaba despistado. Fuimos al neurólogo, esperamos un año para el PET-TAC y dio positivo en amiloide. Los médicos lo explican como un problema de memoria, un deterioro cognitivo”.

Entre las consecuencias del cuidado, el 69,8% de las personas cuidadoras presenta fatiga, el 50,1% sufre alteraciones del sueño y el 39,3% experimenta cambios de humor e irritabilidad, según el II Estudio del Observatorio Cinfa de los Cuidados

Aquel diagnóstico cambiaría tanto la vida de su padre como la de Alba, que tuvo que reorganizarse y aprender sobre la marcha lo que implica acompañar y cuidar de un ser querido que está perdiendo la memoria, la movilidad, el habla y, en el caso de su padre, también la visión. Con la dificultad añadida de que a sus 70 años, él es consciente de su deterioro pero, al mismo tiempo, quiere vivir de forma autónoma, con apoyo. “Dejé de trabajar dos años mientras me encargaba de todo esto, le ayudaba con papeleos, visitas médicas, centro de día, cuidados… y no es fácil. Ahora estoy embarazada, trabajo y sientes mucha culpa, porque no sabes si lo estás haciendo bien. Tengo días mejores en los que pienso que la vida me está acompañando y otros peores, como cuando me llama mi padre llorando por teléfono y tratas de sostenerle en esa llamada”, reflexiona. Como la de Alba Muñoz, millones de familias en España viven su día a día entre cuidados invisibles para la sociedad. La iniciativa de personas cuidadoras de Cinfa se enmarca en el movimiento por los cuidados que ha desarrollado en los últimos años, como compromiso para mejorar la vida de las familias y reconocer y visibilizar una realidad que en muchas ocasiones pasa desapercibida. Con este objetivo ha lanzado el II Estudio del Observatorio Cinfa de los Cuidados, avalado por la Sociedad Española de Geriatría y Gerontología, que analiza cómo afectan las tareas del cuidado en la salud física, mental y social de quienes asumen esta labor. Es una visión que nace de la escucha, a partir de entrevistas a familiares, que desvela lo positivo y negativo de atravesar una etapa de atender a personas mayores con o sin dependencia.

Nueve de cada diez personas cuidadoras entrevistadas por Cinfa afirman sentirse satisfechas con su rol, a pesar de las consecuencias físicas, psicológicas y la pérdida de relaciones sociales que implica apoyar a seres queridos

“Deseamos saber, desde la empatía y con un enfoque inclusivo, cómo se sienten las personas cuidadoras a todos los niveles y hasta qué grado la experiencia de cuidado ha afectado a su vida cotidiana y salud”, explica la doctora Alicia López de Ocáriz, directora médica de Grupo Cinfa y presidenta del Observatorio. “Compartir sus vivencias permite generar empatía y conciencia social y, en muchos casos, tal y como nos han transmitido, expresar lo vivido transforma la experiencia del cuidado”.

Un desgaste silencioso

El nuevo informe de Cinfa pone de manifiesto que el estrés afecta a dos de cada tres cuidadores familiares y la mitad sufre ansiedad. La fatiga perjudica al 69,8%, las alteraciones del sueño, al 50,1%, y cuatro de cada diez personas cuidadoras (39,3%) sienten cambios de humor e irritabilidad. Síntomas que pasan desapercibidos mientras estas familias siguen cuidando y atendiendo. En silencio, la depresión y la tristeza acompañan al 35,2% de los familiares y casi el 25% sufre dificultades para concentrarse.

Alba Muñoz comparte con su padre actividades cotidianas como salir en bicicleta o ir de compras. Algo que le está permitiendo estrechar su vínculo y enriquecerse con nuevos recuerdos. cinfa

“Una de las cosas que te encuentras cuando un ser querido enferma es la soledad absoluta. No sientes que tengas acompañamiento médico ni emocional; ni para el paciente, ni para los familiares, ni tampoco tenemos un asesoramiento. Sí, nos dicen: ‘haz deporte, come bien y relaciónate’. Pero cada familia es un mundo; no todos tenemos los mismos recursos ni apoyos familiares”, describe Alba Muñoz.

El II Estudio de Cinfa también ha analizado las consecuencias en las relaciones sociales. Nueve de cada diez personas cuidadoras consideran que tienen menos tiempo libre de ocio, descanso o aficiones, mientras que el 30,8% siente que esta responsabilidad ha provocado aislamiento o pérdida de relaciones familiares y amistades. De hecho, el 17,6% siente incomprensión social, el 17,2% desamparo y soledad y dos de cada diez experimentan una pérdida de identidad y autonomía.

A pesar del sacrificio y de todos los síntomas físicos y psicológicos que acompañan a hombres y mujeres cuidadores, la investigación también desvela que casi nueve de cada diez (88%) afirman que se sienten satisfechos con este rol. Alba es una de ellas y asegura que esta etapa le está permitiendo conocer de otra forma a su padre. Incluso se compró una bicicleta de carretera, sin haber montado jamás en ella, para tener una nueva afición en común con él y compartir largas charlas en el camino.

“Ahora paso momentos muy bonitos que quizá no tuve en mi infancia. Esto me da una nueva oportunidad de conocer a mi padre. Hay algo en él que ha cambiado: antes era más una figura de autoridad, poco emocional, pero ahora hablamos desde un lugar muy emotivo, muy vulnerable. Tenemos conversaciones de todo tipo, compartimos cosas como ir de compras juntos, darnos un capricho o comer un bocadillo de calamares. La enfermedad de un ser querido llega y tú decides cómo quieres vivir esa experiencia: yo siento que es un privilegio, porque supone un aprendizaje difícil y doloroso, pero también muy humano”.

¿Cómo se cuidan y con quién hablan las personas cuidadoras? Cerca del 54% de los cuidadores declara que su vida social se ha visto afectada por esta tarea, pero 9 de cada 10 personas cuidadoras se sienten satisfechas con este rol. AUTOCUIDADO 35% desconecta con la televisión, lectura o internet 31,1% dedica su tiempo a familiares y amistades 30,9% practica algún tipo de deporte ENTORNO 65,2% habla de su rol como cuidadora con amistades 53,6% habla de su rol como cuidadora con familiares 27,2% habla de su rol como cuidadora con compañeros/as de trabajo

World.title: La segunda vida de los productos gana terreno en el hogar: recuperar y reutilizar para consumir mejor
World.content:
El alquiler de productos y herramientas del hogar, según Leroy Merlin, cerró el ejercicio de 2025 con un total de 12.500 operaciones, una cifra que supone un incremento del 42% respecto al año anterior.

Leroy Merlin integra la economía circular en su estrategia empresarial mediante el reacondicionamiento y alquiler de productos y la gestión de residuos, cuya tasa de valorización alcanza ya el 85,9%

El grifo del lavabo. El aplique de una pared. El césped artificial de un patio o un azulejo cerámico para el baño. Los productos con los que equipamos nuestros hogares también tienen un impacto ambiental, desde la extracción de materias primas hasta su fabricación, transporte y uso. Prolongar su vida útil o recuperar aquellos que todavía pueden utilizarse se ha convertido en una de las principales vías para avanzar hacia un consumo más eficiente.

En la web y tiendas de Leroy Merlin, cada uno de esos objetos cotidianos recibe una nota gracias a Home Index. Notas de la A a la E, para indicar cuál es el impacto medioambiental y social de cada uno a lo largo de toda su vida útil. Se utilizan para ello treinta criterios divididos en 8 categorías que se puntúan de 0 a 100. El filtro de selección por defecto de la web de Leroy Merlin muestra solo aquellos productos que han obtenido una A o una B, según ese baremo.

Medir el impacto para consumir mejor

“Home Index es un indicador que evalúa el impacto ambiental y social de un producto a lo largo de su ciclo de vida, desde su producción hasta su fin. Actualmente ya hemos formado en España a más de 700 proveedores y hemos calificado más de 150.000 referencias según los criterios del indicador”, explica Cristina Sánchez, directora ejecutiva de Sostenibilidad e Impacto Positivo en Leroy Merlin España. “Una manera muy clara de visualizar este trabajo con los proveedores es a través de un ejemplo: es el caso de la aplicación del ecodiseño en el diseño del estor Charlina, fabricado con un 88% de materia prima reciclada, que cuenta con 5 años de garantía (por encima de lo legal, que son 3 años) y con etiqueta OEKO-TEX”. Repensar y extender la vida de los objetos es clave. España es consciente de ello: según un estudio realizado en 2025 por la Organización de Consumidores y Usuarios (OCU), un 75% de los españoles ya compra, año a año, productos de segunda mano. La cantidad dedicada a este tipo de objetos de segundo uso alcanza los 167 euros anuales por ciudadano, con el hogar y todo lo relacionado con su equipamiento entre las categorías más demandadas.

Artículos expuestos o devueltos

Segunda Vida es el programa que Leroy Merlin ha implantado en todas sus tiendas para recuperar productos de exposición, devoluciones o artículos con pequeños desperfectos que conservan su funcionalidad, y volver a ponerlos a la venta con descuentos que pueden alcanzar entre el 40% y el 50%.

Ampliamos las opciones de nuestros clientes con productos a precios más asequibles, adaptados a diferentes necesidades y presupuestos. Apostamos por un consumo más consciente, tanto por los materiales como por la generación de residuos Cristina Sánchez, directora de Sostenibilidad e Impacto Positivo en Leroy Merlin España

Los españoles están reaccionando a este tipo de productos año a año y el programa Segunda Vida refleja el crecimiento de este modelo de consumo. Tras alcanzar los 3,5 millones de euros en ventas en 2025, la iniciativa ha registrado 5,07 millones de euros hasta septiembre de 2026, con 142.000 productos comercializados; una evolución que muestra cómo la recuperación de artículos puede contribuir tanto a prolongar su vida útil como a generar nuevas oportunidades de negocio.

La compra de artículos identificados como 'Segunda Vida' permite al cliente ahorrar y contribuir al mismo tiempo a un consumo más eficiente. RALF PASCUAL

Desde la compañía aseguran que esta estrategia no es una alternativa para quien no puede adquirir un producto nuevo. Se trata de eliminar el estigma de los productos ya usados: “Los resultados alcanzados demuestran que existe un interés real por este tipo de soluciones y que la circularidad también puede convertirse en un motor de competitividad y de negocio, capaz de generar valor para nuestros clientes, para la compañía y para el entorno”.

Pero Segunda Vida es solo uno de los programas de la estrategia desplegada por la marca, dentro del plan de acción Make It Positive, del grupo ADEO, en el que se incluye la compañía. Cristina Sánchez resume el reto que plantea la sostenibilidad: “Para lograr una economía más justa y sostenible existe un consenso cada vez más amplio sobre la necesidad de acelerar la transformación de las organizaciones”. En esa dirección avanzan dos de las iniciativas de Leroy Merlin, centradas en dar una segunda vida a los productos y reducir los residuos que genera su ciclo de consumo.

Por otra parte, el alquiler de productos y herramientas ha experimentado también, según la compañía, un fuerte crecimiento. En 2025 aumentó un 42% respecto al año anterior, llegando a las 12.500 operaciones; se trata de alquiler de utensilios por un tiempo limitado, sin que el cliente llegue a adquirirlos. “Nuestro objetivo es que las alternativas circulares estén alineadas con las tendencias de consumo y las preferencias de los clientes, garantizando así la libertad de elección entre comprar un producto nuevo, recuperar uno que conserva toda su funcionalidad o alquilar aquello que solo se necesite utilizar para usos ocasionales o concretos”, destaca la directora de Sostenibilidad e Impacto Positivo de la compañía.

Menos residuos

La gestión de los residuos constituye, finalmente, otro de los pilares de esta estrategia. No se trata únicamente de recuperar artículos que todavía pueden utilizarse, sino también de mejorar el tratamiento de aquellos materiales que han llegado al final de su vida útil.

En este ámbito, Leroy Merlin alcanzó en 2025 una tasa de valorización de residuos del 85,9% en sus tiendas y almacenes. Este indicador refleja el esfuerzo por reincorporar materiales al circuito productivo en lugar de destinarlos a eliminación, y completa un modelo de actuación que incluye tanto la prevención de residuos como su aprovechamiento cuando ya se han generado.

World.title: Judges say no requirement to help Gazans travel to NL
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The Netherlands is not required to provide consular services to Gazans who are unable to travel abroad to obtain Dutch entry visas, a judge ruled on Friday.

The case revolves around 111 people currently living in Gaza who have been granted entry visas to the Netherlands.

Documents must be picked up in person and the Dutch have no consular presence in the enclave, so people have to travel abroad to obtain their visas.

The lawsuit argued that it is nearly impossible for Gazans to travel to Jordan to get their visas and the Dutch have an obligation to assist them in travelling to the embassy.

A judge at the District Court of The Hague disagreed, ruling that “there is no entitlement to consular assistance.”

The decision noted that the outcome would hit the plaintiffs hard, but “the decision to help the plaintiffs in Gaza is reserved for the political sphere and not for the court.”

World.title: VVD ministers rally round Yesilgöz ahead of party congress
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Members of the right-wing liberal VVD party have flocked to defend their leader Dilan Yesilgöz after mounting criticism of her leadership and her dual status as party leader and defence minister, as well as the recent cabinet crisis, led to speculation she could be ousted, ahead of the party’s congress on Saturday.

Prime minister Rob Jetten, whose minority cabinet was on the brink of collapse earlier this month after Yesilgöz described the government as a “failed experiment”, also spoke in favour of her on Friday, saying “I have every confidence that her fighting spirit will serve her well at the congress”, according to Het Parool.

The VVD’s former chair Christianne van der Wal spoke on TV talk show Pauw & De Wit earlier this week saying that there was “enormous discontent” within the party rank and file, but that loyalty kept criticism largely under wraps. She said that Yesilgöz’s dual role was a particular point of contention.

But Jetten said this is perfectly normal in Dutch politics and that her roles are well compatible.

The criticism levelled by Van der Wal led to doubts over Yesilgöz’s continued leadership in the build-up to Saturday’s VVD congress, where party issues will be discussed after a turbulent few weeks.

The Volkskrant also reported that VVD members are concerned about the provincial elections next March.

Despite the media pressure building around Yesilgöz, Friday’s cabinet meeting saw VVD members come out in support of her.

“I know no one who works harder than she does,” infrastructure minister Vincent Karremans said.

“I work closely with Dilan and I think she combines her various roles well,” health minister Sophie Hermans told the Volkskrant.

Yesilgöz avoided the press and gave no comment after Friday’s meeting, NOS said.

World.title: Dutch destinations: an autumn getaway in Middelburg, Zeeland
World.content:
The Dutch flock to Zeeland in the summer to take advantage of the wide beaches, the seafood and hopefully the sunshine. But it is also a great location for an autumn or winter break, with the provincial capital Middelburg making the perfect base.

Middelburg, on the former island of Walcheren, can trace its history back to 880 and was awarded city rights in 1217, making it nearly 100 years older than Amsterdam.

In 1585 Middelburg opened its gates to refugees after the fall of Antwerp in the Eighty Years’ War with Spain, and the Flemish influence is still palpable in some of the architecture. In 1705 the first chocolate mill was set up on the outskirts of the city and its railway station opened in 1872.

Today its medieval centre is elegant, compact and well worth a wander around. Check out the names of the houses along the Rotterdamsekaai and the area around the magnificent Oostkerk, which now hosts concerts, and you will see plenty of testimonials to its past. We spotted an Edinburg and an Edenberg, a Groot Brittangie, a Spaerpot (piggy bank) and a strangely named “de twee harde Bollen” among the signage.

Five things to do

Stroll through the Abdij

Middelburg’s centre is dominated by its abbey, an impressive complex of buildings, with a garden, various towers and a wide, tree-filled square which is used to host cultural events. The abbey dates back to 1100 when the first parts were built by the Norbertine monks. Today it is home to the provincial council offices and the Zeeuws Museum. Note, the Lange Jan tower is closed to the public for the winter season.

Visit a museum

The Zeeuws Museum is one of our favourite provincial museums because it does not overwhelm you with information and is happily lacking in infotainment. The first two floors are devoted to temporary exhibitions and the third floor focuses on the history of the province. Carefully selected objects – children’s cloth caps, pottery, portraits of notables – nod to important stages in the city’s past.

The top floor has three “cabinets of curiosities” compiled from the museum’s collection such as the skeleton of a cat coupled with pottery moggies from 1850. It’s easy to cover the entire museum in a couple of hours.

Catch up on Christmas shopping

Middelburg has a main drag full of the brands you would expect, interspersed with local stores and a number of specialty outlets such as a store selling kites and juggler’s equipment. There are several chocolate specialists to choose from and wine shops selling local Zeeland wine.

For souvenirs, pick up some Zeeuwse bolus – a sticky spiral pastry with cinnamon and dark brown sugar or a packet of Boterbabbelaar, a buttery sort of toffee.

Walk in the woods

De Manteling is a coastal nature reserve near the seaside resort of Domburg, some 15 minutes’ drive from Middelburg. It is based around several former country estates, the main one of which is now a youth hostel. There are several routes to follow winding through the oak forest, and the blue one, which is four kilometres long, will take you out to the beach.

Visit Veere

Only 10 minutes from Middelburg by car, the village of Veere used to be open to the sea, and its wealth stems from its position as a major port in the wool trade with Scotland back in the 15th century. The splendid Schotse Huizen museum on the waterfront is well worth a visit and goes into this history in more detail. Veere gets very busy with coach parties in the summer.

Where to eat

Middelburg has masses of places to eat, and you would be advised to book if you plan to have dinner in one of the more highly-rated places. Lots of cafés and restaurants are based around the main market square, where you can get a burger, ribs or local fish. The Herberg is a favourite with the locals and offers more adventurous fare. You’ll find more choice on the Dam next to the abbey.

We had lunch at Brasserie 1600 which was pretty standard for a Dutch café lunch – croquettes on bread, warm goat’s cheese broodjes – but cheaper than the big cities and with friendlier staff.

In the evening we ate at the Packhuys on the Kinderdijk which offers an interesting seafood-based tasting menu of four to seven courses in a converted warehouse. Restaurant Scherp is in a city centre townhouse and also has two rooms where guests can stay. Basalt also comes highly recommended.

Where to stay

There are lots of options in Middelburg but you would do well to book up in plenty of time for your trip if you are coming at the weekend. It’s a popular place.

We stayed in a “city loft” in Hotel St Joris, which originally dates from 1582 and is close to the abbey walls, and paid €156 for the night including breakfast by booking directly. Ask for a room on the first two floors if you are not good with stairs. The nearby Poorthuys B&B comes highly recommended, as does the Zilver Reiger.

How to get there

It takes about two hours to reach Middelburg by car from Amsterdam, depending on the traffic, and there is plenty of parking on the edge of town. Inner city parking is pricey and nothing is far away on foot. There are regular trains from Amsterdam and The Hague, and you can pick up an OV-fiets (bike) at the station if you want to explore the countryside.

Anything else

When we were in Middelburg, in late November, the Stadhuis, or town hall, was wrapped in scaffolding as part of a major renovation project. The main market square had also been filled with an artificial ice rink and the café terraces had been turned into ski chalets for the winter season.

World.title: Prosecutors open investigation into neo-Nazi cage fights
World.content:
The prosecution service has begun an investigation into the neo-Nazi events that were exposed by a Zembla documentary last week, in which politicians, teachers and a health care professionals were seen attending cage fighting tournaments organised by extreme-right groups.

Since the documentary was released, which was based on an undercover investigation, six members of the far-right FVD have been expelled from the party.

A Rotterdam lecturer who acted as a medic, a high school teacher and a psychiatrist were also identified. The psychiatrist has also worked as an expert witness in judicial cases and previously had a firearms licence.

The footage shows members repeatedly throwing up Nazi salutes and shouting Sieg Heil, and members of one group holding an annual commemoration for Adolf Hitler in Luxembourg.

The former chief of the Dutch national intelligence agency AIVD, Rob Bertholee, told news programme Nieuwsuur that the groups and neo-Nazi symbols should be banned. The issue is that they were held as private events. Public displays of Nazi symbology can be punished in some cases.

Bertholee also said investigating connections between political parties and neo-Nazi organisations is complicated. Individuals can be held to account but investigating inherent links with entire political organisations, as some have called for with the FVD, would be sensitive.

A total ban would be easier said than done because of freedom of speech, he said, but he also voiced concerns that the far-right ideology is spreading throughout society. “We used to associate the far right with skinheads. We know now: people who adhere to this ideology look like anyone and can practice any profession.”

World.title: Abattoirs face closure for threatening and abusing inspectors
World.content:
Junior agriculture minister Silvio Erkens wants start shutting down slaughterhouses if inspectors are threatened there. This follows revelations recently that food safety authority workers are afraid to inspect some abattoirs because of the violence and intimidation they face.

Erkens told MPs during Wednesday’s debate on the agriculture budget that one option was a three-strikes principle, under which a slaughterhouse could be closed after, for example, three violations, broadcaster NOS reported.

“There should be no place in the Netherlands for slaughterhouses like this,” he said, though he did not name any particular culprits.

In the debate, Erkens said inspectors had reported intimidating phone calls, threats and being followed, sometimes by someone with a guard dog, and in some cases even into the toilet. Staff had also faced discrimination, physical aggression, and sexual intimidation, and some had been targeted in their private lives along with their families.

“It happens too often and too widely,” Erkens said, adding that these were not isolated incidents. He declined to name the slaughterhouses involved.

The NVWA can already halt slaughter at a plant until a problem is resolved. Erkens said that made sense for a single incident, but that a pattern called for a permanent solution.

MPs from left-wing PRO, the anti-immigration PVV, the Party for the Animals (PvdD), and centrist D66 had urged him the day before to take tougher action rather than rely on talks with the meat industry. Erkens said appealing to the sector had not worked.

He said he would set out early next year whether the legislation will go ahead and how it would work.

“A rebel with a strong cause.” That’s how prince Constantijn described Ghanaian artist and poet kąrî’kạchä seid’ou when presenting the Prince Claus Fund 2026 Impact Award on Thursday.

Set up in 1996 as a 70th birthday gift for the late husband of princess Beatrix, the fund awards international artists and creators in places “where cultural expression is under pressure”.

“Known for his radical and democratic approaches to artistic practice and teaching, seid’ou has been a key catalyst for artistic innovation in Ghana and across West Africa since the early 1990s,” the fund said.

According to NOS, seid’ou, who was born in 1968, does not believe that art needs to meet any conditions, and is less concerned with exhibitions or sales than with how artists are trained.

seid’ou travelled outside the African continent for the first time to accept his 50,000 euros during a ceremony in Amsterdam.

He “works with quiet discretion, preferring to remain out of the limelight while working from his base in Kumasi,” the fund said.

World.title: November set to be coldest in almost 30 years after record night
World.content:
This November is on course to be the coldest in the Netherlands since 1998, after many weather stations recorded their coldest November 27 night on record, broadcaster NOS reported on Friday.

The temperature in Twente dropped to -8.1° overnight, and 26 other stations also set a new cold record for the date, NOS said.

The month has had an unusually high number of frost nights. The normal November average is around 7°, according to weather forecaster Weerplaza.

Temperatures will stay around or just above freezing on Friday, with sunshine all day and a moderate easterly wind. In some places the temperature may not rise above zero at all.

The cold has made natural ice skating possible in several places. The first marathon on natural ice was held in Winterswijk on Thursday evening, won by Jade Groenewoud in the women’s race and Christiaan Haasjes in the men’s.

Friday night will be cold again, with lows of -4° to -7°. Temperatures will rise slightly on Saturday and there will be more cloud. Sunday will be wet, with highs of 2° to 5°, and the rain may start as wet snow.

A mural appeared on the outer wall of the Dutch embassy in Moscow on Thursday, depicting flying missiles with the words “flowers of Dutch diplomacy” written in their blast trail.

The mural, for which no one has claimed responsibility, appeared days after the dispute over Dutch defence company Destinus, who publicised the use of its weapons on the Crimea bridge.

The Russian embassy in The Hague was quick to respond that staff from the company may be considered legitimate military targets if so and asked if The Hague was “joining the conflict”.

A subsequent investigation by the NRC found that Destinus employees may have been personally engaging in drone battles.

Shortly after, the Dutch embassy in Kyiv was struck during a barrage of drone strikes. Whether the building was an intended target remains unclear.

Prime minister Rob Jetten said the Netherlands would not be intimidated by Russian threats.

The Russian embassy has lodged a formal request for clarification over the involvement of Destinus staff in the conflict.

World.title: President vetoes Polish government’s middle-class tax cuts
World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. President Karol Nawrocki has vetoed a government bill that would have lowered income tax for millions of people earning around or slightly above average salaries, while increasing taxes on large companies and the highest earners. Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, argued that the income-tax cut would benefit only a small minority of workers, while the changes to corporate taxes would disproportionately affect Polish businesses, as international corporations could move profits abroad. The government, however, rejected Nawrocki’s reasoning, accusing the president of siding with large corporations at the expense of ordinary working Poles. ❌ Prezydent RP Karol Nawrocki zawetował ustawę o reformie podatkowej. pic.twitter.com/tvXCVKnTMs — Kancelaria Prezydenta RP (@prezydentpl) November 27, 2026 The legislation, which was due to come into force in 2027 – an election year – would have adjusted the income tax brackets, including an increase in the earnings threshold at which the lowest rate of income tax is paid and the introduction of a new rate between the lowest and highest earnings brackets. Currently, there are two income tax brackets: the first taxes earnings of up to 120,000 zloty (around €26,850) at a rate of 12%; the second taxes earnings above that level at a rate of 32%. There is also a tax-free allowance for earnings of up to 30,000 zloty. Meanwhile, anyone who earns more than 1 million zloty a year pays an additional “solidarity levy” (effectively a third tax bracket) of 4% on income above that amount. Under the new proposals, the threshold for the first 12% tax bracket would be raised to 130,000 zloty. For earnings between 130,000 and 150,000 zloty, a new tax bracket of 24% would be introduced. Then earnings above 150,000 would be taxed at 32%. According to the government’s estimates, 3.5 million workers would benefit from the reform. However, Nawrocki said that this means around nine out of every ten taxpayers would not benefit. He also claimed that in practice the reform “This bill divides citizens. It gives to a few, while taking away from the majority,” said Nawrocki in a video published on social media. The president also noted that the government had failed to deliver on its promise, made when coming to power in 2023, to double the tax-free income allowance to 60,000 zloty, a change that would have benefited a much broader group of taxpayers, including the lowest earners. According to figures from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, average monthly earnings at companies employing more than nine people were 9,405.19 zloty in October this year, the equivalent of almost 113,000 zloty a year. The Polish government has approved a final version of the state budget for 2027, including planned middle-class tax cuts funded by higher rates on the richest. The budget act and associated legislation still need approval from parliament and the president https://t.co/I2Gz0h6cHd — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 29, 2026 To finance the proposed relief, the legislation also included an increase in the corporate income tax (CIT) rate from 19% to 22% for companies and tax groups generating annual revenues above €50 million. The solidarity levy paid by highest-earners would have also increased to 5%, while the earnings limit for qualifying for a simplified lump-sum tax on gross business revenue – commonly used by professionals such as lawyers, IT specialists and healthcare workers – would be lowered from €2 million a year to €250,000. Nawrocki criticised the government for making the “entry into force of the tax relief contingent upon the simultaneous implementation of tax hikes.” He said that the higher corporate tax would disproportionately fall on “Polish, growing firms,” while “foreign ones will move their profits to other countries”. Credit rating agency S&P has revised Poland’s outlook to negative. It notes that the country has seen "one of the most significant fiscal deteriorations globally", while "political polarisation" and "institutional tensions" make consolidation unlikely https://t.co/2Nix7R6Pjj — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 7, 2026 Finance minister Andrzej Domański condemned Nawrocki’s veto, saying that he had taken “the side of large corporations rather than the Polish people”. “Only the Grinch and the Nawrocki can steal people’s money right before Christmas,” wrote Prime Minister Donald Tusk on social media. However, Nawrocki’s veto was welcomed by the right-wing opposition. Sławomir Mentzen, a leader of the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja), praised the president for blocking what he described as “another government attempt to harm Polish businesses”. Mariusz Błaszczak, a deputy leader of the national-conservative Law and Justice, said that his party wanted to raise the second income tax thresshold from 120,000 to 180,000 zloty, but “without introducing any hidden tax increases”. Weto Prezydenta Nawrockiego pozbawia 3,5 mln Polaków obniżki podatków. To nawet 7200 zł rocznie, które mogły zostać w budżecie ciężko pracujących rodzin. Prezydent ponownie stanął po stronie wielkich koncernów, a nie po stronie Polaków. Wstyd. — Andrzej Domański (@Domanski_Andrz) November 27, 2026 According to the government’s own estimates, the bill was expected to generate a net gain of 2.6 billion zloty for the public finance sector in its first year of implementation. Over the following 10 years, the cumulative net gain was projected to reach 50.7 billion zloty. Nawrocki’s veto could therefore make it more difficult for the government to tackle Poland’s fiscal problems, which have seen public debt rise to record levels on the back of ballooning budget deficits. Last year’s deficit, at 7.3% of GDP, was the second-highest in the European Union. This year it is forecast to drop slightly, to 6.7%, according to recent finance ministry projections. But next year’s budget foresees a deficit of 7.1%. The big three global credit rating agencies have all either lowered Poland’s rating or shifted its outlook to negative, citing its recent fiscal deterioration combined with political gridlock between the government and Nawrocki, who has vetoed a record number of bills. World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland’s defence ministry has signed a $300 million (1.2 billion zloty) deal with US data integration and analytics firm Palantir for use of its Maven Smart System, an AI-powered software platform for battlefield analysis and decision-making Defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz says that the system will help Poland “build a modern army, ready for the challenges of the future”. He has also confirmed all servers and data will remain in the possession of the Polish armed forces. We are extremely proud to stand with Poland and support its undisputed leadership in defending a free, safe, and sovereign Europe. Maven Smart System is universally recognized as the vanguard of next-generation AI warfare. And we are honored that Poland is adopting Maven Smart… https://t.co/b8MCLypIea — Palantir (@PalantirTech) November 27, 2026 Poland has signed a five-year contract for Maven, whose other users include the US military and NATO’s Allied Command Operations. Ukraine has also developed its own equivalent of the system and has collaborated with Palantir. The system, which grew out of Project Maven, a programme initiated by the US Department of Defence in 2017, uses machine learning to integrate and analyse various sources of data for military operations. The software is advertised as supporting military “command and control” functions, aiding in identifying military targets and helping manage battlefield information. “This is one of the biggest steps in the transformation of our armed forces,” declared Kosiniak-Kamysz. He said that Maven would benefit all branches of the armed forces and help “build the best capabilities”, adding that “it is impossible to build the Polish army today without artificial intelligence”. Palantir has faced criticism from some quarters due to concerns over its role in expanding governments’ use of sensitive data, as well as over its work relating to immigration enforcement in the United States and Israel’s military operations in Gaza. However, Kosiniak-Kamysz assured that Poland would “hold all the tools and all the keys in our hands”, including maintaining possession of servers and data. He added that he believed there had “never been a more thoroughly analysed agreement” signed by the defence ministry and said that no European providers were able to offer the same capabilities. Kosiniak-Kamysz also emphasised that NATO has already integrated Maven into its military exercises, so the new agreement with Palantir would “bring us closer to NATO and improve our position in the alliance”. Palantir CEO Alex Karp, who was present at today’s signing, also addressed potential opposition to the contract. “There will always be someone who opposes Palantir,” he said, according to a Polish translation of his remarks. “But it is Poland’s enemies who shout loudest against Palantir…They spend a lot on propaganda, persuading useful idiots that good solutions are unnecessary and that bad ones are good.” Palantir registered a Polish subsidiary a decade ago and has since grown its Warsaw office. Last year, the defence ministry signed a letter of intent with the firm on strengthening cooperation on AI, cybersecurity and information technology. Poland and the US have signed an agreement on defence research, development, testing and evaluation, concluding 17 years of negotiations and opening the way for deeper cooperation on military technology https://t.co/rCHzK00Pwa — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 24, 2026 Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Poland has rapidly and significantly ramped up defence spending to some of the highest relative levels in NATO. It was the alliance’s biggest importer of arms between 2021 and 2025, with 44% of that equipment coming from the US. Last week, Poland and the US signed an agreement on defence research, development, testing and evaluation, opening the way for deeper technological cooperation. Earlier this month, Polish defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth signed a declaration on expanding bilateral defence-industrial cooperation Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland releases international expert findings that Smolensk air disaster was an accident
World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Polish prosecutors have published findings by international experts that the 2010 Smolensk air disaster in Russia that killed President Lech Kaczyński and 95 others was an accident caused by a series of human errors. The findings contradict claims by the opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party, which is led by Lech’s identical twin brother Jarosław Kaczyński, that the crash was caused deliberately by Russia. PiS figures have claimed that today’s announcement was a “manipulation” that omits key facts. Według Międzynarodowego Zespołu Biegłych katastrofa samolotu Tu-154M z 10 kwietnia 2010 r. była następstwem ciągu zdarzeń podczas końcowego podejścia do lądowania na lotnisku Smoleńsk Północny, w tym niestabilnego podejścia do lądowania, błędnej oceny rzeczywistej wysokości… — Prokuratura (@PK_GOV_PL) November 27, 2026 The international team of experts was, in fact, first appointed in 2019 under the then-PiS government, which ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023. During that time, it launched various new investigations into the Smolensk tragedy. PiS has always rejected the findings of official Polish and Russian investigations into the crash, which found it to have been an accident. It has also accused the Polish government that was in power in 2010 – then, as now, led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk – of helping to cover up the true causes. In its announcement today, the National Prosecutor’s Office said that the team of 22 experts – which included individuals from the US, UK, Hungary, Denmark and Ireland, as well as Poland itself, none of whom were named – analysed a wide range of information relating to the crash. That included photographs, audio recordings, laboratory test results and written documentation. The experts did not, however, have access to the wreckage of the plane – which Russia has refused to hand over – or the crash site itself. The experts found that the aircraft had descended too quickly and too far in its approach to Smolensk amid very difficult weather conditions, including heavy fog. Around 15 seconds before the crash, the plane’s commander decided to abort the landing, but the aircraft’s left wing then struck a birch tree, causing the plane to roll sharply. It then “collided with further terrain obstacles” before hitting the ground short of the runway. “According to the experts, the course of the disaster was consistent with a Controlled Flight Into Terrain (CFIT) event,” wrote the prosecutors. “This is a type of aviation accident in which a technically sound aircraft, under the control of the crew, inadvertently collides with terrain or an obstacle.” Among the contributory factors identified by the experts were the crew initiating the landing descent too late, incorrectly assessing the plane’s altitude during the approach, and failing to abort the landing early enough. The experts also identified failings from Russian air-traffic controllers, who wrongly told the crew that the aircraft was maintaining a correct heading and descent path when, in fact, it was to the left of the correct approach and its descent was unstable. A court in Poland has ordered the arrest of a Russian air traffic controller accused of intentional actions that caused the crash at Smolensk in 2010 which killed President Lech Kaczyński and 95 others. Russia has so far refused to cooperate in the case https://t.co/dYxyiRHk3B — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 20, 2022 The experts also found that there had been failings on the Polish side, including the selection of Smolensk North Airport for the landing and various irregularities and a lack of relevant experience in the air force unit assigned to oversee the flight. They also noted that cockpit recordings indicated the voices of individuals other than the crew in the cockpit, which could have distracted the pilots. However, they said that they could not confirm if any of these individuals was President Kaczyński himself. Significantly, prosecutors say that the experts found “no evidence of an explosion” on board the aircraft before it crashed. PiS has regularly suggested that explosives were used to bring down the plane.” A court has ordered Antoni Macierewicz, deputy leader of opposition party PiS, to apologise to @donaldtusk and two of his ministers, @sikorskiradek and @TomaszSiemoniak, for accusing them of “hiding the perpetrators” of the 2010 Smolensk plane crash https://t.co/6p0VmlhV0o — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 2, 2024 Commenting on the findings, Tusk said that they confirmed the earlier official investigations. Those were “questioned for purely political reasons” by Jarosław Kaczyński and PiS deputy leader Antoni Macierewicz, who has been the chief proponent of conspiracy theories around the Smolensk crash, he added. “They destroyed public life with these accusations of an attack [on the plane] in which I was allegedly involved,” declared Tusk, saying that PiS had turned “the nightmare in Smolensk” into a “political charade”. “I am convinced that the PiS leadership, especially Macierewicz but also Kaczyński, who tries to fan the flames of hatred, should pay a very high price for this, also for the sake of the memory of those who died,” concluded the prime minister, quoted by Polsat News. In 2022, for example, Jarosław Kaczyński said that the decision to bring down the plane carrying his brother was made “at the highest level of the Kremlin” and that Tusk’s government “covered up” the incident as part of a “macabre reconciliation with Russia”. Smolensk was an “attack decided at the highest level of the Kremlin”, says Jarosław Kaczyński ahead of the 12th anniversary of the crash. Donald Tusk's government then “covered up” the incident as part of a “macabre reconciliation with Russia”, he adds https://t.co/5ae0gHJj3B — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 4, 2022 At the time of writing, Kaczyński had not commented on today’s announcement by prosecutors. However, it was strongly criticised by other leading PiS figures. Małgorzata Wassermann, a PiS MP whose father, Zbigniew, also a PiS MP, died in the Smolensk crash, accused prosecutors of “clumsily presenting a version of events” that was based on “significant manipulation”. She said that, without an inspection of the crash site being carried out, the findings were unreliable. Meanwhile, Macierewicz himself attended the prosecutors’ announcement of the expert findings today, where he accused them of omitting key findings that did not fit their narrative. When PiS was in power, Macierewicz led the main investigatory commission that was tasked with re-examining the causes of the crash. However, despite spending almost eight years and millions of zloty, it failed to produce any conclusive evidence to support Macierewicz’s claims that the plane was deliberately brought down Macierewicz o ekspertach: Żaden z nich nie był w Smoleńsku! Dziennikarz: A pan był? Macierewicz: Nie, ja akurat nie byłem w Smoleńsku. Kurtyna. pic.twitter.com/QzbtKOKy6f — Aneta ObserwatorXY ® (@ObserwatorXY) November 27, 2026 After Tusk’s government came to power in December 2023, one of its first actions was to abolish Macierewicz’s commission. The following year, it published findings indicating major irregularities in how the PiS government had investigated Smolensk. In August this year, prosecutors announced that they had ended a decade-long investigation into whether Tusk’s earlier government had been guilty of the crime of “diplomatic treason” in its response to the Smolensk crash. The government-backed judges who have taken control of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) have issued a decision suspending chief justice Bogdan Święczkowski, who was appointed to the tribunal under the former government, for 12 months. The news was welcomed by justice minister Waldemar Żurek. However, Święczkowski has rejected the validity of the decision, saying that the “robed usurpers” currently claiming control over the TK are acting unlawfully. Szanujemy decyzje niezależnych instytucji, bo dokładnie na tym polega przywracanie praworządności. Sąd dyscyplinarny TK zawiesił Bogdana Święczkowskiego na 12 miesięcy za bezprawne blokowanie sędziów wybranych przez Sejm. Skończył się czas prywatnego folwarku, który chronił… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 26, 2026 The move marks the latest twist in a long-running battle for control over the TK, which dates back a decade to the unlawful appointment to the court of three judges under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. As a result, Tusk’s centrist government, which took power from PiS in 2023, had effectively ignored the court and its rulings until this year, when it began appointing new judges to fill a growing number of vacancies on the TK’s 15-person bench. However, opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki has refused to swear in five of the eight judges chosen by Tusk’s coalition in parliament, citing concerns over their qualifications or method of appointment. Events came to a head on 30 October, when those eight judges seized control of the court and announced that Święczkowski had been provisionally suspended for a month. Święczkowski, backed by Nawrocki and PiS, rejected their actions as an illegal “coup d’état” and maintains he is the rightful head of the court. On 3 November, the eight government-backed judges held their first general assembly. It was boycotted by the TK’s seven other judges, including Święczkowski, who were all appointed to the tribunal when PiS was in power. The general assembly approved moving forward with disciplinary proceedings against Święczkowski for alleged violations of his duties in leading the court, including refusing to accept the five judges chosen by parliament but whom Nawrocki has refused to swear in. On Thursday this week, the TK’s disciplinary court, made up of three government-backed judges, issued a decision to suspend Święczkowski for 12 months, saying that it would provide time for the disciplinary proceedings against Święczkowski to be fully resolved. A lawyer representing Święczkowski told the hearing that the disciplinary court was improperly convened, noting that two of the three judges had not sworn their oath before the president. He also said that the entire takeover of the TK and subsequent decisions made by it were unlawful, reports Gazeta Wyborcza. The International Commission of Jurists has criticised the takeover of Poland’s constitutional court, saying it “contravenes international standards on the independence of the judiciary” But it also criticised the president for refusing to swear in judges https://t.co/2kBv3GT20d — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 4, 2026 Święczkowski, who did not attend the hearing, afterwards condemned the entire process, calling the judges involved “usurpers dressed in robes” and saying that “the decisions of this body are illegal and have no legal effect”. He also argued that they had violated the basic judicial principle of judges not being permitted to rule on their own cases, given that the disciplinary proceedings against him concerned his refusal to accept judges not sworn in by Nawrocki, two of whom were on the disciplinary panel. The TK’s decision was, however, welcomed by Żurek, the justice minister, who said that it was another step in “the tribunal returning to serving the public” rather than being Święczkowski’s “private fiefdom”. Prezes @TK_GOV_PL Bogdan Święczkowski: Nemo iudex in causa sua – nikt nie może być sędzią we własnej sprawie. Tego uczą na pierwszym roku prawa. Przebrani w togi uzurpatorzy nie odrobili nawet tej lekcji. Nie wyłączyli się od orzekania w sprawie, która dotyczy ich samych. A… — Weronika Ścibor (@WeronikaScibor) November 26, 2026 Separately, the judges currently controlling the TK last week also approved requests from Żurek, in his role as prosecutor general, to lift Święczkowski’s immunity so that he can face charges over alleged crimes committed while heading the TK and previously serving as a senior prosecutor under the PiS government. However, Święczkowski’s position was effectively endorsed last week by the Supreme Court – a separate body from the TK – which issued a resolution stating that TK judges are only legitimate if sworn in by the president. The government has rejected the legitimacy of that resolution itself given that it was issued by Supreme Court judges who were themselves appointed unlawfully. Meanwhile, earlier this week the government moved to restore funding to the TK after its accounts were frozen at the central bank, whose governor, Adam Glapiński, was appointed under PiS and is a close associate of the party’s leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. World.title: Court overturns Warsaw mayor’s ban on protest outside Constitutional Tribunal
World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A court has overturned the mayor of Warsaw’s decision to ban the ongoing demonstration taking place outside the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) in protest against the takeover of the TK by a group of government-backed judges. While the mayor, who is a deputy leader of Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party, argued that the gathering threatened public safety, Warsaw’s district court found that banning it completely was too “radical” a step. Sąd uchylił decyzję stołecznego ratusza odmawiającą przedłużenia zgody na zgromadzenie pod TK#PAPinformacje pic.twitter.com/kBLm9kT9vc — Polska Agencja Prasowa/Polish Press Agency (PAP) (@PAPinformacje) November 26, 2026 Protesters have been present in front of the TK since mid-September, fearing that the government would make a move to take control of the tribunal from its chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, who was appointed to the court under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. On 30 October, a group of eight judges appointed to the TK this year by Tusk’s parliamentary majority – but five of whom opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki has refused to swear in – did indeed seize control of the tribunal and announced that Święczkowski had been suspended. They avoided the demonstrators who were blocking the tribunal’s main gate by entering through a side entrance that leads in from the prime minister’s chancellery. On Wednesday this week, city hall announced that mayor Rafał Trzaskowski had refused a request from the organiser of the protest for the public gathering in front of the TK to be allowed to continue from the end of November through to early January. The municipal authorities said that the demonstration had blocked the busy road outside the tribunal, thereby hindering access for emergency vehicles. They also pointed to a number of “dangerous incidents”, including aggression towards the police by participants in the protest. Such developments “have caused the gathering to lose its peaceful character”, wrote city hall. There are also “grounds to assume that the intention is, in effect, a long-term blockade of the entrance to the Constitutional Tribunal and the street itself”. The mayor’s decision was condemned by the opposition, with PiS party leader Jarosław Kaczyński calling it “authoritarianism in its purest form” and a “trampling of citizens’ constitutional rights” to freedom of assembly and speech. Warsaw's mayor, who is deputy leader of Poland's main ruling party, has refused permission for opposition protests outside the constitutional court to continue, saying they threaten public safety. The opposition has condemned the "authoritarian" decision https://t.co/b6fIsqXzDH — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 25, 2026 The organisers of the gathering had the right to appeal the decision within 24 hours, which they exercised. And late on Thursday, Warsaw’s district court announced that it had overturned Trzaskowski’s prohibition of the gathering. The information provided by city hall “does not provide grounds to assume that the assembly violates the rules for organising assemblies and may pose a threat to people’s life or health or to property to a significant extent”, found judge Anna Bonkowska-Kubek. “The court holds the view that the most radical measures in the form of a ban on demonstrations can only be applied in very exceptional cases, and the authorities must always first consider actions and decisions that would enable the peaceful holding of the planned assembly,” she added. A prohibition of a gathering “can only be applied in absolute exceptional circumstances, and the authorities must always first consider actions and decisions that would enable the peaceful holding of the planned assembly”, said the judge. Bezprawna decyzja prezydenta Warszawy Rafała Trzaskowskiego zakazująca zgromadzenia przed Trybunałem Konstytucyjnym uchylona przez sąd! Kolejni sędziowie nie chcą ochraniać nielegalnych decyzji polityków Koalicji Obywatelskiej, a tym samym żyrować ich swoim nazwiskiem. To… — Jarosław Kaczyński (@OficjalnyJK) November 26, 2026 The court’s ruling was welcomed by Kaczyński, who said that it showed how “judges are refusing to protect the illegal decisions of Civic Coalition politicians”. He called on supporters to join him for a further protest outside the TK at 3 p.m. on Sunday. However, Bonkowska-Kubek’s decision was questioned by Tusk’s justice minister, Waldemar Żurek. “I’m always a supporter of freedom of speech and the right to protest,” he told broadcaster RMF on Friday morning. “However, I would very much like the court to approach this rationally.” Żurek said that, due to the effective blockade of the TK by the demonstrators, it is not possible for people to exercise their right to file cases to the tribunal in person. Later on Friday morning, Trzaskowski announced that, while he “respects the court’s decision”, the city would exercise its right to issue a further appeal against Bonkowska-Kubek’s ruling. Szanuję decyzję sądu, ale skorzystamy z prawa do zażalenia. Chodzi o mieszkańców i o służby ratunkowe, które muszą przejechać przez Aleję Szucha. Wolność zgromadzeń – tak. Blokowanie ulicy przez ponad miesiąc – nie. — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) November 27, 2026 The legal situation at the TK itself remains under dispute. The group of eight government-backed judges have begun holding meetings and processing cases, including stripping Święczkowski of legal immunity to face criminal charges. However, Święczkowski and Nawrocki continue to insist that the actions of those judges are unlawful and that their decisions have no legal effect.
