World.title: OpenAI countersues Apple in row over trade secrets, suppliers
World.content:
SAN FRANCISCO: OpenAI countersued Apple on Friday, alleging that the iPhone maker committed similar trade secret theft that it had accused the ChatGPT provider of this summer.

OpenAI alleged that Apple was stealing trade secrets through a former employee and pressuring shared suppliers to hamper its entry into the connected devices market.

The countersuit came in a filing Friday in federal court in San Jose, California, in which OpenAI responded to a lawsuit filed by Apple on July 10 against it and two of its employees who previously worked for Apple.

The two companies, partners since ChatGPT was integrated into Apple products in 2024, are poised to become rivals: OpenAI is developing its first connected devices designed for artificial intelligence with the studio of Jony Ive, Apple’s renowned former design chief.

Apple is seeking “to compete unfairly by any means available,” OpenAI’s lawyers wrote.

According to the filing, Apple is demanding that suppliers identify their projects for OpenAI and the employees assigned to them.

“Suppliers have expressed fear of losing Apple business and have moved or rescheduled meetings with OpenAI to avoid Apple seeing them,” the filing says.

One supplier moved OpenAI’s production to a night shift, while another dropped planned work “because of threats from Apple,” according to the filing, which does not name any of the firms.

OpenAI also accused a former Apple employee, who spent six months at OpenAI before leaving in June and returning to the iPhone maker, of sending “dozens of OpenAI documents” about a prototype to his personal phone numbers, then presenting OpenAI’s plans to senior Apple staff in July “at Apple’s request.”

The lawyers also challenged a clause barring former Apple employees who joined OpenAI from trying to poach their former colleagues for one year.

They also challenged a practice that allegedly encourages Apple employees to mix work files with their personal iCloud accounts so that, according to the lawyers, the company can later accuse those who leave of theft.

OpenAI on Friday also withdrew its motion to dismiss the case, without giving a reason.

In October, OpenAI pledged not to use the information Apple claims as trade secrets, after the judge said he was “highly likely” to issue an order barring OpenAI from using it until trial.

Apple did not immediately respond when contacted by AFP for comment.

World.title: Parts of the US clean up, power being restored after Thanksgiving storm soaks East Coast
World.content:
Heavy rain over flooded East Coast communities began easing Friday, and power was slowly restored to hundreds of thousands of customers as some places stayed on guard for high-tide flooding following a round of holiday storms.

The storms snarled travel and downed trees and power lines. The intense weather led to water rescues from New York to Virginia. In New York City, preparations were underway to hold Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade on Saturday after an unprecedented postponement because of rain and high winds.

Elsewhere, wet snow fell as far south as the Tennessee Valley and freezing rain moved across northern New England. Cold rain was reported in parts of the Midwest, including the Ohio Valley and the lower Great Lakes.

Another storm system in the Northwest brought rain along coastal Oregon. More snow was forecast in the Cascade Range and in mountain passes in Montana and Wyoming.

Storm means post-holiday cleanup for many

Conditions were expected to improve across the entire eastern US, “but this huge system will take some time to weaken,” the National Weather Service said. Coastal flood warnings were posted from New Jersey to Virginia.

The number of power outages, which peaked Thursday at more than 900,000, fell to 360,000 by Friday evening as crews worked to restore electricity, according to poweroutage.us. Pennsylvania had the most, followed by Missouri, where snow caused problems.

In Hampton, Virginia, the storm toppled a beloved landmark at Grandview Beach: a weathered, leafless tree known as the “Grieving Tree” or the “Shell Tree.” Visitors regularly decorated its branches with seashells, and it became a popular subject for photographers.

After surviving many storms, the tree “may have finally met its match,” local meteorologist Ricky Matthews said on Facebook, sharing a photograph.

Cynthia Battles, 70, said the storm ripped a two-story deck off her waterfront cottage in Oak Orchard, Delaware, and sent waves crashing through a sliding glass door. Glass was everywhere, her pontoon boat was in pieces and her partner’s boat was submerged.

Battles was drying out photographs and important documents. Some treasured books were ruined.

“I know it’s stuff — you can’t take it with you — but it’s the stuff that I need,” said Battles, who did not know if the cottage can be saved.

Part of a fishing pier collapsed in Virginia Beach, Virginia, closing a 3-mile (4.8-kilometer) section of beach, including the boardwalk, the city said.

Downtown merchants in Avalon, New Jersey, scrambled to pump out saltwater after some of the most significant tides in the seaside community’s history. Santa Claus was scheduled to arrive on a fire truck by evening to light the Christmas tree.

Conditions were a “million times better than they were 24 hours ago,” borough business administrator Scott Wahl said.

Water flooded the garage and surrounded the property of Cheryl McKenna of Ocean City, New Jersey, keeping her family inside for six hours on the holiday.

“Our family’s been here for 36 years,” McKenna said. “But honestly we’re thinking, is this the right place for us to be? We’re now retired, and we want to stay down here, but how often can we continue to do this?”

Parts of the South and Midwest see snow while California faces floods

Part of Tennessee was under a winter storm warning for up to an inch of snow Friday, after rain turned into light snow on Thanksgiving. Conditions were calmer for the Midwest compared with the previous day, when as much as 15 inches (38 centimeters) of snow fell in eastern Missouri. The ice arena in Wentzville, Missouri, was empty when the roof caved in.

Waves driven by high tides caused flooding along the Pacific coast and continued to affect train service. Buses were pressed into service as Amtrak’s Pacific Surfliner canceled or shortened more than a dozen trains between San Diego and Los Angeles.

Record tides along the California coast prompted evacuations from Humboldt County in the far north to Ventura County near Los Angeles.

Heavy snow was expected in parts of Montana and Wyoming. A renewed surge of moisture associated with an atmospheric river across the Pacific Northwest moved toward the northern Rockies, the weather service said.

World.title: Army deems lead azide detonation a success but criticism lingers over notification
World.content:
The detonation of the nation’s aging stockpile of lead azide, which spurred widespread concerns about potential environmental contamination, has been deemed a success by the US Army. But questions remain about how and when the federal government communicated its plans.

The US Environmental Protection Agency said about 300 people spent Thursday in the field sampling schools, playgrounds, churches and homes across the region. EPA expected to begin releasing preliminary results as early as Friday night.

More than 1,500 samples were taken of air, water, soil and dust before the detonation. After, they took hundreds of samples including from homes, parks and drinking water, the EPA has said.

So far, the EPA said there has continued to be “zero” airborne lead detected in the region since Wednesday’s controlled detonation.

While that’s reassuring, residents and some elected officials have criticized the Army for not being more transparent and providing more notice when it first determined the stockpile was unstable.

A notice that plant managers intended to neutralize the stockpile was posted on a government website last year in the fall. Growing concern led to a plant closure in March that was publicized, and an October public meeting warned that the chemicals would soon need to be detonated.

Residents in the tiny town of Middletown, where the Army stockpile was held, knew of the plans, but few others did — and the warnings largely failed to register with elected officials and the broader public until days before the planned detonation.

Democratic Gov.-elect Rob Sand is among those calling for an investigation into why the lead azide was allowed to get to this precarious point.

“The lead-up to the detonation should never have been so chaotic and unclear,” he said after the detonation.

Pause at the ammunition plant brings first notice to Middletown

Middletown Mayor Rodney Johnson and fellow residents said they were anything but blindsided. They learned of the problem in March.

Johnson said he was briefed by the plant commander at the time and shown photos of the bunkers where the 68 barrels had been stored since being transferred there nearly two decades ago.

A working group assembled by the Army in January spent months charting a path forward and in October, about 200 residents attended a public meeting where experts outlined the urgency of detonating the hazardous material before it could spark a chain reaction of unintended explosions.

The Army said then they were aiming for a date in November and that the weather would dictate the schedule.

The Army submitted an application to the EPA in late October, winning approval from regulators within about two weeks. The lengthy document covered everything from the alternatives that had been considered to the environmental sampling that would follow and community engagement that was required.

“Because this action may raise public concerns related to noise, blast effects, and potential environmental contamination, this Community Engagement Plan establishes the framework for proactive, transparent communication with the EPA, local elected officials, the Middletown community, the media, and other interested stakeholders,” the application states.

Critics blast the Army for not sharing info more widely

Johnson has said he believes the Army did its job.

“Unfortunately negative social media and unconfirmed theories have made this task more complicated for all parties involved,” he said in a social media post after a legal challenge delayed the original Nov. 20 date for the detonation.

At the time, he said Middletown residents were fearful, not knowing when the lead azide would be taken care of so they could get on with their lives.

Environmentalists and other critics argued that the Army should have cast a wider net, providing information sooner to more downwind communities. They said contamination from toxic lead dust can have long-lasting health and environmental impacts and people needed time to prepare.

“The failure of communication and transparency throughout the planning process is inexcusable and left many Iowans feeling confused, helpless, and scared,” said Josh Turek, a Democratic state lawmaker who was recently elected to Iowa’s open US Senate seat.

Public adviseries for permits went unnoticed by many

The EPA issued public adviseries about the flurry of required permitting as early as May. The agency said in a letter to Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds that those notices went to Iowa’s congressional delegation, state lawmakers and local officials.

Reynolds’ office did not answer emails asking whether the governor knew about the plant’s shutdown in March or the permit adviseries. Some Democratic state lawmakers said they were blindsided, while Iowa House Majority Leader Bobby Kaufmann, a Republican, said he had concerns about how notification was handled.

US Sen. Joni Ernst, a Republican and former lieutenant colonel in the Iowa Army National Guard, said that although the Army began discussing disposal with some communities months ago, critical details about the plume and how far it could reach weren’t part of those conversations.

“At a time when trust in our institutions is already low, the military owes the people it serves more transparency, not less,” Ernst said in a statement the day before the detonation.

The situation turned into political finger-pointing, said US Sen. Chuck Grassley. The Iowa Republican noted that his office had been in contact with federal officials since March and that the Oct. 15 town hall was well attended.

“But it’s clear it wasn’t enough,” he said earlier this week, vowing to continue pressing for answers so people have a better understanding of the Army’s decision-making process.

With more time to prepare, the Army added more safeguards

With the public outcry and the legal delay, environmentalists said the Army had more time to put in additional safeguards beyond the dirt barriers, walls of water and special foam.

The EPA also brought in more workers to help with air, water and soil sampling.

According to court documents and briefings by federal officials, much of the lead azide stockpile had been transferred to the Iowa plant in 2009 and at the time records showed much of the material was old and already a concern for the military.

For years, contractors inspected the barrels and would replenish the water-ethanol solution that kept the lead azide stable. Court documents state that because crystals began to form inside the barrels and around the lids, the containers could not be handled or opened. The last time they were replenished was September 2025, Army officials said.

It was then that plant operator American Ordnance first provided notice that the lead azide needed to be neutralized. The resulting contract was later withdrawn as the working group determined detonation was the safest way.

World.title: French far-right leader Le Pen clashes with Macron over EU budget
World.content:
BRUSSELS, Belgium: French President Emmanuel Macron slapped down far-right leader Marine Le Pen on Thursday, accusing her of “arrogance” for criticizing a push to lock in the EU’s next budget before France’s 2027 elections.

A Brussels summit failed to bridge deep divides over the bloc’s 2028-2034 budget, wrapping up on a sour note after more than 12 hours of talks, with leaders agreeing only that a deal by year-end will be an uphill battle.

“We are not there yet,” German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told reporters afterwards, though he had “not given up hope” for a deal when leaders meet again on December 17.

Failure would mean the tense negotiations spilling into a year of elections across Europe — most crucially in France — whose president has raised the stakes by threatening to walk away if that happens.

The current frontrunner to succeed Macron next spring, Le Pen denounced the budget push on social media as “underhanded political manoeuvring to thwart the democratic will of the French people.”

Swiping back on the summit sidelines, Macron said of Le Pen: “It is an odd kind of arrogance to behave as if she is already in charge of France’s destiny because, as things stand, she has not been elected.”

It is not the first time the two have clashed over the budget.

Macron took aim at Le Pen last month, telling her to “stay humble” after she laid out plans to cut France’s aid to Ukraine and its contribution to the European Union.

‘Not afraid’

Leaders have spent nearly all of 2026 butting heads over the size of the long-term budget after the European Commission proposed a two-trillion-euro spending plan, which most capitals disapproved.

The latest proposal by European Council head Antonio Costa sought to bridge divisions by slashing the budget by 204 billion euros ($224 billion) and proposing a tax on digital companies.

Costa urged leaders to “compromise” heading into the talks — but they failed to produce a breakthrough.

On one side, a group of so-called “frugal” countries including heavyweight Germany and the Netherlands — nicknaming themselves the “Sensible Seven” — are pushing for a smaller spending pot.

Briefing reporters afterwards, Merz said Germany would keep pressing for cuts — and several likeminded countries sat out the final summit meetings to signal dissatisfaction with the process so far.

Meanwhile, 17 southern, central and eastern European nations in the “Friends of Cohesion” group still wanted greater funding to support agriculture and regional development — as hundreds of farmers demonstrated outside the summit.

But Costa played down the summit divisions at a press conference afterwards, calling it “a necessary step” in the negotiation process.

“Everyone had to show they did not agree — and stage a bit of political theater,” echoed one EU diplomat.

The call for cuts has raised hackles from France, which wants more money for farmers and insists Europe needs larger funding to match its rising challenges.

Addressing the media, Macron said slashing the budget was a “strategic error” that risked hobbling the bloc’s efforts to invest on a par with economic rivals China and the United States.

The upcoming French vote loomed large over the talks.

“The prospect of a potential Le Pen victory — and its consequences — is always in the back of everyone’s mind,” one EU diplomat said.

But several leaders pushed back at that idea, with Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker saying he was “certainly not afraid of an election in France.”

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni similarly said she saw “no hard deadline” to reach a deal.

Ukraine link

An already-fraught dealmaking process was complicated further after Merz linked any resolution to an agreement on Ukraine funding by all 27 EU countries.

Member states are being asked to back an extra 45-billion-euro ($49 billion) loan to help keep Ukraine funded through 2027, but Prague, Budapest and Bratislava want an opt-out.

The trio, which opted out of a similar giant loan last year, are normally net recipients of European money.

But Merz reiterated that he considered this a non-starter, warning: “I stand by my position that aid for Ukraine must be borne by the entire European Union.”

World.title: Chelsea suffer third successive loss as Gibbs-White grabs double for Nottingham Forest
World.content:
NOTTINGHAM: Chelsea suffered a ‌third successive Premier League defeat as Morgan Gibbs-White scored twice for Nottingham Forest in a 3-2 victory at a cold and rainy City Ground on Friday. A stunning volley by Igor Jesus gave Forest a fifth-minute lead and Gibbs-White made it 2-0 from the penalty spot six minutes after the interval after Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana had clumsily brought down ex Chelsea player Liam Delap. Substitute Emmanuel Emegha pulled a goal back almost immediately for the visitors but Gibbs-White was played in by a superb dinked pass by Xaver Schlager to restore ‌his side’s two-goal ‌advantage after 72 minutes. There were late nerves ‌for the hosts though as Emegha struck again with a header from Pedro Neto’s cross in the 89th minute but Forest hung on for a first win over Chelsea at the City Ground since 1997. Defeat increased the scrutiny on Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso, whose side have now lost four of their last five league games and sit eighth in the table. Forest moved up to 14th place.

“It’s a difficult ‌moment for everyone, for the fans, ‌for sure it’s disappointing to lose again,” Alonso told Sky Sports.

“We need ‌to keep trying to find solutions, trying to be critical, we ‌can’t stop. We are low in confidence but we are responsible to try and find solutions.

“We can do better for sure.”

Chelsea have now conceded 23 Premier League goals in 12 games, a total only surpassed by ‌bottom club Crystal Palace who Chelsea face at Stamford Bridge on Wednesday.

Another bad result then and the pressure will really start to mount on former Liverpool midfielder Alonso but for Forest’s new manager Oliver Glasner, things are looking up.

They have now beaten Manchester City and Chelsea in their last three games and appear to be getting to grips with former Palace boss Glasner’s demands.

“I feel we need to take a bit of realization that we have a new manager, we’re sticking with him, we’re trusting the process, believing in him and trusting what he wants,” Gibbs-White said.

“Not every week is it going to be pretty or is it going to be nice, but when times like this happen tonight we’ve got to make the most of it and enjoy it.”

World.title: Where science meets enterprise: Saudi startups transform research into real-world impact
World.content:
Saudi Arabia is investing heavily in water and food research, as startups increasingly turn scientific discoveries into commercial ventures, developing solutions to resource challenges and attracting investor interest.

Startups supported by King Abdullah University of Science and Technology have raised approximately $1.4 billion in cumulative funding, with 66 companies securing $338 million between July 2025 and June 2026, an increase of more than 30 percent year on year. The university’s 282 active startups have generated $1.1 billion in cumulative revenue.

“Ultimately, a technology must demonstrate not only scientific merit, but also a clear market need and a credible path to commercial adoption. This is particularly important when attracting private sector investment,” Haitham Al-Humsi, director of Innovation Ecosystem Development at KAUST, told Arab News.

One example is Namya, a venture established by KAUST and Riyadh-based venture builder SEQUENCIVE.

Its first product, Plantiva, aims to improve crop yields and help plants use water and nutrients more efficiently.

Other ventures are addressing challenges across the water and agriculture sectors.

KAUST’s Venture Studio program further supports technology-based founders through expert mentorship and $125,000 in seed capital.

The university also works with the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture through incubation and acceleration programs. One beneficiary is SeaCras, a Croatian-founded company using artificial intelligence and satellite imagery to monitor seas, coastal waters and inland water systems.

“Scientific research and academia played — and still play — an enormous part in our product development, not only for quality control, but also for disseminating the generated knowledge and technology,” SeaCras CEO and founder Mario Spadina told Arab News.

Adapting technologies to local conditions remains crucial, as solutions developed in other climates may not perform similarly under Saudi Arabia’s heat, soil salinity and water scarcity.

“Getting from a lab result to a product in the market is the slowest and most expensive step in science everywhere in the world. Saudi Arabia is already showing it can be done in water and food. AI can make it faster and cheaper,” academic and AI expert Prof. Mohammed Al-Qarni told Arab News.

“Solutions proven in controlled greenhouses or benchtop cells often behave differently under Saudi Arabia’s extreme heat, soil salinity, and water scarcity,” said Alia Omar Bahanshal, founder and CEO of Aurora AI Consultancy Firm.

“Ultimately, while AI does not replace wet-lab science, agronomy, or engineering, it compresses the cycle between discovery, validation, and commercial scale — a decisive advantage when building resilient food and water businesses in harsh climates,” she said.

World.title: Siddique leads Sharjah Warriorz to first ILT20 win with seven-wicket victory over Dubai Capitals
World.content:
SHARJAH: Junaid Siddique took three wickets before Tim Seifert and Paul Walter led a blistering batting display as Sharjah Warriorz secured their first win of DP World ILT20 Season 5 with a seven-wicket victory over Dubai Capitals on Friday.

Siddique finished with figures of 3-25 as the Capitals were bowled out for 126 at Sharjah Cricket Stadium. Adam Milne and Richard Gleeson took two wickets apiece, while Karim Janat top-scored for the Capitals with 30 off 18 balls.

The Warriorz made light work of the chase, reaching 127 for three in just 13 overs, with 42 balls to spare. Seifert struck 41 from 20 deliveries and Walter added 42 off 25, putting on 82 for the first wicket. Brandon McMullen remained unbeaten on 26 from 19 balls to complete the win.

The Capitals struggled to get going after being put in to bat, scoring only three runs in the first two overs as Milne and Gleeson kept the opening batters in check.

Siddique made the breakthrough during the powerplay, dismissing Masood Gurbaz for 17 after the opener had briefly threatened to accelerate with a six. Walter then removed Max Holden for one, before Sikandar Raza dismissed Faf du Plessis for 15 to leave the Capitals at 40-3.

Siddique struck again in the 12th over, having captain Sam Billings caught behind for 12. Marcus Stoinis, who had hit two successive sixes in Raza’s previous over, fell to Sharafuddin Ashraf for 23, before Siddique removed Rovman Powell for two to leave the Capitals struggling at 78-6.

Janat and Hassan Khan offered some resistance, adding 44 runs from 27 balls. Khan made 18 from 15 deliveries, while Janat’s 30 was the highest score of the innings.

Milne took two wickets in the 19th over before Gleeson dismissed Janat and Dushmantha Chameera off successive deliveries in the final over to end the Capitals’ innings.

The Warriorz made an explosive start to their reply, with Seifert and Walter attacking from the outset. They took 18 runs from Chameera’s opening over, followed by 14 from Tymal Mills and 20 from Stoinis in successive overs, reaching 79 without loss at the end of the powerplay.

Muhammad Arfan broke the partnership in the seventh over when Seifert was caught behind by Billings. Walter was bowled by Noor Ahmad in the ninth over, and the Afghanistan spinner later dismissed James Rew for 10 to leave the Warriorz at 111-3.

McMullen then finished the chase with back-to-back fours off Noor in the 13th over.

Siddique, named Player of the Match, described it as his best bowling performance.

“This was my best bowling performance. I wanted to bowl for my team today because we had to win the game. The two guys (Adam Milne and Richard Gleeson) bowled very well in the powerplay, so I just wanted to bowl to my strengths,” he said.

Capitals captain Sam Billings said his side had been unable to match the Warriorz’ aggressive start.

“It was a big toss to win, and their openers killed it in the powerplay. We scrapped really well, and I thought that partnership at the back end got us to a half-decent score. Gleeson and Milne have done it all around the world for a long time, and they're quality bowlers in difficult conditions. We needed early wickets to fight fire with fire, but it wasn't to be,” he said.

World.title: Kuwait summons Iran ambassador over ‘continued Iranian attacks’
World.content:
KUWAIT CITY: Kuwait’s foreign ministry on Friday said it summoned Iran’s ambassador over “continued Iranian attacks” after a drone attack a day earlier killed two Italians in the first fatal strike in the Gulf state for months.

The ministry “summoned His Excellency Ambassador Mohammad Totonji, Ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran to the State of Kuwait, and handed him a note of protest over the continued Iranian attacks on the State of Kuwait, most recently the drone attack that yesterday, Thursday, targeted a vital site in the country, killing two Italian nationals,” it wrote on X.

UN chief Antonio Guterres on Friday condemned the attack and called on "all parties to exercise restraint."



The secretary-general expressed solidarity with Kuwait and offered his condolences to the families of the victims, his spokesman Stephane Dujarric said.

Iran has in the last week ratcheted up attacks on Kuwait and Gulf neighbor Bahrain while it continues to contest control of the Strait of Hormuz with the United States.

But its top diplomat and military both denied any involvement in the attack that killed two employees of German defense contractor Rheinmetall who were working on an air defense system.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held phone calls with both his Kuwaiti counterpart Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah and Italian counterpart Antonio Tajani to deny Tehran’s involvement, according to Iran’s state TV and foreign ministry.

In his call with Tajani, “Araghchi stated that Iran had no role or involvement whatsoever in the occurrence of this event,” the Iranian foreign ministry said in a statement.

Araghchi added that Tehran was prepared to cooperate with Kuwait and Italy to “determine the origin of the incident,” the ministry said.

World.title: Iraq seizes smuggled oil bound for Sulaymaniyah as Baghdad tightens control
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi security forces intercepted a truck carrying smuggled oil at the Chimen checkpoint in Kirkuk on Friday as Baghdad steps up efforts to fight oil smuggling and reinforce federal authority across the nation.

According to Iraq’s Security Media Cell, which reports to the Prime Minister’s Office, forces from the Kirkuk Operations Command seized a vehicle traveling from Basra to Sulaymaniyah, which was carrying a container labeled as plumbing materials and protected with customs seals.

Security staff got suspicious of the package and ran a scan, which revealed hidden oil.

The driver was apprehended, and the truck was confiscated for further investigation and legal action.

The seizure comes as Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi pushes for more federal supervision of border crossings in Iraq’s Kurdistan Region and oilfields in disputed territory as part of larger measures to curb smuggling and defend Iraq’s national resources.

On Friday, US President Donald Trump voiced support for Al-Zaidi’s efforts to establish state authority across Iraq, curb oil smuggling, battle corruption, and place all weaponry under government control.

The operation comes as Baghdad steps up its attempts to improve government management of transportation routes, border crossings, and the country’s oil resources.

World.title: Trump backs Baghdad’s push to assert federal authority across Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US President Donald Trump pledged support for Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s attempts to establish federal authority throughout the country on Friday, as Baghdad prepares to place border crossings in the Kurdistan Region and numerous oilfields in disputed territory under federal control.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump praised Al-Zaidi’s efforts to fight oil smuggling, battle corruption, and place all weaponry under state control.

“We support Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s efforts to build a united, prosperous, and strong Iraq that makes its own political decisions,” Trump said.

Washington’s backing is a diplomatic setback for the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG), which has sought international support against Baghdad’s aspirations to strengthen federal authority over border crossings and oil resources.

Iraqi Kurdish officials have aggressively criticized Al-Zaidi’s decree, claiming it breaches the region’s constitutional rights and weakens Iraq’s federal structure.

Iraqi Kurdish Prime Minister Masrour Barzani urged the international community to protect the region’s constitutional rights. In contrast, Trump’s speech expressly supported Baghdad’s attempts to impose state authority throughout the country.

The support also indicates the improved ties between Washington and Baghdad under Al-Zaidi’s leadership.

A national conversation is set for December 1 to resolve remaining conflicts between Baghdad and Erbil in line with the Iraqi constitution.

The advances occur as Baghdad works to consolidate state power, establish national sovereignty, and create a unified Iraq that serves all residents, regardless of race, religion, or sectarian affiliation.

World.title: Under-attack Palestinians find unlikely ally in Israeli retired general
World.content:
As Sawiyah – The four Israeli soldiers stepped out of their car in the occupied West Bank, their faces masked, their uniforms unmarked and automatic weapons strapped across their shoulders.

They had entered a Palestinian olive grove but, little did they expect, the person there planning to tell them to leave could have once been issuing them orders.

A retired Israeli general, Eyal Ben Reuven, had come that day to the Palestinian town of As Sawiyah, on a mission to prevent some of the rampant violence against Palestinians by extremist Israeli settlers.

For the 72-year-old, joined by fellow battle-hardened veterans of the Israeli military, the violence is a stain on the institution in which they once served.

“I’ve fought in a number of wars. And unfortunately, I have reached the point where I have seen an evolution,” said the former military man with piercing eyes, who spent much of his career driving tanks.

The army is failing to act, he said, even when the violence has reached a level “I never could have imagined”.

Unrest has soared in the West Bank since the unprecedented October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas on Israel, which responded with a massive military campaign in the Gaza Strip.

More than 1,100 Palestinians have been killed by the army or settlers in the West Bank since then. More than 50 Israelis have died in the same time in the territory, which Israel captured in 1967.

The olive harvest has become a flashpoint, with settlers attacking or stealing from Palestinian farmers on a nearly daily basis.

With the other former soldiers, Ben Reuven has set up a protective presence, a tactic more common among leftist activists who put themselves in the way in a bid to stop attacks against Palestinians.

– Army intervenes in harvest –

Clad in comfortable hiking attire and carrying walking sticks, it is difficult to imagine that some of the greying volunteers fought in intense combat.

Like good soldiers, they review instructions upon going out — they are there to assist the olive harvest, not to confront the settlers, and they will obey the army’s instructions.

A Palestinian human rights activist, Arafat Abu Ras, led the military men to a small olive grove. An old Palestinian woman was waiting to guide them and the soldiers, more accustomed to the battlefield than to farming, used sticks and small rakes to start knocking the olives off the trees, volunteering to do the work on the Palestinians’ behalf.

Almost immediately a military vehicle arrived. Under the humming of a drone, one of the serving soldiers shoved aside an AFP team to prevent filming, while another checked Abu Ras’s identity papers and ordered everyone to leave.

Abu Ras said that the olive farmers had coordinated with the army, which insists that Palestinians receive approval for their harvests in the occupied West Bank, arguing that it is for safety reasons.

“They say, ‘yes, yes’, and then the next day they come and force us to leave,” Abu Ras said.

After the serving soldiers arrived, a second vehicle came, this time with Israeli settlers. An official from a neighbouring settlement also ordered the olive pickers out, with troops saying it was a “closed military zone”.

The Israeli veterans, in line with their guidance, complied. They instead moved elsewhere with the farmers, hoping to prevent attacks on them.

“Our army is a joke,” fumed Yoel Feldschuh, a 77-year-old former air force brigadier general.

“Is it its role to shut an olive grove? What does the military have to do with that?”

Feldschuh made headlines when he was handcuffed and taken away by police in a similar action a month earlier.

Changing the behaviour of the military, he said, “will take a generation”.

– Rampant violence –

COGAT, the Israeli body responsible for civil affairs in the Palestinian territories, maintains that “security forces are deployed to ensure a safe olive harvest”.

But since September, the harvest has been marked by nearly 500 attacks, some of them fatal, according to the Israeli human rights organisation Yesh Din.

Amram Mitzna, an 81-year-old retired general, attributes the army’s inaction to the young ages of the soldiers, who have grown up under now-caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving leader.

“They consider every Arab an enemy who must be treated as such,” said Mitzna, who has also served as mayor of Haifa, Israel’s third largest city.

Netanyahu has allied himself with the far-right and championed a rapid growth of West Bank settlements, which are considered illegal under international law.

Netanyahu is fighting for political survival after losing ground in elections. Gadi Eisenkot, a former general seeking to succeed him, supports many of Netanyahu’s security policies but accuses him of yielding to “Jewish terrorism” in the West Bank and vowed to crack down on extremist settlers.

In As Sawiyah, the former soldiers eventually finished harvesting the olives in a nearby area alongside a school, putting them in bags to be taken by Palestinian villagers.

While no one was injured, Ben Reuven remained deeply disturbed by how the young soldier acted during the altercation.

“When I saw him arrive, masked, shouting, kicking sacks of olives, I was ashamed.”

World.title: BP eyes deeper energy ties with Iraq as CEO visits Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – British energy giant BP has reaffirmed its commitment to expanding operations in Iraq following CEO Meg O’Neill’s first visit to the country and meeting with Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi in Baghdad.

According to the Prime Minister’s office, talks centered on developing oilfields and boosting exploration efforts, notably at Rumaila in Basra, Eridu in Dhi Qar, and Kirkuk, as Iraq aims to produce 10 million barrels of oil per day by 2032.

To reach output objectives, Al-Zaidi advocated for faster development, intensified field activities, and longer working hours.

Iraq’s Prime Minister also emphasized the need for collecting related gas and decreasing waste to improve domestic energy supply.

O’Neill reaffirmed BP’s commitment to expanding its activities in Iraq, utilizing sophisticated technology and technical experience to boost production and develop the country’s oilfields.

Following the meeting, O’Neill lauded Iraq’s objectives, workforce, and energy potential on LinkedIn, stressing prospects to enhance the company’s collaboration with Baghdad.

Along with its partners and the Iraqi operator, BP plays a critical role in Rumaila, Iraq’s biggest producing oilfield, providing technical knowledge to boost production and maximize resource recovery.

In Kirkuk, BP is engaging in a large rebuilding program involving oil, gas, electricity, and water infrastructure, with the first phase covering resources amounting to more than three billion barrels of oil.

The company’s growing presence is especially important as Iraq pursues foreign investment, modernizes its energy infrastructure, reduces gas flaring, and expands its oil production capacity.

O’Neill emphasized that combining Iraq’s immense natural resources and indigenous knowledge with BP’s technology and worldwide experience may provide significant benefits for both parties.

The visit highlights Iraq’s strategic significance to BP, as well as the company’s long-term engagement in growing the country’s oil industry.

World.title: Iraq and Bahrain to strengthen economic and diplomatic ties
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi met with Bahraini Ambassador Khaled Ahmed al-Mansour on Thursday, as the two countries work to repair and enhance their bilateral ties.

The envoy delivered congratulations from Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa and underlined his government’s commitment to developing economic cooperation with Iraq, promoting mutual growth, and resolving common difficulties.

Both parties addressed ways to further collaboration across sectors, as well as regional and international trends, emphasizing the necessity of coordinating views and ensuring regional stability.

The meeting comes after Bahrain’s decision on November 7 to reinstate its ambassador to Baghdad, after Al-Zaidi’s historic visit to Manama on November 4, the first by an Iraqi prime minister since 2003.

Al-Mansour departed Baghdad in April due to increased diplomatic tensions over drone strikes on Bahrain by Iran-backed Iraqi forces.

The reinstatement of full diplomatic representation represents a major step forward in Iraqi-Bahraini relations, creating new potential for commerce, investment, and economic cooperation while improving Iraq’s links with its Gulf neighbors.

World.title: Baghdad cracks down on Kurdistan oil smuggling to Iran
World.content:
Baghdad – The Iraqi government’s crackdown on oil smuggling through the Kurdistan region targets routes used to move crude into Iran to help it evade sanctions, according to document cited by state media and a security official.

On Tuesday, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi moved to put Kurdistan’s border crossings and several oil fields under federal control in an effort to curb oil smuggling.

Following Zaidi’s announcement, the state news agency INA cited what it described as an intelligence document revealing that crude oil was being smuggled in tanker trucks from fields in Kirkuk and Sulaymaniyah provinces into Iran.

There, according to the document, it was being blended with Iranian crude and then exported to Afghanistan for domestic consumption.

The document, which AFP has seen but could not independently authenticate, says Iranian and Iraqi crude are mixed in an effort to help Iran “evade sanctions.”

The United States, with which Zaidi has enjoyed close ties since taking office earlier this year, accuses Iran of using Iraq’s economy to evade sanctions, and has previously sanctioned Iraqi individuals and companies for blending Iraqi and Iranian oil.

A security source in Baghdad told AFP that the government’s position is that “any smuggling to Iran or elsewhere is prohibited, and the entire international border must be secured.”

The source added that Zaidi’s crackdown on oil smuggling, whether in the Kurdistan Region or elsewhere in Iraq, is backed by the United States, which has sought to choke Iran’s economy.

The intelligence document also indicated that another smuggling route runs through border crossings to Turkiye, but it was not clear if Turkiye was the final destination.

A former oil ministry official told AFP on condition of anonymity that the Kurdistan region has long exported oil to Turkiye not only via a pipeline, but also in huge quantities in tanker trucks.

He added that “illicit crossings in the Kurdistan region are used to smuggle crude oil, including from other parts of Iraq, to neighboring countries,” including to Iran and onwards to Afghanistan.

For months, Zaidi has been cracking down on the illicit oil trade, arresting officials and challenging an Iran-backed armed group after smuggling was uncovered in its stronghold near Baghdad.

But the move to bring Kurdistan’s border crossings and several oil fields under federal control could sour relations with Kurdish authorities, who have denounced Zaidi’s decision while keeping the door open for talks.

World.title: Iraq sentences eight French Daesh members to life in prison
World.content:
Baghdad – An Iraqi court sentenced eight French nationals to life in prison on Thursday for joining the Daesh group, according to an AFP correspondent, as the country presses ahead with prosecuting thousands of suspected militants.



Another two French defendants were sentenced to 15-year terms on similar charges, while 10 people who were supposed to receive verdicts had those postponed to another date.



The Daesh group swept across Syria and Iraq in 2014, committing massacres and forcing women and girls into sexual slavery, while many supporters traveled from Europe and elsewhere to join its ranks.



Iraq’s prisons, already packed with Daesh suspects, have recently received thousands more detainees transferred from neighboring Syria.



The 10 who received their sentences on Thursday are among 47 French citizens put on trial in Iraq since September, having been brought from Syria last year.



The court had already sentenced 15 of the group to life imprisonment, while one person had received a 15-year prison term.



Among those still awaiting verdicts was Adrien Guihal, known as the person who voiced the Daesh claim for the 2016 Nice attack when an attacker drove a truck through Bastille Day crowds, killing 86 people. His verdict was postponed on Thursday to another date.



Also waiting were Thomas Collange, whose wife who had traveled with him to Syria was sentenced to 10 years in prison in France last year, and Quentin Le Brun, who appeared in a propaganda video.



Romain Garnier, who worked for the group’s radio operation, was given a life sentence on Thursday.



During their hearings, most of the suspects pleaded guilty, and all expressed regret over joining the group, with some asking to be repatriated to France.



During his session last week, Guihal spoke in a loud, clear voice, in contrast with other defendants, who spoke quietly and at times stuttered.



He claimed he had renounced the group’s actions. “I have changed a lot, I am a new person,” he said.



Collange, who converted to Islam in the early 2000s, said he regretted bringing his wife and kids with him to Syria, and had renounced the group since trying to escape in 2017.

– Thousands on trial –

France has repatriated hundreds of family members of militants, but has refused to bring back most of the men accused of involvement, leaving them to face justice abroad.



During their hearings, many defendants argued that they had only been to Syria, questioning why they are being tried in Iraq.



Baghdad is prosecuting them under its anti-terrorism law for joining Daesh, regardless of whether they operated in Iraq or Syria.



Iraq, backed by US-led forces, proclaimed victory over Daesh in 2017, and Kurdish-led forces supported by Washington defeated the group in neighboring Syria two years later.



Iraq, however, is still reckoning with the group’s legacy, with mass graves being uncovered and testimonies of Daesh brutality still to be investigated.



For years, Iraqi courts have handed down hundreds of life and death sentences to people convicted of terrorism offenses, including foreign fighters.



But some rights groups have denounced the trials as rushed and lacking due process.



In February, Iraq also received more than 5,700 Daesh detainees from over 60 countries after the United States transferred them from Syria, following years of detention in Kurdish prisons.



Trials for that group started on Sunday, with the first hearings involving Syrian nationals.

World.title: Asian stocks mostly rise as markets calm after tech rout
World.content:
Hong Kong – Asian stocks mostly rose Friday, with technology firms building on the previous day’s gains and enjoying a much-needed period of calm following the ructions at the start of the week.

With Wall Street closed for the Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday, traders had no new business-driving catalysts heading into the weekend, though they remain on edge over concerns about the AI boom.

They were also keeping an eye on possible retaliation to Donald Trump’s proposed tariffs of up to 20 percent on some of the United States’ biggest trading partners, including China, the European Union, India, Japan and South Korea.

Seoul and Tokyo were the standouts on a generally quiet day on trading floors, with chipmakers SK hynix, Samsung and Kioxia enjoying healthy buying — having been among the most brutally sold during a rout earlier in the week.

Taipei, which also saw huge swings, was marginally higher.

Still, analysts warned that there would likely be more volatility to come as investors assess the outlook for the AI trade with questions over the vast sums pumped into the sector and profitability.

Also in view is the Federal Reserve’s next interest rate decision next month, with speculation swirling that it could opt for a hefty 50-basis-point hike instead of the usual 25 points.

Stocks in Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Jakarta, Singapore and Manila also rose.

Wellington edged down as New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon’s right-wing coalition lost its parliamentary majority, plunging the country into political uncertainty with an insurgent centrist party set to play kingmaker.

“In the absence of any new information the backdrop does remain fragile but for now investors have returned to equities with technology shares leading,” wrote Skye Masters at National Australia Bank.

“The test will be whether this improved sentiment can be sustained through to the end of the week as the US returns from Thanksgiving holiday.”

Oil prices extended Thursday’s gains of more than one percent amid fresh concerns over an escalation of hostilities in the Middle East after Tehran-backed Houthis struck a Saudi refinery, temporarily halting some operations. That came after an attack on another hub in the Gulf earlier in the week.

In company news, Japan Tobacco rallied more than four percent following a report that it was considering joining up with US giant Altria for a takeover of Britain’s Imperial Brands. Imperial jumped 13 percent in London on Thursday.

Japan Tobacco is dealing with a $8.9 billion hit after the Russian government seized all seven of its local subsidiaries, as relations with Tokyo worsen following the arrest of a Japanese journalist on spying allegations.

World.title: Support to Bill may not automatically lead DMK to NDA, but will open alignment path
World.content:
NEW DELHI: If Congress and DMK could join hands in 2004 after their bitter split where the Sonia Gandhi-led outfit accused the M Karunanidhi government of complicity in the assassination of former PM Rajiv Gandhi and brought down the United Front government in 1998, then anything can happen in politics.

Thus said a multi-term DMK MP over the prospect of his partyâs widely-expected support to BJP in securing passage of the delimitation bill in Parliament after it was in the vanguard of opposition to the governing party since 2014.

While DMKâs support to the bill is unlikely to automatically lead the party to BJP-led NDA but it does open a path for their alignment and offer the national party a fresh opening in Tamil Nadu, which has remained a tough nut for it to crack despite repeated attempts.



It certainly weakens the anti-South charge DMK, Congress and others have levelled against BJP.

Besides making explicit provision in the bill that the share of every state in Lok Sabha will remain the same and the maximum strength of LS will be frozen till 2051, both concessions aimed at winning over DMK, BJP has of late made subtle moves to dial down its push for legislative measures which had drawn sharp opposition from the Tamil party.





This includes a sudden slowdown in the working of two parliamentary committees overseeing Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, which has proposed an apex regulator in place of several for higher education, and a Constitution Amendment Bill, which proposes automatic removal of PM, CMs and ministers detained on criminal charges for 30 continuous days, when they were on the verge of adopting their reports.

DMK, which has long championed state autonomy and decried central governmentâs alleged encroachment on its turf, has been sharply critical of both bills.

Both parties have a history of working together. BJP and DMK were allies in the 1999 Lok Sabha elections and the regional party was a member of the Atal Bihari Vajpayee-led government before their split in 2003. Their âsecularâ opposition to BJP, which then moved closer to DMKâs rival AIADMK, helped them explain away their alliance. DMKâs current challenge is the sudden emergence of Vijay-led TVK as Congress dumped it overnight to help the star actor become chief minister.

With DMK out of INDIA bloc, its options are limited. With misgivings persisting in a section of party over joining hands with BJP, which too has been a bitter critic of its anti-Hindutva rhetoric, political compulsions may be the glue for them in the same it worked for DMK and Congress in 2004.

World.title: Opposition mood despondent as NCP (SP), DMK change stand
World.content:

and

That is the design of this episode.â But the mood in the opposition was despondent as its persisting confidence about unity in the anti-bill ranks dissipated with statements from M K Stalin and NCP (SP) leaders.

World.title: Attacks on shipping, seafarers unacceptable: EAM
World.content:
EAM S Jaishankar has called on Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) nations to deepen collaboration, ensure maritime safety

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Attacks on maritime shipping and seafarers are simply unacceptable and call for a global response, EAM S Jaishankar said Friday. Addressing the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), an inter-governmental body comprising 23 member-states, he said international law, particularly United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, must be respected.The 25th meeting of the IORA council of ministers here was followed by a joint communique that expressed concern over the undermining of maritime safety and security of vessels and seafarers and called for ensuring their safety and security.PM Narendra Modi met the foreign ministers and heads of delegation of the 23 IORA member-states participating in the meeting. âIndian Ocean has connected our people for a millennia. As chair of IORA, India looks forward to working closely with all partners to advance its vision of Mahasagar (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) and to strengthen peace, security, stability and prosperity in the Indian Ocean Region,â he posted on X.According to the Delhi communique, IORA reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining the Indian Ocean as a region of peace, stability and prosperity, and to upholding applicable international law to ensure âfreedom of navigation and overflight, unimpeded commerce, peaceful settlement of disputes and other lawful uses of the seaâ.It also reaffirmed its commitment to sovereign equality, territorial integrity, political independence, non-interference in internal affairs, peaceful co-existence and mutual benefit.India announced a grant of $500,000 for the associationâs institutional and financial capacity-building. âWhether it is to counter terrorism, narcotics trade or illegal, unreported, unregulated fishing, or indeed response to climate events and disaster situations, we have to become more self-reliant as well as more enthusiastic about cooperating with partners,â said Jaishankar.âWe are focused on the volatile aspects of a transforming global order, especially conflicts, frictions and disruptions. It is equally imperative to appreciate the promising aspects: deep interdependence, strong globalisation and the benefits of international cooperation,â he said.The Indian Ocean is central to global trade, energy security, connectivity and economic prosperity. It is also a region of immense diversity, opportunity and of shared challenges, he stressed. âOur collective responsibility is to ensure that it remains peaceful, stable, secure and conducive to development,â Jaishankar added.

World.title: Killing at Rohtak eatery was directed from Georgia: Sleuths
World.content:
According to sources, gangster Ravi Rathi, a native of Gangnauli village in UPâs Baghpat district and a key associate of jailed gangster Himanshu Bhau, is currently operating from Georgia.

NEW DELHI: Investigative agencies suspect the brazen quadruple murder at a hotel in Haryanaâs Rohtak was orchestrated from Georgia.According to sources, gangster Ravi Rathi, a native of Gangnauli village in UPâs Baghpat district and a key associate of jailed gangster Himanshu Bhau, is currently operating from Georgia.Rathi is reported to have assumed command of the syndicateâs operations following Bhauâs detention in Las Vegas last month. His name also surfaced in an Instagram post by the gang claiming responsibility for the deadly shooting. Agencies are trying to geolocate Rathi and will press for his return to India.Agencies had brought back notorious gangster Venkatesh Garg, a top henchman of UK-based gangster Kapil Sangwan, from Georgia in June this year. Sources said Georgia has been attracting Indian gangsters primarily because it serves as a strategic transit hub with lax entry rules and low enforcement scrutiny.Located at the crossroads of Eastern Europe and Western Asia, it offers easy e-visas or visa-free entry via third-country permits like the UAE or Schengen visas and cheap flights, allowing fugitives to slip in easily and move onward if needed.The shooters were using a less popular, encrypted chat app for communicating with their overseas handlers.The intended target of the attack was rival gangster Sunny Ritoli, who narrowly escaped the ambush.Officers said the assailants had deployed a honeytrap strategy, a known modus operandi of Rathiâs, to lure Ritoli to the spot. A woman, who identified herself as Janhavi, invited Ritoli to the hotel on the pretext of having coffee together.Ritoli was staying at the hotel along with three of the men who were eventually gunned down. Once Ritoli arrived at the venue, the armed assailants struck. While Ritoli managed to flee the scene, his aides died on the spot. The role of the fourth deceased is unconfirmed, with cops suspecting he was âcollateral damageâ.Footage from the hotel shows the assailants arriving at the hotel in a Swift car with a driver. The gunmen were seen entering the eatery brandishing arms, with one of the shooters having concealed his face with a black cloth. With the prime target surviving the latest attempt on his life, agencies remain on high alert for potential retaliatory strikes.

World.title: Gavai cites two examples to buttress caste bias claim
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Slamming the

collegiumâs recent recommendation for transfer of Tripura HC Chief Justice MS Ramachandra Rao as the chief justice of Karnataka HC, former CJI B R Gavai Friday asked whether the judge, who was transferred multiple times on punitive considerations, was being rewarded with a bigger and more prominent high court just because he belonged to an upper caste.

Without naming Justice Rao, the ex-CJI in his letter to President Droupadi Murmu said the recommendation âraises several unanswered questions as to how a judge transferred multiple times on punitive considerations is now being recommended to be chief justice of a much bigger and prominent high courtâ.

On Nov 26, TOI had reported that Justice Rao, son of former Supreme Court judge Justice M Jagannadha Rao, was appointed as judge of Andhra Pradesh HC in 2012 and had opted for Telangana HC in 2019 after the stateâs bifurcation.



He was transferred to the Punjab and Haryana HC and then made the chief justice of the Himachal Pradesh HC. Later, he was shifted to the Jharkhand and Tripura high courts.

âA chief justice who was transferred from one high court to another smaller HC and thereafter from that HC to one of the smallest HCs of the country has now been rewarded for being from a particular community, by transfer to a prominent high court,â the ex-CJI said.





Sources in the top court said serving Supreme Court judges from Karnataka, one of whom is in the collegium and is slated to become the first woman CJI next year, were prominent backers of the proposal to transfer Justice Rao as CJ of Karnataka.

The Centre is yet to act on the recommendations, which include transfer of Karnataka HC CJ Vibhu Bakhru to Jharkhand HC and appointment of Justice Vivek Singh Thakur of Himachal HC as the chief justice of Tripura HC.

Again, without naming Justice Bakhru, former CJI Gavai said the transfer of the âmeritorious and hardworking CJ of Karnatakaâ to a smaller high court to make way for Justice Rao not only demoralises meritorious judges like Justice Bakhru but âalso has a chilling effect on all hard-working judges, including persons belonging to marginalised sections of societyâ.

Justice Gavai said he was highlighting the issue (relating to Justice Rao) as he was part of the collegium when the judge was transferred from one HC to a smaller HC (Jharkhand) and was heading the collegium when he was transferred to the smallest high court (Tripura).

World.title: Centre proposes freeze on Lok Sabha seat proportions for States until 2051
World.content:
A new Constitutional Amendment Bill approved by the Union Cabinet on Friday (November 27, 2026) proposes an extension of the existing freeze on the inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats for another 25 years, until 2051, addressing the core concern of States that feared a loss of their proportionate strength due to the decline in their share of the national population.

Also read | Lok Sabha seat freeze is no longer linked to population stabilisation

The 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill marks a significant turn from the 131st Amendment Bill moved by the Centre in April 2026 that sought to redistribute Lok Sabha seats among States according to the 2011 Census population.

The proposed amendment removes the linkage of the existing distribution of Lok Sabha seats to the 1971 Census and links it with provisions related to women’s reservation in Article 334A of the Constitution. The guarantee for a 50% increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats for each State is being written into this, providing that, for the purposes of giving immediate effect to such reservation for women, “the delimitation so undertaken shall provide for an increase of fifty per cent in the number of seats allocated to each State and Union territory in the House of the People.” The total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of each State and Union territory will also increase similarly, “over and above the number of seats existing immediately before such delimitation”.

The new Bill, accompanied by a fresh Delimitation Bill, proposes to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats in each State by 50%, while the maximum strength of the lower House will rise from the current 550 to 850. If these Bills are passed by Parliament in its special sittings from November 30 to December 3, the path to immediate delimitation will open, which will also bring into force the 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha.

Amendments to Articles 81 and 82, which mandate the size and distribution of Lok Sabha seats among the States, propose to extend a sunset clause for the existing proportion until 2051.

The existing provision in Article 82 that says that “until the relevant figures for the first census taken after the year 2026 have been published, it shall not be necessary to readjust” the distribution of seats is being amended in the Bill and will be changed to read “until the year 2051”.

Article 82 currently has two definitions for population: for the purposes of distribution among States, the 1971 population; and for the purposes of delimitation of individual constituencies within the States, the 2001 Census. The proposed amendment will extend the sunset clause to “until the year 2051”, but the reference to the 1971 Census has been dropped.

The Bill proposes that the distribution among States will be determined “in accordance with Article 334A”, while the boundaries of individual constituencies will be determined by the “latest published census figures available on the date of the commencement of the Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-second Amendment) Act, 2026”.

World.title: Makkah alliance countries review regional security situation, condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
World.content:
The top officials of the trilateral Makkah Defence Alliance on Friday (November 27, 2026) met in Pakistan's capital and reviewed the evolving regional security situation while condemning "persistent and heinous" attacks by Yemen's Iranian-backed Houthi militia on Saudi Arabia.

Comment | A new security triangle emerges with the Makkah Pact

The Makkah defence agreement, signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in August, establishes a framework for collective deterrence and stipulates that an armed attack against any one of them would be regarded as an attack against all.

The meeting of the third session of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) — the highest decision-making body of the alliance — was held in Islamabad, which was decorated with the flags of Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.

Addressing the media after the meeting, which lasted for more than two hours, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said that the three countries reiterated their commitment to the pact, including collective defence, mutual solidarity and respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, Dawn reported.

“The committee reviewed the evolving regional security situation and reaffirmed the determination of the three countries to continue working collectively towards peace, security, and stability,” he said.

He said the committee also reviewed progress towards implementing the decisions taken at the previous meeting of the Makkah Alliance for Defence.

The two previous meetings of the committee — which comprises the foreign and defence ministers and top military officials of the three countries — were held in Istanbul and Riyadh.

Mr. Dar said the three countries agreed to continue consultations to enhance cooperation and coordination among them in areas of mutual interest, and to support efforts towards de-escalation of regional tensions and encourage peaceful dispute resolution.

The three countries condemned the “persistent and heinous” attacks by Yemen’s Houthis on civilians and civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, reaffirming their “collective resolve” to continue efforts in safeguarding Saudi Arabia’s security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity in accordance with the “collective defence provisions” in the pact, Mr. Dar said.

He said that the three countries also pledged to strengthen cooperation in defence industries, joint technological development, training and capacity building “with a view to enhancing the collective capabilities and cohesion of their armed forces in order to address mutual security concerns and contribute to peace and security in the region.”

Earlier, a senior official in the Shehbaz Sharif government told PTI that the Foreign and Defence Ministers as well as senior military leaders from the three countries attended the meeting.

"The agenda focused on the practical implementation of the agreement, including standard operating procedures, coordination mechanisms among political, defence and military institutions, intelligence sharing and air defence cooperation, alongside the Houthi conflict and attacks targeting Saudi Arabia," the official said.

He said a joint statement was expected to be issued later.

The federal government announced a public holiday in Islamabad on Friday (November 27) and imposed special movement restrictions in view of the high-level gathering. A local holiday was also declared in Rawalpindi.

On Thursday (November 26), Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said that the Foreign and Defence Ministers of Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan would attend the meeting.

Terming the meeting as "very important,” Mr. Asif said the “continuous turmoil south of Saudi Arabia will obviously be on the agenda."

"Any threat to Saudi Arabia is a threat to Pakistan and Turkiye according to the pact, which is absolutely clear,” Mr. Asif was quoted as saying by Dawn.

A day earlier, Mr. Dar spoke with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi over the phone and exchanged views on the wider regional situation and efforts to promote peace and security in the region.

Saudi Arabia has faced repeated attacks by Yemen's AnsarAllah movement, commonly known as the Houthis, targeting cities, oil installations and shipping routes amid an escalation in the conflict since July.

On Tuesday (November 24), Houthis targeted a tower in the financial district of Saudi Arabia's capital, damaging the building and injuring 11 people, including two Indians and three Nepalese nationals. On Thursday, Saudi Arabia hit western and southwestern Yemen.

During an emergency meeting of the SPDC in Riyadh on October 5, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agreed to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the kingdom.

Earlier this month, the Pakistan Army's spokesman, Lt. Gen. Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, said that his country is ready to take “all necessary defensive measures” to protect Saudi Arabia amid regional tensions.

In an interview with a Saudi newspaper, the spokesman stressed that Islamabad's commitment to the Kingdom's security, sovereignty and territorial integrity "is absolute and non-negotiable”.

He said that Pakistani troops were already stationed in the Kingdom, where they performed various duties, primarily providing defensive support and participating in exercises and military manoeuvres. He, however, did not disclose specific details.

World.title: Hamas says Israel tried to kill chief’s son in Gaza
World.content:
Hamas said Israel tried to kill an adult son of the Palestinian movement's chief, Khalil al-Hayya, in an overnight strike on Friday (November 27, 2026), with a Gaza security source telling AFP he survived.

Editorial | Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities

The strike follows a series of killings by the Israeli military in recent days that have targeted Hamas officials, despite a ceasefire in the war-shattered Palestinian territory.

Separately, Gaza's civil defence agency said Israeli forces killed seven people across the territory on Friday (November 27).

"Izz al-Din al-Hayya, the youngest surviving son of Hamas political bureau chief Khalil al-Hayya, along with his family and the family of his late brother Azzam, survived an Israeli assassination attempt early on Friday targeting a residential apartment in the Rimal neighbourhood, west of Gaza City," a security source in Gaza told AFP.

When asked by AFP, the Israeli military said it was looking into the incident.

Bassem Naim, a member of the Palestinian Islamist movement's political bureau, told AFP that "Israel's attempt to target the youngest son of Hamas political bureau chief Khalil al-Hayya... constitutes 'state terrorism,'" while Hamas issued a statement calling the targeting "cowardly".

Four of Mr. al-Hayya's sons have already been killed in Israeli attacks, including one in May and another in an Israeli strike targeting Hamas leaders in Doha in September 2025.

Two others were killed before the war on Gaza.

Israeli strikes continue

Gaza's civil defence agency, a rescue force which operates under Hamas authority, said an Israeli drone strike west of Rafah city in southern Gaza killed three people on Friday (November 27), with nearby Nasser Hospital confirming it received three bodies following the strike.

The Israeli military told AFP it had struck "three terrorists in the area".

Another drone strike west of Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza killed one person, the civil defence and Al-Shifa Hospital said.

The Israeli military said it was checking the incident.

The civil defence agency said two more people were killed in an Israeli drone strike near Gaza City's Al-Shifa Hospital, with the medical facility confirming it received two bodies.

The Israeli military told AFP it struck "a terrorist in the area," adding that there was "no harm to the hospital or any medical practice" in the vicinity.

Israeli gunfire in the Rafah area killed another person, the civil defence said. The Israeli military said it was checking that incident.

Israel and Hamas regularly accuse each other of violating the ceasefire that came into effect in October 2025, after two years of devastating war.

More than 1,650 Palestinians have been killed since the start of the truce, according to an AFP tally based on data from the Gaza health ministry, which also operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

In the same period, the Israeli military says seven of its soldiers have been killed, as well as one civilian contractor.

World.title: Uttar Pradesh Khadi Mahotsav begins in Lucknow
World.content:
Uttar Pradesh Minister for Khadi and Village Industries, Silk Industry and MSME Rakesh Sachan in Lucknow on Friday (November 27, 2026) said Khadi is not merely a fabric, but a powerful idea of self-respect, Swadeshi and self-reliance. Mr. Sachan made the remark while inaugurating the 10-day state-level ‘Uttar Pradesh Khadi Mahotsav-2026’ on Friday at the Central Sanskrit University campus in Lucknow’s Gomti Nagar. Organized by the Uttar Pradesh Khadi and Village Industries Board, the festival will run from 27 November to 06 December 2026. “The Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi, had made Khadi the most important medium in the struggle for the country’s independence and self-reliance. The Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s calls for ‘Vocal for Local’ and ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’ have given Khadi a new identity and fresh momentum since 2014, “ said the Minister.

Minister Rakesh Sachan said that under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the State government is committed to creating employment in rural areas and making young people ‘not job seekers, but job creators’. He said that over the past 05 years, loans worth ₹2,544.35 crore have been disbursed under the ‘Chief Minister’s Village Industries Employment Scheme’ and the ‘Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme’. With this financial assistance, 24,799 village industries units have been established across the state, providing direct employment to more than 2,79,000 people. In addition, through 27,508 stalls at 115 exhibitions organized in all 18 divisions of the state, entrepreneurs have recorded sales of more than ₹161.54 crore, reflecting the growing public confidence in Khadi and Village Industries products.

Mr. Sachan said that by adopting Khadi garments for weddings and other auspicious occasions, citizens are enriching traditional culture. “New Khadi sales centers are being opened in various cities for the convenience of customers. In addition, a special discount of 30% is being offered on the purchase of Khadi fabrics and garments from Gandhi Jayanti [02 October], so that more and more people can connect with Swadeshi products. Based on the theme ‘Culture in Threads, Progress through Khadi’, a total of 150 stalls have been set up at the festival by Khadi and Village Industries entrepreneurs and artisans from various districts of the State,” said the Minister.

Mr. Sachan also visited all the stalls and encouraged the artisans. He said that today’s Khadi, with the assurance of 100 percent pure cotton, is increasingly becoming the first choice of young people in the form of modern and designer garments. Principal Secretary, Khadi and Village Industries Department, Anil Kumar Sagar, and Chief Executive Officer of the U.P. Khadi and Village Industries Board, Shishir, were present at the inaugural ceremony.

World.title: Delhi police busts cybercrime network supplying mule accounts; five arrested
World.content:
The Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit of the Delhi Police has busted an organised cybercrime network supplying mule bank accounts to fraudsters operating from abroad and arrested five persons from different parts of the country. The investigation also uncovered suspicious transactions worth approximately ₹2 crore in one of the identified accounts, with the entire amount put on hold following coordinated intervention by the police and HDFC Bank.

The accused allegedly worked as facilitators for an international cybercrime syndicate operating from Cambodia, procuring bank accounts and supplying them to cybercriminals to receive and route money siphoned off through online fraud. The operation also helped the police solve two cybercrime cases registered in Andhra Pradesh.

The probe

According to the police, the investigation began after information was received during the probe into an FIR registered at the Special Cell police station regarding a gang supplying bank accounts for cybercrime activities.

The suspects were staying at a hotel in Dwarka and operating a bank account in the name of M/s MR Traders, maintained with HDFC Bank, to route proceeds of cyber fraud. Acting on the information, a police team raided the premises and apprehended the suspects. A fresh FIR was subsequently registered at the Special Cell police station.

The investigation revealed that the accused allegedly procured and supplied mule bank accounts to cybercriminals, enabling them to receive and transfer cheated money through multiple accounts to conceal the money trail.

Digital evidence

A forensic examination of the seized mobile phones revealed a suspicious application named ‘SMS TOOLS’, which was allegedly configured to automatically forward incoming SMS messages, including one-time passwords (OTPs), to cybercriminals operating from abroad. This arrangement could allow handlers to remotely access and operate bank accounts using OTPs received on the linked mobile phones, the police said.

Investigators also found that the accused used Telegram to coordinate their activities. Seven Telegram channels suspected to have been used for buying and selling mule bank accounts have been identified, pointing to a wider network involved in supplying accounts to cybercriminals.

The five arrested accused have been identified as Anish Khan, 31, Intekhab, 27, Altaf Hussain, 45, Md. Mahfuzar Rahman, 41, and Izhar Alam, 34.

Examination of their mobile phones led to the recovery of Telegram chats, WhatsApp conversations, cryptocurrency transaction details and other digital evidence allegedly linking them to the network. The police also seized six mobile phones and a cheque book belonging to the bank account of M/s MR Traders.

The identified mule bank account was linked to two cybercrime cases registered in Andhra Pradesh. Suspicious transactions amounting to approximately ₹2 crore were detected in the account, and the entire amount was put on hold with the help of HDFC Bank officials.

Further investigation is under way to identify other members of the network, trace the complete money trail, identify additional mule accounts and establish the roles of the international syndicate and its handlers.

World.title: Holy Family Hospital opens 150-bed super speciality block in Delhi
World.content:
Holy Family Hospital in south Delhi on Friday inaugurated a 150-bed super speciality block, expanding its capacity to provide advanced cancer care, organ transplantation and specialised neurological and cardiac services.

Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the facility at the hospital premises on Okhla Road. The new block will introduce services in surgical, radiation and medical oncology, haematology-oncology and bone marrow transplantation, nuclear medicine, advanced cardiothoracic and vascular surgery, neurology and neurosurgery, and organ transplantation.
